“Under Captin Day’s guidance we find that in India an ancient quarter-tone system has become in modern times a half tone one, substantially our Equal temperament, but permitting an expressive or ornamental use of smaller intervals than the half-tone according to the players.”
“Captin Day colluvatik kavaṉittāl intiyāvil paḻamiyāy vaḻaṅki vanta kāl curamuṟiyāṉatu, taṟkālattil ari curamuṟiyāy māṟiyirukkiṟatu. ati anēkamāy Equal temperament muṟiyeṉṟē collalām. āṉāl anta aricura muṟiyāṉatu vācippavarkaḷuṭiya maṉōtarmattiṟkicintapaṭi kamakamāyk kuṟittum kūṭṭiyum nuṭpamāṉa curaṅkaḷāyc colluvataṟku iṭaṅ koṭukkiṟatu.”
intiyāvil paḻamiyāy vaḻaṅki vanta kāl cura muṟiyāṉatu taṟkālattil ariccura muṟiyāy māṟiyirukkiṟatu eṉṟum anta aric cura muṟiyāṉatu pala nuṭpamāṉa curaṅkaḷik kamakamāyk kuṟittum kūṭṭi yum colvataṟku aṉukūlamāyirukkiṟa teṉṟum ati Equal temperament muṟi eṉṟē collalāmeṉṟum Capt. Day collukiṟār eṉṟu collukiṟār. ivvacaṉaṅkaḷi nām kavaṉikkiyil ivar teṉṉintiya caṅkītattiṉ irakaciyatti mikat teḷivāka aṟintirukkiṟār eṉṟu pūraṇamāyt terikiṟatu.
pūrvam āyappāliyil vaḻaṅki vanta curaṅkaḷ paṉṉiraṇṭē. appaṉṉiraṇṭum ca-pa vāy allatu iṇi, iṇiyāy, ēḻāvatu, ēḻāvatu irāciyil paṉṉiru curaṅkaḷum poruntukiṉṟaṉa. itupōl aintāvatu aintāvatu irāciyil kiḷi kiḷiyāy ca-ma vākap paṉṉiraṇṭu curaṅkaḷum kiṭikkiṉṟaṉa. iti Equal temperament eṉṟu evvitattilum āṣcēpaṉi yiṉṟi nām collalāmē.
nātam cama iṭiveḷikaḷuḷḷatāy illāmal Mr. Deval, colluvatupōla 84, 27, 71, 22, 90, 22 ceṉṭsukaḷāyiruntāl eppaṭip paṉṉiru curaṅkaḷum kiṭikkum? pūrvatamiḻ makkaḷ vaḻaṅki vanta ivvuttama māṉa muṟi pallāyira varuṭaṅkaḷāka maṟintu pōka pitākōras colliya 2/3, 3/4 eṉṟa muṭivu peṟāk kaṇakkum oru stāyiyil 22 curutikaḷeṉṟa iṭaṟukallum pala vittuvāṉkaḷuṭiya maṉatik kalaṅka vittaṉa.
pūrva tamiḻ makkaḷ āyappāliyāṉa paṉṉiru aric curaṅkaḷilēyē kirakam māṟṟi irākaṅkaḷ pala uṇṭākkik kāṉam ceytu vantārkaḷ. vaṭṭappāliyil 24 alaku allatu kāl cura muṟiyākavum tirikōṇap pāliyil arikkāl curamuṟiyākavum caturappāliyil vīcam curamuṟi yākavum pirittup paṉṉiru aric curaṅkaḷil oṉṟōṭu cērttuk kama kamāy vācittu vantārkaḷeṉṟu colliyirukkiṟōm. pūrva teṉṉintiya kāṉattil vaḻaṅki varum ariccura muṟiyiyum kālcura muṟiyiyum ivvaḷavāvatu kavaṉittārēyeṉṟu nām mikavum cantōṣappaṭak kūṭiyatāyirukkiṟatu.

teṉṉintiyāvil vaḻaṅki varum kāṉattil kāl curaṅkaḷip pārkkilum arikkāl vīcam curaṅkaḷ atikamāy vaḻaṅki varukiṉṟaṉa veṉṟu kaṇṭiruppārāṉāl mikunta cantōṣamaṭin tiruppār. atōṭu ippōtu vaḻaṅkum nuṭpamāṉa curutikaḷip paṟṟiyum colliyiruppār. oru stāyiyil 22 curutikaḷ varavēṇṭumeṉṟa kūkkuralukkuḷ ivar oru stāyiyil 24 curutikaḷ varukiṉṟaṉaveṉṟu coṉṉatu mikavum koṇṭāṭappaṭak kūṭiyatē.
itōṭu mēṟṟici cāstirikaḷil piyāṉā curuti cērkkum muṟiyi mikat teḷivāy eḻutiya Hermann Smith eṉpavaruṭiya cila kuṟippukaḷiyum iṅkē pārppatu mika nallateṉṟu tōṉṟukiṟatu. ivar curuti cērkkum muṟiyippaṟṟi oru puttakam eḻutiyirukkiṟār. atu taṟkālattil yāvarālum mika upayōkamāṉateṉṟu koṇṭāṭappaṭukiṟatu. nāḷatu variyum aṉuṣṭāṉattiliruntu varukiṟatu.
The art of tuning the Pianoforte by Hermann smith P.75, 76.
“Mr. W.H.B. Woolhouse remarks truly, “It is very misleading to suppose that the necessity of temperament applies only to instruments which have fixed tones. Singers and performers on perfect instruments must all temper their intervals, or they could not keep in tune with each other, or even with themselves; and on arriving at the same notes by different routes would be continually finding a want of agreement. The scale of Equal temperament obviates all such inconveniences, and continues to be universally accepted with unqualified satisfaction by the most eminent vocalists; and equally so by the most renowned and accomplished performers on stringed instruments, although these instruments are capable of an infinite variety of intonation. The high development of modern instrumental Music would not have been possible, and could not have been acquired, without the manifold advantages of the tempered intonation by equal semitones, and it has, in consequence, long become the established basis of tuning.”
Mr. Woolhouse  eṉpavar eṉṉa collukiṟār eṉṟāl, curaṅkaḷ stāpakamāyirukkappaṭṭa vāttiyaṅkaḷukkuttāṉ curaṅkaḷic caripākamāyp pirikkummuṟi avaciyam, maṟṟavikaḷukku avaciyamalla eṉṟu niṉippatu picaku. pūraṇavāttiyaṅkaḷi vittup pāṭupavarkaḷum, vācippavarkaḷum kūṭa taṅkaḷ curaṅkaḷ curutikkēṟka amittuk koḷḷāviṭṭāl, maṟṟavarka ḷōṭu cērntu pāṭavāvatu tāṅkaḷē cutta curattil pāṭavāvatu kūṭātu. pala vaḻikaḷiṉ mūlamāy orē curaṅkaḷil vantu cēra vēṇṭiya avaciyam iruppatāl aṭikkaṭi vācippōrukkum pāṭuvōrukkum curavittiyācaṅkaḷ ēṟpaṭṭuk koṇṭēyirukkak kūṭiyatu. curutikaḷi camapākamākap pirittu stāpikkappaṭṭa ārōkaṇamāṉatu ivvita vittiyācaṅkaḷi uṇṭākka māṭṭātu. atuvē caṅkītam pāṭukiṟa vitvāṉkaḷ muṟi, vāttiyaṅkaḷ palavum palavitamāy curutiyēṟakkūṭiya viyāyirunta pōtilum tanti vāttiyaṅkaḷil nipuṇarāṉa ellā caṅkīta vitvāṉkaḷum cariyeṉṟu oppuk koḷḷum vaḻiyum ituvē. ippaṭi curaṅkaḷuk kiṭiyiluḷḷa iṭi veḷikaḷi camapākaṅkaḷākap pirikkum muṟi ēṟpaṭṭa piṟakutāṉ caṅkīta vāttiyakāṉamāṉatu atikat tērcciyaṭintirukkiṟatu mallāmal atuvē ellā vāttiyaṅkaḷiyum curutikkēṟkak koṇṭuvarum muṟiyeṉṟum atiṉāl uṇṭākum pirayōcaṉaṅkaḷ aṉantam eṉṟum yāvarālum oppuk koḷḷappaṭukiṟatu.
curaṅkaḷi cama ōciyuḷḷatākap pirikkum muṟi aṉu curaṅkaḷ cērttup pāṭuvataṟku utaviyāyiruppatu pōlavē taṉittup pāṭum oruvaṉukku mikunta pirayōcaṉamāyirukkiṟatu. pala vāttiyaṅkaḷ oṉṟu cērttup pāṭuvataṟkum tantivāttiyaṅkaḷil vācippataṟkum itu mikavum ēṟṟatāyirukkiṟatu. ituvē ellāt tērccikkum mūlakāraṇa māyirukkiṟateṉṟu collukiṟār. ivar collum Equal temperament muṟiyāṉatu camīpa kālattil kaṇṭupiṭikkappaṭṭateṉṟu 69-m pakkattil colliyirukkiṟōm.

“The two cardinal points of the system are :
1. All octaves shall be tuned perfect.
2. All the fifths shall be a litle flatter than perfect.’

“These trials, as they are called, afford at each step a check by which the correctness of the progress may be indicated, or, untortunately, probably the incorrectness of your first estimates of “how much” and “how little.”
The last is the severest test, as the two notes of which this fifth is formed have been obtined by different series of fifths, and any imperfection in the gradation of the beatings allotted to the previous fifths will minfest itself here. Hence this fifth, from the frequent harshness and howlings of its beats, has been technically termed the wolf, and strict injunctions are, “Look out for the wolf” Reekon yourself fortunate if no wolf appears.”

“But the scale used on the Vina since the 16th century, at least by one school viz., the Karnatic, has been temperament, except for any accidental defects in tuning. What circumstances led to the adoption of this scale will have to be discussd on a future occasion. But it may be remarked here that this temperate scale is a capital discovery and the Hindus deserve to be congratulated on it, unless indeed it was borrowed like many other things in music from the Persians and Arabs. If any Indian perceives the Vina music to be defective, now that he has been made aware that its scale is one of equal temperament, let him taboo the instrument altogether or introduce modifications which will allow of the use of what he thinks to be a better scale.”

2. pūrva intiyarkaḷiṉ nākarīkamum avarkaḷ aracāṭciyum.
Ancient Indians in Mesopotamia.
History repeats itself in the strangest manner. This is not the first time that Indians (now forming the Expeditionary Force) are playing an important part in altering the history of the fertile valley drined by the waters of the Tigris and Euphrates. Archeological researches have tended towards the establishment of the most remarkable fact that colonists from ancient India in remote ages settled in Mesopotamia.
What leading part they played in that cradle of civilisation will be realised when itis stated that an eminent archeologist of great experience, after patient studies, is inclined to come to the starting conclusion that the wonderful Mesopotamian culture displayed by the ancient Babylonians and Assyrians was derived from the Sumerians. These were no other than Dravidian settlers from India, who had migrated to the head of the Persian Gulf at the very dawn of civilisation.
Mr. H.R. Hall, of the British Museum, thus expresses the latest views on the origin of the Sumerians, who were the pioneers of the high degree of civilisation to which the ancient nations of the Euphrates valley attined :-
The Sumerian culture springs into our view ready-made, as it were, which is what we should expect if it was, as seems on other grounds probable, brought into Mesopotamia from abroad. The earliest scenes of their culture development had, perhaps, not been played upon the Babylonian stage at all, but in a different country away across the Persian mountins to the eastward.
The ethnic type of the Sumerians, so strongly marked in their statues and reliefs, was a s different from those of the races which surrounded them as was their language from those of the Semites. Aryans or others, they were decidedly Indian in type. The face-type of the average Indian of to-day is, no doubt, much the same as that of his race ancestors thousands of years ago. And it is by no means improbable that the Sumerians were an Indian race which passed, certinlyby land, perhaps, also by sea through Persia to the valley of the Two Rivers. It was in the Indian home (perhaps the Indus Valley) that we suppose for them that their culture developed.
There their writing may have been invented, and progressed from purely pictorial to a simplified and abbreviated form which afterwards in Babylonia took on its peculiar “cuneiform” appearance owing to its being written with a square ended stylus on soft clay. There is little doubt that India must have been one of the earliest centres of human civilisation, and it seems natural to suppose that the strange un-Semitic un-Aryan people, who came from the East to civilise the West, were of Indian origin, especially when we see with our eyes how very Indian the Sumerians were in type.
The origin of the Dravidian race, the most primitive of the Indian types, is lost in obscurity. No satisfactory theory has yet been forthcoming to point out their original home (if they had any other than India) from which they migrated. Huxley’s theory as to their connection with the aborigines of Australia, although apparently supported by Sclater’s hypothesis of a vast continent now submerged under the Indian Ocean, which once embraced Africa, India and Australia, has been traversed by Sir William Turner’s comparative studies of the Australian and Dravidian crania.
Sir W.W. Hunter’s assumption,  which assigned a trans-Himalayan origin to the Dravidians, has been discounted for various reasons. The failure of all theorists to assign a foreign home to the Dravidians appears to justify the conclusion that they were among the original inhabitants of India.
There is every reason to suppose that pre-Aryan Dravidian culture flourished in their great home, well-endowed as it was by bountiful Nature. Whether the Dravidians from India who migrated to Mesopotamia were compelled to seek a new home forced by famine or by persecution, or whether they were traders or adventurers, we have no means of ascertining. We are also in the dark as to whether they took the difficult land route across Baluchistan and Persia or they went by sea along the coast.
The presence of the Brahuis in Baluchistan, who have a dialect showing strong affinity with the Dravidian languages, appears to lend much support to the former theory, specially when we take into consideration the fact that their ancestral neighbours who inhabited ancient Persia, most probably belonged to the Dravidian race.
These ancient non-Aryan inhabitants of Persia were called “Anarikoi” by the Greeks which is undoubtedly a corrupted form of “Anarya.” by which name the Dravidians were known to the first Aryan settlers in India.
Several years ago, Mr. Hewitt pointed out that the Euphrates valley was the home of the Hindu lunar astronomy, which was introduced into India before 4700 B.C. He also produced evidence pointing to the existence of trade relations between India and Mesopotamia in very ancient times.
The discovery of indigo and muslin in Egyptian tombs conclusively showed that Indian products found their way into Egypt so long ago as at least 1700 B.C. There is also evidence that the Sumerians traded in teak and muslin, which were exclusive products of India. Mr. Hewitt was of opinion that these commercial transactions between Western India and Sumer took place in 6000 B.C. He also endeavoured to trace the presence of Sumerians in ancient Gujarat, Later researches have not only confirmed some of the conclusions of Mr. Hewitt, but, as we find from the above quotation from a leading authority on archeology and ancient history, the identification of the Sumerians with the ancient Dravidians of India leaves little room for doubt.
The linguistic evidence as supplied by the Brahuis of the survival of a Dravidian language in the remote central highlands of Baluchistan forms a strong link for establishing the identity of the Sumerians. If the opinion of Dr. Grierson to the effect that of all Dravidians the Brahuis alone retin the true ethnic type owing to their isolation, be accepted, then we are led to the conclusion that the Sumerians were imigrants from Southern India as is evidenced from their strong resemblance to the Dravidian ethnic type as modified by admixture with aboriginal nationalities.
If the Brahuis really represent the true Dravidian ethnic type, an althernative theory may be proposed pointing to Baluchistan as the original home from which a great Dravidian emigration to India took place in very ancient times.
The recent geological investigations of Mr. Vredenburg appears to favour such a hypothesis, as there is now good reason to surmise, on the basis of Mr. Vredenburg’s explorations, that the desert tracts of Baluchistan were once covered by fertile lands which were well populated. The exhustion of the water resources and consequent production of famine conditions threatened the ancient inhabitants, rendering migration on a vast scale imperative.
That the Sumerians who settled in Southern Babylonia (Sumer) were the founders of Babylonian culture is abundantly shown by the relics recovered by archeologists from the excavation conducted on the sites of the ancient cities. The early history of Babylonia is a record of Sumerian domination and progress.
The excavations of the city mounds at the lowest levels disclose Sumerian culture so advanced that the people were already using copper. The Sumerian copper implements found at Tello in Babylonia, probably go so far back as 4000, B.C. A bronze statuette of Gudea, perhaps the greatest of all the Sumerian Kings, dating back to 2500 B.C., is a landmark in the history of the antiquity of copper.
More than one eminent archeologist has advanced the opinion that India was the first home of the bronze industry. Even such a conservative historian as Mr. Vincent Smith admits that copper was used in India in very ancient times. Some of the prehistoric copper implements (probably dating back to about 2000. B.C.) of the most remarkable board discovered in 1870 at Gungeria, in the Central Provinces, bear a close resemblance to those found in Babylonia.
Although very valuable work has been done in Southern India by Mr. Rhea by his discoveries of prehistoric metal implements, a great deal has yet to be done in this direction in the way of discovery and serious study to throw light on the ancient history of metallurgy in India and its possible connection with Mesopotamian Culture.
The Sumerians were great builders of towns and irrigation works. They were the first town-planners known to history. They developed the City State to a marked extent. Each city had its temple with a city god, who was the owner of all the city land. Every city was governed by a hereditary ruler, who was also the high priest of the local god with the title of “patesi” or vicegerent of the god. We do not known much about the Sumerian deities.
Nippur, which was the chief city of ancient Babylonia, had a great temple dedicated to Ennil. The identity of this name with the Dravidian name for the Moon god is significant. The corresponding Dravidian name, Bal is most prominent in Babylonian mythology.
The temple at Nippur was a great repository for votive offerings of the Sumerian Kings which have yielded valuable material for ancient history, showing that the Sumerians who lived 6,000 years before us lived in great an populous cities under organised civil and religious government.
They had long ago emerged from the savage state, as they were already using metal and had their own system of writing. From their statues we see them with shaven heads and wearing long garments. Their physiognomy and fashions of dress bear such close resemblance to the Dravidian that their common origin is not improbable, as such striking similarity cannot be merely accidental.
Dr. Buhler traced the derivation of the ancient Brahui script, the parent of most of the known alphabets of India from Mesopotamia, fixing the date of its introduction into India at about 800 B.C.
It is acknowledged by some authorities that the Tamil alphabet, with its peculiar characters of a primitive type, was  in existence long before the introduction of Brahui or Kharosthi. The supposition that the Tamil alphabet was derived from a Semitic source and is a variety of the Aramic or Hymiaritic script which originated in Mesopotamia ought to undergo modification in the light of recent researches which appear to reverse the country of origin of the Tamil alphabet.
When another Champollion is found to unearth the deeply buried relics of the ancient Dravidian culture, in all probability it will be discovered that lunar astronomy as well as the very first alphabet originated in India just as it is now being recognised that the advanced civilisation of ancient Mesopotamia owed its inception to the Sumerians from India. How far the world is thus indebted to the ancient Dravidians, as appears to be disclosed by recent researches is a subject which finds no place in the works of the modern historians of ancient India.

“cumēriyaruṭiya nākarīkamāṉatu ellā viṣayattilum pūraṇamaṭinta nākarīkam pōl tiṭīreṉa nammuṭiya kaṇkaḷukkut tōṉṟukiṟatu. āṉāl veḷitēcattiliruntu atu mecōppottāmiyāvukkuk koṇṭuvarappaṭṭatu eṉṟu maṟṟak kāraṇaṅkaḷāl nām aṟivatāl appaṭittāṉ iruntirukka vēṇṭum................... avarkaḷuṭiya nākarīkattiṉ āti virttiyāṉatu pāpilōṉ rājjiyattil alla, pārcīka malikaḷukkuk kiḻakkēyuḷḷa vēṟoru tēcattil uṇṭāyiruntirukkalām...............
cumēriya jātiyāruṭiya jāti lakṣaṇamāṉatu avarkaḷic cuṟṟik kuṭiyirunta maṟṟa jātiyāruṭiya lakṣaṇattukku vittiyācamāyiruntatāka avarkaḷuṭiya cilikaḷ mutaliyavaṟṟāl teriyavarukiṟatu pōla avarkaḷuṭiya pāṣiyum cemiṟṟiyar āriyar mutaliyavarkaḷuṭiya pāṣikaḷukku vittiyācamuḷḷatāyiruntatu. avarkaḷ uruvam, pāṣi mutaliyavi intiyaruṭiyati ottiruntatu.
taṟkālattiluḷḷa oru cātāraṇa intiyaṉuṭiya muka uruvamāṉatu anēkamāyira varuṭattiṟku muṉṉirunta avaṉ muṟpitākkaḷuṭiya uruvam pōlavē irukkiṟatu eṉpataṟkuc cantēkamilli. inta cumēriyar eṉṉum jātiyār tarivaḻiyāka allatu kaṭalmārkkamāka intiyāviliruntu pārcīkattiṉ vaḻiyāy inta iraṇṭu natippiratēcattukkuc ceṉṟa oru intiya jātiyār eṉṟu cantēkamillāmal collalām. avarkaḷuṭiya nākarīkam virttiyāṉa iṭam intiyāvē, atāvatu cintunatip piratēcamā yirukka vēṇṭum.
avarkaḷuṭiya eḻuttukaḷ iṅkē mutal mutal paṭarūpamāy ārampikkappaṭṭu piṟaku viruttiyaṭintu curuṅkiṉa ciṟu eḻuttukkaḷāki yirukka vēṇṭum. piṟpāṭu atu pāpilōṉ tēcattukkuk koṇṭu pōkappaṭṭu aṅkē kaḷimaṇṇil muṉiyil catura vaṭivuḷḷa eḻuttāṇi yāl eḻutappaṭṭapaṭiyāl kūriya muṉiyiṉ rūpatti (Cuneiform) p peṟṟirukka vēṇṭum. intiyāvāṉatu ātiyil maṉita nākarīkam uṟpatti yāṉa tēcaṅkaḷil oṉṟu eṉpataṟkuc cantēkamēyilli. mēlum cumēriya jātiyār intiyari ottiruntārkaḷ eṉpati nām kavaṉikkumpōtu, kiḻakkiliruntu mēl tēcattiṟku nākarīkattik koṇṭu vanta cemiṟṟik allāta, āriyarallāta jātiyār intiyarāyirukka vēṇṭum eṉṟu colluvatu iyaṟkiyē.”
intiyāviluḷḷa jātiyāril ellāvaṟṟiṟkum pūrva kuṭikaḷāyirunta tirāviṭa jātiyāruṭiya āti uṟpatti iṉṉateṉṟu colluvatu kūṭiya kāriyamalla. intiyāvilō maṟṟenta tēcattilō enta āstāṉatti liruntu avarkaḷ vantu kuṭiyēṟiṉārkaḷ eṉṟu oruvarum niccayamāyc colla muṭiyavilli. avarkaḷ āstirēliyāviṉ pūrva kuṭikaḷic cērntavarkaḷāyirukka vēṇṭum eṉṟu Huxley eṉpavar coṉṉatāṉatu Sclater eṉpavar colvatāl stiramāy stāpikkappaṭṭatu. atāvatu Sclater eṉpavar oru kālattil āpirikkā, intiyā, āstirēliyā eṉṟa perum pūpākaṅkaḷi aṭakkik koṇṭirunta oru kaṇṭamāṉatu. intu camuttirattil amiḻntippōṉatu eṉkiṟār.
āṉāl ivarkaḷ iruvarum colluvataṟku etirāka Sir William Turner eṉpavar āstirēliyar intiyar ivarkaḷuṭiya maṇṭiyōṭukaḷip paricōtittatil avikaḷ iraṇṭukkum evvita oṟṟumiyumilli eṉṟu kaṇṭupiṭittapaṭiyāl muntic coṉṉa iruvaruṭiya apippirāyattiyum kaṇṭittu viṭṭār.
Sir. W.W. Hunter eṉpavar tirāviṭar imayamalikku vaṭakkiliruntu vantirukka vēṇṭum eṉṟu coṉṉa apippirāyamum tappu eṉṟu anēka kāraṇaṅkaḷāl terikiṟatu. ākiyāl tirāviṭar veḷi nāṭṭiliruntu intiyāvil vantu kuṭiyēṟiṉārkaḷ eṉṟu rūpippataṟkuk kāraṇaṅkaḷ illātatāl avarkaḷ intiyāviṉ pūrva kuṭikaḷāyiruntārkaḷ eṉṟu colvatē uṇmiyāṉa apippirāyam.
nāṭāṉatu iyaṟkiyilē ceḻippāṉa tēcamāyiruntapaṭiyāl āriyarukku muṉṉāṉa kālattilēyē uḷḷa tirāviṭa nākarīkamāṉatu intiyāvil virttiyaṭintiruntatu eṉṟu eṇṇak kāraṇamuṇṭu. āṉāl intiyāviliruntu mecōppottāmiyāvil pōyk kuṭiyēṟiṉa tirāviṭarkaḷ yātu kāraṇam paṟṟit taṅkaḷ tēcatti viṭṭu vēṟiṭam pōka nēriṭṭatu eṉṟu kaṇṭupiṭikka muṭiyavilli.
oru vēḷi pañcattiṉ koṭumiyiṉālō allatu tuṉpam poṟukkamāṭṭāmalō allatu viyāpāra viṣayamākavō allatu pala tēcam pārkka vēṇṭumeṉṟa āvaliṉālō avarkaḷ iṭam peyarn tirukkalām. mēlum enta vaḻiyāy aṅkē pōṉārkaḷ eṉṟu colvatum kaṣṭamāyirukkiṟatu. avarkaḷ paluccistāṉam pārcīkam mutaliya tēcaṅkaḷiṉ vaḻiyāyk kaṭumiyāṉa pirayāṇam ceytirukkalām allāmal camuttirakkari mārkkamāyk kappalkaḷil pōyirukkalām.
tirāviṭa pāṣikkotta oru pāṣiyi paluccistāṉattil vacikkum pirakūyis (Brahuis)  eṉṉum jātiyār pēcuvatāl tirāviṭar paluccistāṉattiṉ vaḻiyāy vaṭakkē ceṉṟār eṉṟu eṇṇa iṭamirukkiṟatu. avarkaḷukku aṭutta tēcamākiya pārcīkattiṉ ātik kuṭikaḷ tirāviṭa jātiyic cērntavarkaḷ eṉṟu eṇṇa iṭamiruppatālum nām muṉ coṉṉa viṣayam atika niccayamāka stāpikkappaṭukiṟatu.
pārcīkattiṉ āriyarallāta inta pūrva kuṭikaḷ kirēkkarāl “aṉārik kāy” eṉṟu aḻikkappaṭṭārkaḷ. “aṉāriyā” eṉṟa vārttiyē “aṉārik kāy” eṉṟu maruviviṭṭatu. mutal mutal intiyāvil vantu kuṭiyēṟiṉa āriyarkaḷ tirāviṭari ‘aṉāriyā’ eṉṟē aḻittārkaḷ.
anēka varuṣaṅkaḷukku muṉ Hewitt eṉṟa cāstiri intiya vāṉacāstiram piṟantu virttiyāṉa iṭam aipirāt natippira tēcantāṉ eṉṟu coṉṉār. inta cāstiram intiyāvil ki.mu.4700 varuṣaṅkaḷukku muṉ koṇṭuvarappaṭṭatu. mēlum avar pūrvakālattil intiyāviṟkum mecōppottāmiyāvukkum viyāpāra campantam iruntatu eṉpataṟku anēka ātāraṅkaḷi eṭuttuc coṉṉār.
avuri nīlamum masliṉ kavuṇiyum ekiptiyaruṭiya kallaṟikaḷil kāṇappaṭṭatāṉatu kuṟintatu ki.mu.1700 varuṣaṅkaḷukku muṉṉēyē intiya carakkukaḷ ekiptukkuk koṇṭu pōkappaṭṭaṉa eṉpatic cantēkamaṟa rūpikkiṉṟatu.mēlum cumēriyar tēkkumaram masliṉ tuṇi mutaliya carakkukaḷik koṇṭu varttakam ceytārkaḷ eṉpataṟku rucu irukkiṟatu. intac carakkukaḷ intiyāvukkē uriyavi.
Hewitt  eṉpavaruṭiya apippirāyam eṉṉaveṉṟāl mēl intiyāvukkum cumar eṉṉum tēcattiṟkum ki.mu.6000 varuṣaṅkaḷukku muṉṉēyē varttaka campantam iruntatu. āti kujarāttil cumēriyar kuṭiyiruntārkaḷeṉṟum avar rūpakārappaṭuttiyirukkiṟār. pintiṉa cila ārāyccikaḷāl Hewitt  cāstiriyār colvatu uṇmi yeṉṟu veḷippaṭuvatu mallāmal cumēriyarē intiyāviṉ pūrva tirāviṭa jātiyar eṉṟu nām munti eṭuttuc coṉṉa pūrva carittira ārāycciyil mutaṉmiyāṉavarum ati nipuṇarumāṉa Hall eṉpavariṉ apippirāyattāl pariṣkāramāy stāpikkappaṭukiṟatu.
intiyāviṟku tūrattiluḷḷa paluccistāṉattiṉ malip piratēcaṅ kaḷil uḷḷa pirakūyis (Brahuis) eṉṉum jātiyār tirāviṭa pāṣiyip pēciṉārkaḷ eṉṟa caṅkatiyāṉatu cumēriya jātiyār yār eṉṟu kaṇṭu piṭippataṟku oru periya rucuvāyirukkiṟatu. ellā tirāviṭa jātiyārilum pirakūyis jātiyār māttiram maṟṟa tēcattārōṭu kalavātatāl āti jāti laṭcaṇam māṟāmal irukkiṟārkaḷ eṉṟu Dr. Grierson eṉpavar colvati nām oppuk koḷḷum viṣayattil cumēriyar kūṭiyavariyil (maṟṟa āti jātikaḷōṭu kalanta pōtilum) tirāviṭa jāti lakṣaṇatti yuṭiyavar kaḷāṉatāl avarkaḷ teṉ intiyāviliruntu vantu kuṭiyēṟiṉavarkaḷ eṉṟu colvatu uṇmiyāyirukka vēṇṭum.
pirakūyis eṉṉum jātiyār āti tirāviṭaruṭiya jāti lakṣaṇam poruntiyavarkaḷāyiruntatu uṇmiyāṉāl paluccistāṉ tēcamē āti intiyaruṭiya stalamāyirunta teṉṟum, aṅkiruntu tirāviṭar anēkar intiyāvil vantu kuṭiyēṟiṉārkaḷ eṉṟu colluvatum uṇmiyāṉa vēṟoru apippirāyamāyirukkalāmē.
Vredenburg eṉṉum cāstiriyār pūkōḷa viṣayamāy ceyta ārāycciyiṉ mūlamāy atu nicameṉṟu eṇṇavum iṭamirukkiṟatu. avar kaṇṭupiṭitta teṉṉaveṉṟāl ippōtu paluccistāṉattil vaṉāntara māyk kiṭakkiṟa pūpākam oru kālattil atika ceḻippāṉa tēcamāyum anēka jaṉaṅkaḷ kuṭiyirunta iṭamāyum iruntirukka vēṇṭum eṉpatē. taṇṇīr kuṟintapaṭiyāl pañcam uṇṭāki anēka jaṉaṅkaḷ anta tēcatti viṭṭu viṭṭu maṟṟiṭaṅkaḷil pōykkuṭiyēṟa nēriṭṭatu eṉṟu avar collukiṟār.
pāpilōṉ mutaliya ātinakaraṅkaḷ irunta iṭattil tariyil putintu kiṭantu ippōtu veṭṭiyeṭukkappaṭukiṟa anēka vastukkaḷip paricōtittāl, teṉpāpilōṉiyā allatu cumar nāṭṭil kuṭiyēṟiṉa cumēriyar tāṉ pāpilōṉiyaruṭiya nākarīkam puttikkūrmi mutuliya vaṟṟiṟku ātikāraṇarkaḷāyiruntārkaḷ eṉṟu teriya varukiṟatu. pāpilōṉ rājjiyattiṉ āticarittiratti vācittāl, attēcatti aracāṇṭavar kaḷum atu virttiyaṭivataṟkuk kāraṇamā yiruntavarkaḷum cumēriyar eṉṟu teriya varukiṟatu.
paṭṭaṇattiṉ mēṭukaḷi veṭṭip pārkkiyil aṭiyil pittaḷi cāmāṉkaḷ terivatāṉatu cumēriyar aṭintirunta nākarīkattukku aṭi yāḷamāyirukkiṟatu. pāpilōṉiluḷḷa Tello eṉṉum nakaril kāṇappaṭṭa cumēriyaruṭiya pittaḷi āyutaṅkaḷ ki.mu.4000 varuṣaṅkaḷukku muṉṉuḷḷavi yeṉat terikiṟatu. cumēriya rājākkaḷellārilum pēr pōṉavaṉāka eṇṇappaṭṭa Gudea eṉpavaṉuṭiya ki.mu.2000 varuṣaṅkaḷukku muṉṉuḷḷa veṇkalac ciliyāṉatu pittaḷiyiṉuṭiya āti carittirattik kālavariciyāyk kāṭṭum kuṟikaḷil oṉṟu.
pērpōṉa anēka pūrvacarittira ārāyccikkārar mutal mutal veṇkala vēli ceyyappaṭṭa iṭam intiyātāṉ eṉṟu apippirāyap paṭukiṟārkaḷ. carittirakkārarukkuḷ paḻamiyē cirēṣṭam eṉṟa apippirāya muḷḷavarākiya Vincent Smith eṉpavaruṅkūṭa pittaḷiyāṉatu intiyāvil veku pūrvattiliruntu upayōkikkap paṭukiṟatu eṉṟu oppuk koḷḷukiṟār.
1870-m varuṣattil mattiyamākāṇaṅkaḷic cērnta Gungeria eṉṉum iṭattil veṭṭiyeṭukkappaṭṭa āccariyappaṭattakka putiporuḷkaḷuḷ cila ātikālattil pittaḷi āyutaṅkaḷ pāpilōṉiya āyutaṅkaḷi ottiruntaṉa. (ivikaḷ ki.mu.2000 varuṣaṅkaḷukkumuṉ upayōkikkappaṭṭa āyutaṅkaḷāyirukkalām)
itu viṣayattil Rhea eṉpavarāl teṉṉintiyāvil ātikālattil āyutaṅkaḷ anēkam kaṇṭupiṭikkappaṭṭa pōtilum avar ceyta vēli atika meccik koḷḷap paṭattakkatāy irunta pōtilum intiyāvil ulōkaṅkaḷāl ātiyil ceyyappaṭṭa āyutaṅkaḷip paṟṟiyum avikaḷukkum mecōppottāmiyā viṉ nākarīkattukkum uḷḷa campantam iṉṉateṉpatip paṟṟiyum iṉik kaṇṭupiṭippatilum ati ārāycci ceyya vēṇṭiyatilum naṭatta vēṇṭiya vēli aṉantam.
cumēriyar paṭṭaṇaṅkaḷ kaṭṭuvatilum nilaṅkaḷukku nīrppāycca vēṇṭiya viṣayattil ēṟpaṭṭa vēlikaḷ ceyvatilum pēr pōṉavarkaḷ. ciṟpa cāstirattiṉpaṭi paṭṭaṇaṅkaḷ kaṭṭappaṭa vēṇṭumeṉṟu mutal mutal aṟintavarkaḷ avarkaḷē. avarkaḷ kālattil ovvoru piratāṉa nakaramum ovvoru rājyamāka amikkappaṭṭatu. ovvoru nakarattukkum oru kōvilum oru teyvamum iruntatu. nakarattic cērnta nila mellām intat teyvattukkē contam. ovvoru nakaramum vamca parampariyāy atikārikaḷāl āḷappaṭṭatu. anta nakar teyvattukku anta atikāriyē pūcāriyāka iruntu paṟṟēci (allatu teyvattiṉuṭiya stāṉattil uḷḷavaṉ) eṉṟa pēriyum peṟṟāṉ. cumēriyaruṭiya teyvaṅkaḷip paṟṟi namakku atikam teriyātu.
āti pāpilōṉiyāviṉ mukkiya nakarākiya nippūril Ennil eṉṟa teyvattukkup piratiṣṭi ceyyappaṭṭa oru ālayam iruntatu. inta eṉṉil eṉṉum pērāṉatu tirāviṭa pāṣiyil cantiraṉukkup pērākiya nilā eṉṉum vārttiyi ottiruppatu kavaṉikkappaṭattakkatu. itaṟkuc camamāṉa tirāviṭap pērākiya pāl eṉpatu pāpilōṉiya pūrva carittirattil upayōkikkap paṭṭirukkiṟatu.
nippūr nakariluḷḷa inta ālayattil cumēriya rājākkaḷ taṅkaḷ teyvattukkuc celuttum kāṇikkikaḷellām oṉṟu cērttu vikkappaṭṭiruntaṉa. avikaḷi ārāyumiṭattu pūrva carittirattukku utaviyāṉa anēka kāriyaṅkaḷi aṅkē kāṇalām. avikaḷiliruntu nām aṟikiṟateṉṉa veṉṟāl namakku 6000 varuṣaṅkaḷukku muṉṉuḷḷa antac cumēriyarkaḷ periyatum jaṉanerukka muḷḷatumāṉa nakaraṅkaḷil vacittārka ḷeṉṟum annakaraṅkaḷil civil viṣayattukkum mataviṣayattukkumāṉa rājyattukkuriya amcaṅkaḷ anēkam iruntaṉa veṉṟum terikiṟatu.
avarkaḷ ulōkaṅkaḷi upayōkittatiyum taṅkaḷukkeṉṟu uṇṭākkiṉa pāṣiyiṉ eḻuttukkaḷiyum kavaṉikkumpōtu avarkaḷ veku kālattukku muṉ nākarīkatti yaṭintiruntār kaḷeṉṟum terikiṟatu. avarkaḷ cilikaḷip pārttāl avarkaḷ tali mayiri cirit tiruntatākavum nīṇṭa aṅki pōṉṟa vastiraṅkaḷi upayōkittatākavum terikiṟatu. avarkaḷ mukarūpamum, uṭiyum - tirāviṭaruṭiya rūpattiyum uṭiyiyum ottiruppatāl avarkaḷ orē jātiyar eṉṟu cantēkamaṟac collalām. avvaḷavu tūram anēka viṣayaṅkaḷil iruvarum ottiruppatāṉatu taṟceyalāy uṇṭāṉatu eṉṟu colla muṭiyātu. intiyāviluḷḷa anēkam pāṣi eḻuttukkaḷukkut tāyākiya Brahui eḻuttāṉatu mecōp pottāmiyāviliruntu uṟpattiyāṉatāyum atu intiyāviṟku ki.mu.800-m varuṣattil koṇṭu varappaṭṭateṉṟum Dr. Buhler eṉpavar collukiṟār.
āṉāl maṟṟavarkaḷ collukiṟateṉṉaveṉṟāl tamiḻp pāṣi yiṉ eḻuttukaḷ atiṉ atipūrvamāṉa eḻuttukaḷiṉ rūpattik kavaṉikkum pōtu Brahui allatu Karosthi pāṣiyiṉ eḻuttukaḷukku muṉṉālēyē intiyāvil iruntatāka niṉikkiṟārkaḷ. tamiḻp pāṣiyiṉ eḻuttukkaḷ cemiṟṟik pāṣiyiliruntu uṟpattiyāṉa aramēyik allatu ham yāriṭṭik pāṣiyiliruntu mecōppottāmiyāvil uṇṭāyiṉa eṉṟu collum apippirāyattit taṟkāla carittira ārāycci nēril colva tōṭu ottup pārkkumpōtu atu cariyāṉatākat tōṟṟavilli. uṇmi itaṟku etirmāṟāka irukka vēṇṭum.
Champollion  eṉpavari pōlotta iṉṉoru nipuṇar ulakattil tōṉṟi āti tirāviṭaruṭiya nākarīkamum nilimiyum iṉṉateṉṟu pūrṇamāy veḷippaṭum kālattil pūrva mecōppottāmiyāruṭiya virttiyāṉa nākarīkam intiyāviliruntu aṅku vantu kuṭiyēṟiṉa cumēriyarāl uṇṭāṉatu eṉṟu yāvarum oppuk koḷvatu pōlavē vāṉa cāstiramum ātipāṣiyiṉ eḻuttukaḷ mutaliya nākarīka ciṉṉaṅkaḷum intiyāvil mutal mutal ārampamāṉateṉṟu oppuk koḷḷappaṭum.
āṉāl taṟkāla carittira ārāycciyik kavaṉikkumpōtu āti ulaka māṉatu tirāviṭa jātiyārukku ivvaḷavu tūram kaṭamippaṭṭiruntatu eṉṟa caṅkatiyi pūrva intiyāvip paṟṟip pēcum taṟkāla carittirakkārar eṭuttuc collakkūṭa māṭṭārkaḷ eṉṟu terikiṟatu.
A. kōs.
mēṟkāṭṭiya cila vacaṉaṅkaḷiṉāl mecōp pottāmiyāvil kuṭiyēṟiṉa pūrva intiyarkaḷiṉ cila mukkiya kuṟippukkaḷi iṅkē kāṇkiṟōm. mecōp pottāmiyā eṉpatu ciṉṉāciyāvil tikirīs aipirāttu natikaḷ ōṭum ceḻippāṉa piratēcattiṟkup peyarāy vaḻaṅki vantirukkiṟatu. aipirāttu nati ātiyil ulaka ciruṣṭip piṉ kālattil ētēṉ eṉṟa tōṭṭattil pāyntu koṇṭirunta nati eṉṟu collap paṭukiṟatu. innatikaḷ pāyum iṭamāṉatu mikunta ceḻippuṭiyatāy anēka paḻa varkkaṅkaḷum kāy, kaṟi, tāṉiyaṅkaḷum viḷiyak kūṭiya nāṭāyirunta teṉṟu carittiraṅkaḷ mūlamāyp pārttirukkiṟōm.
intukkaḷukkuc cumēriyar eṉṟu peyar. ivarkaḷ muka uruvattilum tēkak kaṭṭuppāṭṭilum intiyāviṉ teṉpākattilirunta tirāviṭa jāti yāri ottiruntārkaḷ. ivarkaḷ intiyāviṉ teṉpākattiliruntu aṅkē pōyk kuṭiyēṟiyirukka vēṇṭum. ivarkaḷ paḻakka vaḻakkaṅkaḷilum tērcci peṟṟirunta kalikaḷilum intiyāviṉ teṉpākattilirunta varkaḷi ottiruppatik koṇṭu teṉṉintiyāviliruntē vantirukka vēṇṭum. pāpilōṉ, acīriyā eṉṉum pūrva kālattu rājyaṅkaḷi stāpittavarkaḷākavum avaṟṟi āṇṭavarkaḷākavum, ciṟpacāstiram, vāṉacāstiram mutaliya kalikaḷilum, tuṇi neytal cāyamēṟṟutal, payiriṭutal, ulōkaṅkaḷāl cili vārttal mutaliya kittoḻilkaḷilum varttakattilum mikat tērntavarkaḷākavum iruntārkaḷ.
ki.mu.6000 varuṭaṅkaḷukku muṉṉālēyē cumēriyarukkum teṉṉinti yarukkum varttaka campantamiruntatākac collappaṭukiṟatu.ki.mu.4700 varuṭaṅkaḷukku muṉ mecōppottāmiyā nāṭṭiṟku intiyāviliruntē vāṉacāstiram koṇṭupōkappaṭṭatākak kāṇkiṟōm. pelujiḵtāṉ mali nāṭṭilum pāracīkattilum pēcappaṭum pāṣi tirāviṭa pāṣiyā yiruntatiṉāl akkuṭikaḷ pūrvam intiyāviliruntu pōyirukka vēṇṭu meṉṟu eṇṇa iṭamirukkiṟatu. avarkaḷ pēci vanta pāṣi pirakūys pāṣiyeṉṟu aḻikkappaṭṭatu. ciṉṉāciyāvukkuc camīpamāṉa it tēcaṅkaḷil tirāviṭarkaḷ kuṭiyēṟiṉārkaḷeṉṟum avarkaḷ tirāviṭa pāṣi pēciṉārkaḷeṉṟum collappaṭukiṟatu. ivarkaḷik kirēkkar ‘anāriyā’ eṉṟu aḻittārkaḷ.
cumēriyarāl ceyyappaṭṭa pittaḷi āyutaṅkaḷum veṇkala cāmāṉkaḷum pāpilōṉ nāṭṭiluḷḷa tellō eṉṉum nakaril veṭṭi yeṭukkappaṭṭaṉa. ivi ki.mu. 4000 varuṭaṅkaḷukku muṉṉuḷḷavi yeṉat terikiṟatu.
cumēriya aracarkaḷil ciṟantavaṉākiya kuṭiyā eṉpavaṉuṭiya veṇkalac ciliyāṉatu ki.mu.2000 varuṭaṅkaḷukku muṉṉuḷḷa ciliyākak kāṇappaṭukiṟatu. itaṉāl intiyarkaḷ mikap pūrvattil pittaḷi vēli ceyvatilum vārppiṭaṅkaḷ ceyvatilum tērntavarkaḷāyiruntārkaḷeṉṟu tōṉṟukiṟatu. itōṭu 1870-m varuṣam mattiya mākāṇattiluḷḷa kaṅkariyā eṉṉum iṭattil veṭṭiyeṭukkappaṭṭa pittaḷi āyutaṅkaḷ pūrvam pāpi lōṉil veṭṭiyeṭukkappaṭṭa āyutaṅkaḷi ottirukkiṉṟaṉa. ivikaḷ ki.mu.2000 varuṭaṅkaḷukku muṉ upayōkikkap paṭṭaviyeṉṟu terikiṟatu.
cumēriyar kaṭṭaṭam kaṭṭuvatilum nilaṅkaḷukku nīrppāyccuvatilum mikat tērntavarkaḷ. ciṟpa cāstirattiṉpaṭi paṭṭaṇaṅkaḷ kōṭṭikaḷ ālayaṅkaḷ kaṭṭuvatilum ālayap paṇiviṭikaḷ ceyvatilum tērntirun tārkaḷeṉṟum avaṟṟil ivarkaḷiyē mutalvarākac collalām eṉṟum kāṇappaṭukiṟatu.
pāpilōṉ rājyattiṉ mukkiya nakarākiya nippūril eṉṉil eṉṉum teyvamāṉatu iruntatākavum atu tirāviṭa pāṣiyil cantiraṉukkup peyarākiya nilā eṉṟa vārttikkuc cariyāyirukkiṟatākavum av vārttikkuc camamāṉa pāl eṉṉum tirāviṭap peyar pāpilōṉiṉ pūrva carittirattil upayōkikkap paṭṭiruppatākavum terikiṟatu. atōṭu avarkaḷ teyva paktiyil ciṟantavarkaḷākavum naṭi uṭi pāvaṉikaḷil nākarīka muṭiyavarkaḷākavu miruntārkaḷeṉṟu kāṇkiṟōm.
avarkaḷ pēci vanta pāṣiyāṉatu pirakūys eṉṟu aḻikkappaṭṭa teṉṟum avveḻuttukkaḷ pāpilōṉiṉ kaṭṭaṭaṅkaḷiluḷḷa ceṅkal kaḷil kāṇappaṭukiṉṟaṉa veṉṟum collukiṟār. avveḻuttukkaḷ tamiḻ pāṣiyiṉ eḻuttukkaḷākavē yirukkiṉṟaṉaveṉṟum avi cemiṭṭik pāṣiyiliruntu uṟpattiyāṉa aramēyik pāṣiyiliruntu uṇṭāka villiyeṉṟum collappaṭukiṟatu.
mēṟkaṇṭa kuṟippukaḷ anēka pūrva carittira ārāyccikkārariṉ apip pirāyaṅkaḷip paricōtittu eḻutappaṭṭatāka nām kāṇpōm. ivvapip pirāyaṅkaḷi aṉucaritta cila kuṟippukaḷi itaṉ muṉ mutalām pākattil kaṇṭirukkiṟōm. ikkuṟippukkaḷiṉāl piraḷayattiṟku muṉṉālēyē teṉ maturiyil aracāṭciyirunta kālattil pāṇṭiyarāja vamcattic cērnta varkaḷum maṟṟum kuṭikaḷumākiya pūrva tamiḻ makkaḷ mecōppottāmi yāvukkup pōyirukka vēṇṭumeṉṟum atiliruntu pāpilōṉ, acīriyā mutaliya rājyaṅkaḷi stāpittu aṅkē aracāṭci ceytirukka vēṇṭu meṉṟum niṉikka ētuvirukkiṟatu.
cantira vamcattic cērntavarkaḷāyiruntatiṉāl tāṅkaḷ aṅkē kaṭṭiṉa pāpilōṉ eṉṉum paṭṭaṇattilirunta eṉṉil eṉṉum teyvat tiṟkum ippeyar koṭuttiruppārkaḷeṉṟu niṉikka iṭamirukkiṟatu.
piḻippataṟku valaci vāṅkiya kuṭikaḷ periya paṭṭaṇaṅkaḷiyum kōṭṭikaḷiyum kaṭṭi mikap pirapalamāyirunta rājyaṅkaḷi stāpippatu kūṭiya kāriyamalla. avarkaḷ teṉ pāṇṭi nāṭṭil aracāṭci ceytu koṇṭu vanta rājarkaḷāyāvatu rāja vamcattārkaḷāyāvatu irukka vēṇṭum. pāpilōṉ eṉṉum paṭṭaṇam aipirāttu āṟṟiṉ irukari yilum 225 caturamil parappuṭiyatāyc cuṟṟilum 75 aṭi uyaramum 32 aṭi akalamumāṉa kōṭṭiyum peṉṉam periya 120 veṇkalak katavukaḷu muṭiyatāyk kaṭṭappaṭṭiruntateṉṟum ataṉ naṭumattiyil rāja araṇ maṉiyum kōvilum kaṭṭappaṭṭiruntaṉaveṉṟum maṟṟum āccariyappaṭat takkavikaḷum amikkap paṭṭiruntaṉaveṉṟum ipputtakattiṉ ārampattil colliyirukkiṟōm.
avikaḷil kaṇṭa kuṟippukaḷi nām pārkkumpoḻutu vāṉmīka muṉivar “navamaṇikaḷ iḻittatāyp poṉṉāṟ ceyyappaṭṭatāyk kōṭṭi matil cuvarkaḷōṭu iṇikkappaṭṭatāṉa pāṇṭiyaṉ kōṭṭi vācaṟkatavukaḷik kāṇpīrka” ḷeṉṟu vāṉara cēṉikaḷukkuc coṉṉa teṉ maturiyiṉ alaṅkārattiṟ kottavikaḷāy avikaḷ kāṇappaṭu kiṉṟaṉa.
teṉ maturiyiṉ nākarīkamum ataṉ aḻakum colliyirukkum ākāsvēru rājaṉ viruntiṉ perumikkēṟṟa vitamākavē iruntirukka vēṇṭum. intiyā mutal ettiyōppiyā variyumuḷḷa 127 nāṭukaḷi aracāṇṭu vantāṉ eṉṟu colvati nām kavaṉikkumpoḻutu ivaṉirunta cūcāṉ paṭṭaṇamum antap paṭṭaṇattic cērnta pāracīka tēcamum oru kālattil teṉmaturiyilirunta pāṇṭiyarāja vamcattōr veḷināṭukaḷukkuc ceṉṟu kaṭṭi āṇṭirunta irājyaṅkaḷāka iruttal vēṇṭumeṉat tōṉṟukiṟatu.
intiyāviṉ vaṭa elliyāyirukkum imayamali variyum teṉ pāṇṭi nāṭṭaracarkaḷ āṇṭukoṇṭu vantirukkiṟārkaḷeṉṟum avarkaḷuk kuriya mīṉakkoṭi imayamaliyil āṭik koṇṭiruntateṉṟum cācaṉaṅkaḷil kāṇkiṟōm.
pāpilōṉ rājyattiṟkum atic cērnta pala rājyaṅkaḷukkum talinakaraṅkaḷākiya ērēk, akkāt, kalṉē eṉṉum iṭaṅkaḷiyum acīriya rājyattic cērntavikaḷākiya niṉivē, rekōpōt, kālāku, rēcēṉ eṉṉum paṭṭaṇaṅkaḷiyum kaṭṭiya nimirōttip paṟṟi nām itaṉmuṉ pārttirukkiṟōm. ivikaḷ ciṉṉāciyāviṉ teṉpuṟamāy tikirīs aipirāttu eṉṉum natikaḷ pāyum mocōp pottāmiyā nāṭākavum ataṟkuc camīpattiluḷḷa iṭaṅkaḷākavu mirukkiṉṟaṉa.
mocōppottāmiyā nāṭṭil cumēriyar aracāṭci ceytu koṇṭiruntārkaḷeṉṟum ivarkaḷ teṉṉintiyāviliruntavarkaḷeṉṟum ivarkaḷ pelujistāṉ vaḻiyāy vantu pelujistāṉattilum pāracīkattilum taṅkiṉārkaḷeṉṟum ivarkaḷ pēciya pāṣi pirakūys pāṣi eṉṟu collappaṭum tamiḻāyiruntateṉṟum avveḻuttukkaḷ pūrva tamiḻ eḻuttāyiruntaṉaveṉṟum colvati nām kavaṉikkiyil pūrvam teṉpāṇṭi nāṭṭiluḷḷa tamiḻ makkaḷ oru kālattil imayamali variyilum ataṟ kappāl peljistāṉ pāracīkam, mecōppottāmiyā mutaliya iṭaṅkaḷilum palapala rājyaṅkaḷi stāpittu āṇṭu vantārka ḷeṉṟum intiyā mutal ettiyōppiyā variyumuḷḷa 127 nāṭukaḷil rājyapāram ceytārkaḷeṉṟum kāṇkiṟōm.
itaṉāl inta 127 nāṭukaḷilum mutal mutal tamiḻpāṣiyē pēcap paṭṭu vantateṉṟum ataṉpiṉ pāṣikaḷ citivuṟṟu vevvēṟu peyar kaḷuṭaṉ aḻikkappaṭṭirukka vēṇṭumeṉṟum avikaḷil miccamāṉa vārttikaḷ tamiḻ vārttikaḷāyiruppatiṉāl ivvuṇmiyik kāṇalāmeṉṟum terikiṟatu.
tamiḻp pāṣi pēci vanta ivarkaḷiṭamiruntē akkampakkattiliruntē maṟṟavar ciṟpa cāstiram, cōtiṭa cāstiram, caṅkīta cāstiram, vittiya cāstiram mutaliya kalikaḷip paṭittirukka vēṇṭum eṉṟu tōṉṟukiṟatu. vāṉa cāstirattiṉ nuṭpattiyum, caṅkīta cāstirattiṉ nuṭpattiyum nām kavaṉippōmāṉāl avikaḷ mikap pūrvamāyt teṉ maturiyil vaḻaṅkit tērcci peṟṟiruntaṉaveṉṟum pēṇuvāraṟṟamiyāl nāḷaṭivil kuṟintaṉaveṉṟum terikiṟatu.
itōṭu cattiya vētam ātiyākamam 10-m atikāram 2 mutal 5 vākkiyaṅkaḷik kavaṉikkiyil yāppēttiṉ kumārarkaḷ ēḻu peyar. yāppāttiṉ kumārar kōmar, yāvāṉiṉ kumārarkaḷ ēḻu peyarkaḷum avarkaḷ peyarāl uṇṭāṉa vevvēṟu jātikaḷum avarkaḷ tīvukaḷum pāṣikaḷum avarkaḷuṭiya tēcaṅkaḷum evvēḻāyiruppatākak kāṇap paṭukiṟatu. avi varumāṟu :
“yāppēttiṉ kumārar, kōmar, mākōku, mātāy, yāvāṉ, tūpāl, mēcēkku, tīrās eṉpavarkaḷ.
kōmāriṉ kumārar, askiṉās, rīppāttu, tokarmā eṉpavarkaḷ.
yāvāṉiṉ kumārar elīcā, tarṣīs, kittīm, totāṉīm eṉpavarkaḷ.
ivarkaḷāl jātikaḷuṭiya  tīvukaḷ  avaṉavaṉ pāṣiyiṉ paṭiyēyum avaravarkaḷ kōttirattiṉ paṭiyēyum jātiyiṉ paṭiyēyum vēṟu vēṟu tēcaṅkaḷāy pakukkappaṭṭaṉa.”
yāppēttiṉ ēḻu kumārarkaḷum ēḻu jātikaḷāṉārkaḷeṉṟum avarkaḷ ēḻu tīvukaḷiliruntārkaḷeṉṟum avarkaḷ ovvoruvarumirunta ovvoru tīvum evvēḻu tēcaṅkaḷāka vakukkappaṭṭateṉṟum niṉikka iṭamirukkiṟatu. itaṉāl lemūriyā eṉṟu aḻikkappaṭṭa teṉ maturi nāṭu ēḻu tīpaṅkaḷākavum ovvoru tīpamum evvēḻu nāṭākavumiruntati annāṭṭiliruntu jalappiraḷayattiṟkut tappip pōṉavarkaḷ oruvāṟu taṅkaḷ ñāpakattiṟkāka ippaṭip pirittirippārkaḷeṉṟu collavum iṭamirukkiṟatu. itaṉāl pūrva tamiḻ vaḻakkam pēṇappaṭṭu vantatāka nām eṇṇa vēṇṭum.
tamiḻ makkaḷ piraḷayattiṟkut tappi ōṭiya kālattil pala iṭaṅkaḷukkup pōyk kuṭi yēṟiṉārkaḷeṉṟum rājāṅka muṟiyāyp pala iṭaṅkaḷi jeyittu rājyaṅkaḷ stāpittārkaḷeṉṟum collalām.
itaṉāl intiyā mutal ettiyōppiyā tēcam variyiluḷḷa 127 nāṭukaḷ tamiḻarkaḷ aracāṭciyilirunta teṉṟum tamiḻp pāṣi pēcappaṭṭu vanta teṉṟum terikiṟatu. inta 127 nāṭukaḷum intiyāviṉ teṉ kōṭi mutal āppirikkāviṉ teṉ kōṭi variyumuḷḷa ārēpiyāk kaṭaliṉ cuṟṟōramāyirukkak kāṇpōm.
cūcāṉ paṭṭaṇattilirunta maṇṭapattiṉ aḻakum pāpilōṉ niṉivē eṉṉum paṭṭaṇaṅkaḷiṉ amippum taṟkālattil nām kāṇakkūṭiyavi yalla. ivvirājyaṅkaḷiṉ perumiyiyum ivaṟṟiṉ vaṉmiyiyum pūrvīkattiyum acal tamiḻarkaḷē stāpittu aracāṭci ceytu vantārka ḷeṉpatiyum nām kavaṉippōmāṉāl teṉṟamiḻ nāṭṭiṉ pūrvattiyum tamiḻarkaḷ paḻaki vanta iyal ici nāṭakameṉṉum muttamiḻiyum avaṟṟil caṅkīta cāstirattil avarkaḷ peṟṟirunta nuṭpamāṉa aṟivi yum evar collum tiṟamuṭiyavar?
pūrva teṉṟamiḻ nāṭē mikac ciṟappuṭiyatāyiruntateṉṟum tamiḻarkaḷ aracāṭcikkuṭpaṭṭa maṟṟum pala rājyaṅkaḷilum caṅkītam atikam vistāramā yiruntirukkiṟateṉṟum tamiḻi iyal ici nāṭakameṉṟu muttamiḻāka vaḻaṅki vantirukkiṟārkaḷeṉṟum avaṟṟil caṅkītamāṉatu uṉṉata niliyi aṭintiruntateṉṟum 1/2, 1/4, 1/8, 1/16 āṉa nuṭpamāṉa curaṅkaḷil kāṉam ceytārkaḷeṉṟum oru tamiḻaṉ colvati evar nampuvār? mecōppottāmiyā nāṭṭiluḷḷa cumēriyar pēci vanta tamiḻ pāracīka nāṭṭilum pelujistāṉ nāṭṭilum pēcappaṭṭu vantateṉṟum avarkaḷ tamiḻarkaḷāyiruntār kaḷeṉṟum pāpilōṉ acīriyā mutaliya rājyaṅkaḷukku rājarkaḷāyiruntārkaḷeṉṟum ciṟanta kittoḻilkaḷil tērntiruntārkaḷeṉṟum colvati yār oppukkoḷvār?
cumēriyarālum pāracīkarkaḷālum peljistāṉattiluḷḷavarkaḷālum pēcappaṭṭu vanta tamiḻppāṣi pirakūyis eṉṟu aḻikkappaṭṭateṉṟum atiliruntu pala tēcaṅkaḷil palavitamāy vaḻaṅkappaṭṭa pirakūyis pala māṟutalkaḷaṭintu pirākiruta pāṣi eṉṟu aḻikkappaṭṭateṉṟum pirākiruta pāṣiyiṉ tiruttamē camaskirutamāyiṟṟeṉṟu terikiṟatu.
ātiyāyirunta tamiḻppāṣi intiyāviṉ teṉpākattilum ataṉ kiḷiyākiya teluṅku, kaṉṉaṭam, maliyāḷam mutaliya pāṣikaḷ intiyā viṉ mattiya pākattilum, tamiḻ, teluṅku, kaṉṉaṭam mutaliya pāṣikaḷ kalanta pāli pāṣi vaṭa nāṭṭilum iruntateṉṟum itaṉ muṉ colliyirukkiṟōm.
mecōp pottāmiyā nāṭṭil kuṭiyēṟiṉa tamiḻ makkaḷiṉ pāṣi yākiya tamiḻ moḻi, pāracīkam, pelujistāṉ, āpkāṉistāṉ, cintu, kujarat pōṉṟa intiyāviṉ mēṟṟici nāṭukaḷil vikārappaṭṭup pirākiruta pāṣiyāka avikaḷ palavum oṉṟākac cērntu camaskirutamākac ceyyap paṭṭaṉaveṉṟu tōṉṟukiṟatu.
pirākiruta pāṣikaḷil cērntatākac collappaṭum pala pāṣikaḷil miccamāṉavi tamiḻ moḻikaḷē. pāli pāṣiyil kalantirukkum tamiḻ moḻiyiṉālum tamiḻiliruntuṇṭāṉa maliyāḷam, kaṉṉaṭam, teluṅku, tuḷuvam mutaliya pāṣikaḷil vaḻaṅkum tamiḻ vārttikaḷiṉālum pūrvam toṭṭut tamiḻ moḻi maṟṟa moḻikaḷukku ātiyākaviruntirukka vēṇṭumeṉṟu teḷivākat terikiṟatu.

The Popular Encyclopedia Vol I Page 370.
“The advanced condition of the Assyrians in various in  other respects is sufficiently evidenced by the representations on the sculptures, and by the remins discovered among their ruined buildings. We now know that they understood and applied the arch; that they constructed tunnels, aqueducts and drins; that they used the lever and the roller; that they engraved gems in a hightly artistic way; that they understood the arts of inlaying, enamelling and overlaying with metals; that they manufactured porcelin and transparent and coloured glass and were acquainted with the lens; that they possessed vases, jars, and other dishes, bronze and ivory ornaments, bells, gold earrings and bracelets of excellent design and workmanship.
Their household furniture also gives us a high idea of their skill, taste, minuteness, and accuracy.
The cities of Nineveh, Assur and Arbela had each their royal observatories superintended by astronomers royal, who had to send in their reports to the king twice a month.
At an early date the stars were numbered and named, a calendar was formed in which the year was divided into twelve months (of thirty days each) called after the Zodical signs, but as this division was found to be inaccurate an intercalary month was added every six years. The week was divided into seven days, the seventh being a day of rest; the day was divided into twelve casbu of two hours each, each casbu being subdivided into sixty minutes, and these agin into sixty seconds.
Eclipses were recorded from a very remote epoch, and their recurrence roughly determined. The principal astronomical work, called the Illumination of Bel, was compiled for the library of Sargon of Agane; it was inscribed on seventy tablets, and went through numerous editions one of the latest being in the British Museum.
It treats among other things on observations of Comets, the polar star, the conjunction of the Sun and Moon and the motions of Venus and Mars. The study of mathematics was fairly advanced, and the people who were acquainted with the sun-dial, the clepsydra, the pully, and the lever must have had considerable knowledge of Mechanics.”

Discoveries in the ruins of Nineveh and Babylon by Austen H. Layard, M.P. Page 343.
“On the north side of the chamber were two doorways leading into separate apartments. Entrance was formed by two colossal bas-reliefs of Dagon, or the fish god. Unfortunately the upper part of all these figures had been destroyed, but as the lower remined from above the waist we can have no difficulty in restoring the whole, especially as the same image is seen entire on a fine Assyrian cylinder of a gate in my possession. It combined the human shape with that of the fish. The head of the fish formed a mitre above that of the man. whilst its scaly back and fanlike til fell as a cloak behind, leaving the two human limbs and feet exposed. The figure wore a fringed tunic, and bore the two sacred emblems, the basket and the cone.
We can scarcely hesitate to identify this mythic form with the Oannes, or sacred manfish, who according to the traditions preserved by Berossus, issued from the Erythrean  sea, instructed the Chaldeans in all wisdom, in the sciences, and in the fine arts, and was afterwards whorshipped as a God in the temples of Babylonia. Its body, says the historian, was that of a fish but under the head of a fish was that of a man and to its til were joined women’s feet. Five such monsters rose from the Persian gulf at fabulous intervals of time. It was conjectured that this myth denotes the conquest of Chaldea at some remote and prehistoric period, by a comparatively civilised nation coming in ships to the mouth of the Euphrates.
I had already identified with the Babylonian idol a figure in a bas-relief at Khorsabad having the human form to the waist, and the estremities of a fish. Such figures are also frequently found on antique cylinders and gems, but those at Kouyunjik agreed even more minutely with the description of Berossus, for the human head was actually beneath that of the fish whilst the human feet were added to the spreading til.”
“anta aṟiyiṉ vaṭappakkattil taṉittaṉi aṟikaḷukkuc cellum iraṇaṭu vācaṟ katavukaḷ iruntaṉa. ovvoru vācalilum tākōṉ allatu mīṉ teyvattiṉ iraṇṭu piramāṇṭamāṉa uruvaṅkaḷ niṉṟaṉa. āṉāl avvuruvaṅkaḷiṉ mēṟ pākaṅkaḷ aḻintu pōṉatu mikavum vicaṉikkappaṭattakkatu. eṉṟālum avikaḷiṉ kīḻ pākaṅkaḷ iṭuppu variyilum keṭāmal irunta paṭiyālum atē uruvam eṉ vacattiluḷḷa ācīriyāvic cērnta ciliṇṭar vaṭivamāṉa oru vācaṟpaṭiyil muḻumiyu māyk kāṇappaṭuvatālum anta muḻu uruvamum eppaṭi yirukkum eṉṟu niccayippatu acāttiyamāṉa kāriyamalla. atu maṉita uruvamum mīṉ uruvamum kalantatu. maṉitaṉuṭiya talikku mēl mīṉiṉ uruvamāṉatu oru kirīṭam pōl iruntatu. cetilkaḷ niṟinta ataṉ mutukum viciṟi pōṉṟa vālum oru niliyaṅkipōl piṉṉāl viḻuntiruntatu. maṉitak kikaḷum kālkaḷum pātaṅkaḷum muṉṉē naṉṟāyk kāṇappaṭṭaṉa. cuṟṟilum curukkaṅkaḷuḷḷa oru mēl vastiram atiṉ mēl pōṭap paṭṭiruntatu. paricuttattukku aṭiyāḷamākiya kūṭiyum Cone um ataṉ kiyil iruntaṉa.”
Berossus  eṉpavarāl collappaṭṭa pārampariyiṉ paṭi Erythrean kaṭaliliruntu puṟappaṭṭu, kaltēyarukku cakalavita kalikaḷiyum ñāṉattiyum pōtittatum, pāpilōṉiyāviṉ kōvilkaḷil piṟaku teyvamāka vaṇaṅkappaṭṭatum inta maṉita mīṉākiya, Oannes eṉṉum peyarāl aṟiyappaṭṭa teyvamē eṉpataṟkuc cantēkamilli. antac carittirakkāraṉ collukiṟapaṭi ataṉ tēkam mīṉ uruvamāyum āṉāl mīṉiṉ taliyiṉ kīḻ maṉita uruvamāyiruntatākavum ataṉ vāluṭaṉ stirīyiṉ kālkaḷ kāṇappaṭṭatākavum aṟikiṟōm.

mēṟkaṇṭa varikaḷik kavaṉikkiyil maṉita uruvamum mīṉ uruvamum kalanta oru teyvatti kaltēyar vaṇaṅkiṉārkaḷeṉṟum ivvuruvaṅkaḷ kaltēya tēcattiṉ carittirattiṟku muṉṉuḷḷa kālattilēyē muntiṉa ūḻiyil kaltēyariviṭa nākarīkamuḷḷa jaṉaṅkaḷ aipirāttu natiyiṉ mukattuvāra mūlamāyk kappalkaḷil ēṟi vantatiṉāl intak kappalkaḷē mīṉ uruvaṅkaḷākac collappaṭukiṉṟaṉaveṉṟum kāṇkiṟōm.
immīṉ uruvaṅkaḷ niṉivē, pāpilōṉ mutaliya pūrva nakaraṅkaḷil atikamāyk kāṇappaṭukiṉṟaṉa. ivvuruvi Berossus eṉpavar  Oannes eṉṉum teyvamākac collukiṟār. iti nām kavaṉikkiyil pūrva tamiḻ makkaḷē kaltēya nāṭṭil pōyk kuṭiyēṟiṉārkaḷeṉṟum teṉpāṇṭi nāṭṭiṟku rājarkaḷāyirunta pāṇṭiya rājarkaḷē aṅkē aracāṭci ceytārka ḷeṉṟum cantēkamaṟac collalām. ēṉeṉṟāl pūrvam cattiya virataṉ eṉṉum tirāviṭa tēcattu aracaṉ cērkkiṟēṉ” eṉṟu coṉṉati nampi ōṭattil ēṟikkoḷḷa anta ōṭam avarkaḷi imaya maliyiṉ aṭivāram cērkka aṅku cērnta cattiya virataṉākiya teṉ pāṇṭi nāṭṭu rājaṉē piṉ vivacutamaṉu āṉāṉ eṉṟum avaṉ mūlamākavē intiyāvil jaṉaṅkaḷ uṟpatti yāṉārkaḷeṉṟum avaṉiliruntē cantiravamcam tōṉṟiyateṉṟum avaṉuṭiya parampariyē pāṇṭiyarkaḷuṭiya parampariyā yirukkiṟa teṉṟum itaṉ muṉ pala iṭaṅkaḷil colliyirukkiṟōm. ippāṇṭiya “On others of the same age we find the Gods represented under various forms. The King and priests worshipping before them, altars and various signs peculiar to the period, and the usual mythic emblems. On a small cylinder in which porcelin or quartz is engraved a cow of the Indian breed suckling a calf, an Assyrian emblem; which occurs amongst the ivory carvings discovered at Nimroud.”
“atē kālattiluḷḷa maṟṟa ciṉṉaṅkaḷil tēvarkaḷ palavitamāṉa rūpattiyuṭiyavarkaḷākak kāṇpikkappaṭṭirukkiṟatu. aracarkaḷum kurumār kaḷum attēvarkaḷi vaṇaṅkiṉatākavum palipīṭaṅkaḷum maṟṟum ataṟkuriya ciṉṉaṅkaḷum antak kālattiṟkēṟṟa irakasya ciṉṉaṅkaḷum irunta tākavum terikiṟatu. veḷḷip pōrcilēṉāl ceyyappaṭṭa oru ciṟiya kuḻāyil allatu ciliṇṭaril intiyā tēcattic cērnta oru pacu taṉ kaṉṟukkuṭṭikkup pāl koṭukkiṟa pāvaṉiyākak kāṇpikkappaṭṭiruk kiṟatu. itu acīriyaruṭiya matak kuṟikaḷil oṉṟu. itu nimrūt nakaril veṭṭiyeṭukkappaṭṭa tantattil ceyta vēlikaḷil kāṇap paṭukiṟatu.
mēṟkaṇṭa vākkiyaṅkaḷik kavaṉikkiyil intiyāvukkuriya jīvap pirāṇikaḷil kuraṅku, yāṉi, pacumāṭu, mayil mutaliyavi iyaṟki yāṉavi eṉṟu nām aṟivōm. pacumāṭṭi maṟṟa tēcattavarip pārkkilum intiyāviluḷḷōr mika mēṉmiyuḷḷatāka matittut taṅkaḷ jīvaṉattiṟku iṉṟiyamiyātatākavum mikap paricuttamāṉatākavum teyvamākavum koṇṭāṭiṉārkaḷeṉpatik koṇṭum mīṉ vaṭivattit teyvamākak koṇṭāṭiṉārkaḷ eṉpatik koṇṭum tamiḻaṟiyum perumāḷ, icikkāṭum perumāḷ, eṉṟu tamiḻ makkaḷ koṇṭāṭum muttamiḻukku mutalvarāṉa paramacivaṉukku riṣapam vākaṉamāyiruppatip koṇṭum teṉ tamiḻ nāṭṭiṟ civālayaṅkaḷil cannitikaḷilirukkum nantiyik koṇṭum mecōppottāmiyar pāpilōṉ acīriyā pāracīkam mutaliya nāṭukaḷil tamiḻ makkaḷē pūrvam kuṭiyēṟi yiruntārkaḷeṉṟu teḷivākak kāṇkiṟōm. mēlum mecōppottāmiyā nāṭṭil kuṭiyēṟiya cumēriyarākiya tamiḻmakkaḷ pēci vanta pāṣiyip paṟṟic cila pārkka vēṇṭiyatu avaciyameṉṟu niṉikkiṟēṉ.
pāṣikaḷip paṟṟic collumpoḻutu avaṟṟiṉ eḻuttu vaṭivaṅkaḷ, ōci, ilakkaṇa viti ākiya ivikaḷil oṉṟaṟkoṉṟiluḷḷa campantam mutaliyavikaḷik kavaṉikka vēṇṭiyatu avaciyam. nām eṭuttuk koṇṭatu curutiyip paṟṟiya kāriyamāṉatāl ivikaḷi atikamāyc collāmal viṭa vēṇṭiyirukkiṟatu. āṉāl caṅkītattil vaḻaṅki varum nuṭpa curaṅkaḷ veku pūrvamāka muttamiḻil oṉṟākiya icit tamiḻil collappaṭuvatiṉāl tamiḻp pāṣi pūrva pāṣiyā yirukka vēṇṭumeṉṟu aṟivataṟkuc cila kuṟippukaḷip pārkka vēṇṭum. avaṟṟi aṭiyil varum vacaṉaṅkaḷiṟ kāṇpōm.
The popular Encylopedia Vol XI Page 34.
“Lastly come the Inflectional Languages represented by the two groups of the Semetic and Indo-Germanic languages. It is from the speakers of languages of these two groups that almost everything most beneficial to the development of the human race has sprung. The Semetic languages are (a) Hebrew closely akin to which were the other ancient dialects of Canaan, Moabite, Phoenician etc. (b) Arabic, widely spread as the result of Mohamadan Conquests; (c) Aramic, the languages of Ancient Syria which in Palestine also had taken the place of Hebrew as a spoken language before the Christian era; and (d) Assyrian, which has been recovered from countless inscriptions upon clay tablets found on the sites of ancient cities like Nineveh and Babylon. The different Semetic languages do not differ more from one another than do Romance languages like French, Italian and Spanish. They are, however, generally divided into a northern and a Southern group; the Souhern group being formed of the various dialects of Arabic, the northern groups of the other languages though Aramic deviates considerably from the rest of the group. The most characteristic feature of the Simitic languages is that with rare exceptions all roots have three Consonants or semi Consonants, which in combination with vowels, form series of words. The verb system is much less perfectly developed than that of the Indo-Germanic system.
To the Indo-Germanic or Indo-European system belong a number of languages and dialects which fall easily into eight groups. These languages are widely spread, extending from India to Iceland in the Old world, and since the end of the fifteenth century having been disseminated over the whole of America, Australia, New Zealand, and the East India as the language of European conquerors or colonizers of those lands. The sysem has been called by other names as Aryan, which is however, more appropriately applied to the most easterly group of the languages. The name Indo-European is commonly used, but seems to imply that the languages are spoken only in India and Europe, which is inaccurate, as is also the notion that all Indian and European languages belong to this system. In Southern Indian the Dravidian languages, of which the chief representatives are Tamil and Telugu are aggultinative languages and therefore of a different type, while in Europe, Turkish, Hungarian, Finnish, Lapp belong to an aggultinative system, and Basque, as we have seen, is an incorporating language. The names Indo-Germanic and Celt-Indic are each an attempt to express the family by the exterme links of the chin. The languages belonging tothe system are descended from an original language long since lost. Where this language was spoken it is difficult definitely to decide.”
kaṭiciyāka cemiṟṟik intu jermaṉik pāṣiḷāl kuṟikkappaṭṭa pala vita māṟutalkaḷuḷḷa (Inflexional) pāṣikaḷ varukiṉṟaṉa. māṉiṭa jāti nākarīka mutaliyavaṟṟil tērcciyaṭivataṟku evi avaciyamō avi inta iraṇṭu jāti pāṣikaḷiyum pēcuvōrālēyē uṇṭāṉavi. cemiṟṟik jātiyic cērnta pāṣiḷ eviyeṉṟāl, (ya) epirēyupāṣi. ātiyil kāṉāṉiyar, mōvāpiyar, peṉikkēyar mutaliyavarkaḷ pēciṉa pāṣikaḷ itaṟku neruṅkiya campanta muṭiyavi. (b) arapippāṣi. itu makamatiyaruṭiya veṟṟikaḷāl anēka tēcaṅkaḷil paraviṉatu (c) aramēyik pāṣikaḷ. ātiyil cīriyā nāṭṭil pēcappaṭṭa pāṣikaḷ ivikaḷē. inta pāṣi kiṟistuvukku muṉ palastīṉā nāṭṭil epirēyu pāṣikkup patilāy pēcappaṭum oru pāṣiyāy iruntatu. (d) acīriyapāṣi. niṉivē, pāpilōṉ, mutaliya āti nakaraṅkaḷil veṭṭi yeṭukkappaṭṭa kaḷimaṇ palakikaḷil kāṇappaṭṭa anēka eḻuttukkaḷāl tāṉ intap pāṣi aḻintu pōkāmal taṟkākkappaṭṭatu. rōmaṉs pāṣiḷākiya pirañci, ittāliya pāṣi, spāṉiya pāṣi eppaṭi oṉṟaṟkoṉṟu atika vittiyāca millāmal irukkiṉṟaṉavō appaṭiyē cemiṟṟik pāṣiyic cērnta paṟpala pāṣikaḷum oṉṟaṟkoṉṟu atika vittiyācamillāmal irukkiṉṟaṉa. āṉāl avikaḷ vaṭakku, teṟku eṉṟa iru kūṭṭaṅkaḷāka cātāraṇamāyp pirikkappaṭukiṉṟaṉa. arapip pāṣiyic cērnta kiḷi pāṣikaḷ teṉ kūṭṭattiyum, maṟṟa pāṣikaḷ vaṭa kūṭṭattiyum cērntavi. āṉāl aramēyik pāṣikkum antak kūṭṭattic cērnta itara pāṣikaḷukkum aṉanta vittiyācaṅkaḷ uṇṭu. cemiṟṟik pāṣikaḷiṉ mukkiyamāṉa aṟikuṟi yeṉṉa veṉṟāl, anēkamāy vārttikaḷiṉ aṭippakutikaḷellām mūṉṟu uyir mey yeḻuttukaḷ allatu Semi consonants uḷḷavikaḷāyirukkum. ivikaḷum uyireḻuttu kaḷum oṉṟu cērumpoḻutu tokutiyāṉa anēka vārttikaḷ avi kaḷiṉiṉṟu piṟakkum. āṉāl atiṉ viṉiccol muṟi intu jermāṉik pāṣikaḷiṉ muṟiyip pōla avvaḷavu pūraṇattiṟku vantatalla.
intu jermāṉik allatu intu airōppiyaṉ kūṭṭattic cērnta pāṣikaḷik kavaṉittāl avikaḷiṉ uṭpirivukaḷāka anēkam perum pāṣikaḷum pēcappaṭum pāṣikaḷum irukkiṉṟaṉa. ivikaḷi mukkiyamāṉa eṭṭuk kūṭṭaṅkaḷāyp pirikkalām. intap pāṣikaḷ veku vistāramāy ulakattil anēka iṭaṅkaḷil pēcappaṭukiṉṟaṉa. paḻiya ulakattil avikaḷ intiyā tēca mutal aislāntu, tēcam varikkum paḻakkattil irukkiṉṟaṉa. putiya ulakattil 15-m nūṟṟāṇṭiṟkup piṟaku amerikkā, āstirēliyā, nīyūcilāntu, kīḻintiyat tīvukaḷ mutaliya tēcaṅkaḷil avikaḷi jeyittavarḷuṭiya pāṣikaḷākavum allatu avikaḷil kuṭiyēṟiṉarvaḷuṭiya pāṣikaḷākavum iruntu varukiṉṟaṉa. intap pāṣikaḷukku āriyapāṣikaḷ eṉṟa maṟu peyarum uṇṭu. āṉāl kīḻakkaṭiciyil pēcappaṭum pāṣikaḷukkuttāṉ intap peyar takum. intu airōppiyaṉ eṉum peyar cātāraṇa vaḻakkattilirunta pōtilum, peyarik koṇṭu atu intiyā airōppā kaṇṭaṅkaḷil pēcappaṭum pāṣi yeṉṟu colvatu tappāṉa apippirāyam. intiyāvilum airōppāvilum vaḻaṅki varum pāṣikaḷ intak kūṭṭattic cērntavi yeṉṟu colvatum tappu. teṉṉintiyāvil tamiḻ teluṅku pāṣikaḷāl kuṟikkappaṭṭa tirāviṭa pāṣikaḷāṉavi vārttikaḷic caṅkilipōl toṭukkum (agglutinative) iṉattic cērntatāl vittiyācamāṉavi. āṉāl airōppāvilō turukki, haṅkēriya, piṉṉiṣ (Finnish)) lāplāntu tēca pāṣikaḷ vārttikaḷic caṅkilipōl toṭukkum jātiyic cērntavi. nām munti kavaṉittapaṭi pāskpāṣi maṟṟa pāṣi vārttiḷit taṉṉuṭaṉ kalakkum (incorporating language) jātiyic cērntatu. intu jermāṉik, kelṭ intik eṉṉum peyarkaḷ, oru caṅkiliyiṉ antattiyum ātiyiyum māttiram eṭuttuk koṇṭu appeyarḷi caṅkili muḻuvatukkum vittatu pōl irukkiṉṟaṉa. ikkūṭṭattic cērnta pāṣikaḷ cantēkamaṉṉiyil orukālam iruntu ippōtu aḻintu pōṉa oru āti pāṣiyiṉiṉṟu uṟpattiyāyirukka vēṇṭum. āṉāl appērppaṭṭa ātipāṣiyāṉatu evviṭattil pēcappapaṭṭateṉṟu tīrmāṉippatu ilēcāṉa kāriyamalla.
pāṣikaḷip paṟṟit teḷivāṉa apippirāyamum kālamum colvatu ilēcāṉa kāriyamalla. nammuṭiya kālattil allatu namakkuc camīpa kālattil uṇṭāṉa tiruttam aṭinta pāṣiyip paṟṟiyum nūtaṉamāy eḻuttukaḷ uṇṭākkappaṭṭa pāṣiyip paṟṟiyum māttiram nām collak kūṭiyatēyoḻiya mikappūrvamāṉa pāṣiḷip paṟṟit teḷivāka oṉṟum collakkūṭāta iyalpuṭiyatāyirukkiṟatu. tamiḻiṉ vārtti kaḷiyum tamiḻiṉ eḻuttukkaḷiyum mikavum ottirukkum tamiḻ nāṭṭiṟkuc camīpattiluḷḷa tiruvāṅkūr nāṭṭil pēcappaṭum maliyāḷa pāṣiyum teluṅku pāṣiyum veku camīpa kālattil camaskiruta pāṣiyiṉ pala eḻuttukkaḷiyum vārttikaḷiyum cērttuk koṇṭu oru periya māṟutali aṭintirukkiṉṟaṉa. curāṣṭira pāṣi (paṭṭu nūṟkārar pāṣi) veku camīpattil eḻutuvataṟkuriya eḻuttu kaṇṭu piṭikkappaṭṭu eḻutum pāṣiyāyiṟṟu eṉpati nām aṟivōm. oṉṟip pārttu oṉṟu tērcciyaṭivatu ulaka iyalputāṉē. pirakūyis pāṣi yilum cumēriya pāṣiyilum pala pirākiruta pāṣikaḷilum pāli pāṣi yilum intu jermāṉik pāṣikaḷilumuḷḷa pala vārttikaḷiyum pala ilakkaṇaṅkaḷiyum nūtaṉamāṉa cila vitiḷiyumuṭiyatāyc cila āyira varuṭaṅkaḷukku muṉṉāka camaskirutam uṇṭāṉateṉṟu itaṉ muṉ pārttirukkiṟōm. camaskiruta pāṣiyiliruntu cila eḻuttukḷiyum vārttikaḷiyum iraval vāṅkik koṇṭa pāṣikaḷ iṉṉum āyira varuṭaṅkaḷukkup piṉ camaskirutattiṉiṉṟē uṇṭāyiṉa eṉṟu colla iṭamākumē.
paricuttamāka vāṉattiliruntu viḻum maḻi jalam vāykkālilum, vāykkāliluḷḷatu kuḷattilum, kuḷattiluḷḷa jalam vayalilum, maṟupaṭi avi āṟṟilum, āṟṟi nīr kaṭalilum pāyntu vevvēṟu ruciyiyum maṇattiyum niṟattiyum aṭivatu eppaṭiyō apṭiyē pāṣiyiṉ vārttikaḷum vevvēṟu uccarippum eḻuttukkaḷumuṭiyavikaḷāy māṟutalkaḷaṭivataṟku utāraṇaṅkaḷ itaṉmuṉ colliyirukkiṟōm. ataṟkiṇaṅka ātiyil pala iṭaṅkaḷukkuppōyk kuṭiyēṟiṉa jaṉaṅkaḷ pūrvīkamāyp pēci vanta pāṣi antanta tēcattiṉ cītōṣṇattiṟkut takuntapaṭi upayōkikkum vastiram poruḷkaḷ, viḷiyum kāy, kaṉi, kīri mutaliya patārttaṅkaḷukkum niracavastukkaḷukkum paḻakka vaḻakkaṅkaḷukkum takuntavitamāy eḻuttukkaḷum vārttikaḷum vaṭivamum kālakkiramattil māṟupaṭṭu vēṟu pāṣiyāyt tōṉṟukiṟatu. ippaṭik koñcam koñca māka māṟutalkaḷiyuṭiya pala pāṣikaḷ akaṇṭamāyirunta pūmi pala aracarkaḷāl vevvēṟāka āḷappaṭumpoḻutu vevvēṟu tēcamākavum vevvēṟu pāṣiyākavum vevvēṟu tiruttaṅkaḷuṭiyatākavum ceyyap paṭumpoḻutu muṟṟilum tāyp pāṣikku ovvātatākak kāṇappaṭu kiṉṟaṉa.
pala carakkukkaṭiyil cintum navatāṉiyaṅkaḷum pala poruḷkaḷum oṉṟāyk kalanta piṉ piritteṭuppatu kaṣṭamākiṟatu eppaṭiyō, taṅkam veḷḷi vēli ceyyum taṭṭāṉ kuppiyiṟ kalanta taṅkattip pirit teṭuppataṟku taṅkam, veḷḷi, cempu, īyam mutaliya ulōkaṅḷi taṉṉōṭu cērttuk koḷḷum pātaracattiṉāl mutal mutal piritteṭuttu ataṉ piṉ taṅkattiyum veḷḷiyiyum māttiram pirikkakkūṭiya cuṇṇāmpuk kukiyil vittu ūti ataṉpiṉ veḷḷiyip pirittu viṭakkūṭiya puṭattiṉāl cutta taṅkatti eṭuppatu evvaḷavu pirayāciyō atu pōla ituvumirukkiṟatu. pūmiyil putintu kiṭakkum pūrva ciṉṉaṅkaḷiyum pāṣikaḷip paṟṟiya kuṟippukaḷiyum ārāyntu eṭukkum carittira ārāyccikkārarukkup pāṣiyiṉ kalappu mutaliyavi kaḷip paṟṟic colluvatu piriyamāyirukkumēyoḻiya maṟṟavarukku itu piriyamāyirātu.
“āti tirāviṭaruṭiya nākarīkamum avarkaḷ nilimiyum iṉṉa teṉṟu pūrṇamāy veḷippaṭum kālattil mecōppottāmi yaruṭiya viruttiyāṉa nākarīkam tirāviṭa tēcattiliruntu aṅku kuṭiyēṟiṉa cumēri yāvil uṇṭāṉa teṉṟu yāvarum oppuk koḷvatu pōlavē vāṉa cāstiramum āti pāṣiyiṉ eḻuttukkaḷ mutaliya nākarīka ciṉṉaṅkaḷum intiyāvil mutal mutal ārampamāṉateṉṟu oppuk koḷḷappaṭum. āṉāl taṟkāla carittira ārāycciyik kavaṉikkum poḻutu āti ulaka māṉatu tirāviṭa jātiyārukku ivvaḷavu tūram kaṭamippaṭṭiruntatu eṉṟa caṅkatiyip pūrva intiyāvip paṟṟip pēcum taṟkāla carittirakkārar eṭuttuc collakkūṭa māṭṭārkaḷ” eṉṟu 184m pakkattil Mr. A. Ghose eṉpavar eḻutiya kuṟippukaḷi nām pārkkum poḻutu avi uṇmi yākavē tōṉṟukiṉṟaṉa. ātaliṉāl ivviṣayattip paṟṟic cila vārttikaḷ collat tuṇintēṉ.
intiyāviṉ teṉpuṟattilinta vicālamāṉa nāṭu tamiḻ nāṭāyirunta teṉṟum pāṇṭiya rājarkaḷāl āḷappaṭṭateṉṟum, iyal ici nāṭaka meṉṉum muttamiḻum aṅkē viruttiyaṭinta teṉṟum avaṟṟil icit tamiḻil vīcam curam varikkum nuṭpamāṉa curaṅkaḷil kāṉam ceytārka ḷeṉṟum itaṉmuṉ pārttirukkiṟōm. atupōlavē iyaṟṟamiḻil iyaṟki amippil kāṇappaṭum ceyalkaḷiyum jīvap pirāṇikaḷiṉ ōciyiyu muṭiyatāyp pala aruṅkalikaḷilum tērnta tāyiruntatu tamiḻ moḻiyeṉṟu pala tiṣṭāntaṅkaḷiṉāl colliyirukkiṟōm.
iṅkē intu jermāṉik eṉṟa pāṣiyum cemiṟṟik pāṣiyumāka iraṇṭu pirivukaḷil pāṣikaḷ uṇṭāyirukkalāmeṉṟu collukiṟār. cemiṟṟik pāṣi eṉpatu ēpirēyupāṣi, arapi pāṣi, aramēyik pāṣi, acīriya pāṣi eṉṟu vakukkappaṭṭirukkiṟatu. intu jermāṉik pāṣi eṉpatu paḻiya ulakattil intiyā tēcam mutal iṅkilāntiṟku vaṭakkēyuḷḷa aislāntu tīvu vari paḻakkattilirunta pala pāṣikaḷākavum avaṟṟiṉ uṭpirivukaḷākavum terikiṟatu.
atu patiṉintām nūṟṟāṇṭiṟkup piṟaku amērikkā, āstirēliyā, niyucilāntu, kīḻ intiya tīvukaḷ mutaliya tēcaṅkaḷil pēcappaṭum pāṣi kaḷākavumirukkiṟatu. intu airōppiya pāṣi eṉṟu collumpoḻutu intiyā airōppā kaṇṭaṅkaḷil pēcappaṭum pāṣi eṉṟu nām niṉikkak kūṭāteṉṟum intu pāṣiyeṉṟu collumpoḻutu tamiḻ, teluṅku eṉṟu māttiram niṉikkappaṭāteṉṟum collukiṟār. āṉāl intiyā mutal aislāntu uḷpaṭa ettaṉi tēcaṅkaḷ aṭaṅki irukkiṉṟaṉavō atupōlavē intu pāṣi ātiyāka jermaṉ pāṣi yīṟākavuḷḷa pala pāṣikaḷum itil aṭaṅkum. oru caṅkiliyiṉ iru kaṭiciyiluḷḷa vaḷiyaṅkaḷik kuṟippiṭṭatupōl iṅkēyum kuṟippiṭṭirukkiṟatāka nām niṉikka vēṇṭum. intu, jermāṉik, kelṭ intik mutaliyavikaḷip pōl collappaṭukiṟatu eṉṟu nām aṟiya vēṇṭum. ikkūṭṭattiluḷḷa pāṣikaḷ pala aḻintu pōyiṉaveṉṟum pala pāṣikaḷiṉ kalappiṉāl ātipāṣi iṉṉateṉṟum atilintu maṟṟa pāṣikaḷ uṟpattiyāṉa vitam iṉṉateṉṟum evviṭattil pēcappaṭṭateṉṟum tīrmāṉippatu lēcāṉa kāriyamallaveṉṟum collukiṟār.
iti nām kavaṉikkiyil cemiṟṟik pāṣiyiliruntu uṇṭāṉa epirēyu pāṣiyil cātāraṇa tamiḻ moḻikaḷ atikam kalantiruppatik koṇṭum epirēyu pāṣiyiṉ vārtti tamiḻil kalavātiruppatik koṇṭu epirēyu pāṣikkum tamiḻ moḻi muntiṉateṉṟu terikiṟatu. epirēyu pāṣikkut tāyaṉa cemiṟṟik pāṣiyilum tamiḻmoḻi kalantirukka vēṇṭum. cemiṟṟik pāṣikkum tamiḻ moḻi muntiṉatā yirukka vēṇṭum. aramēyik pāṣi epirēyupāṣikkup piṟaku kiṟistu vukku muṉ palastīṉā nāṭṭil pēcappaṭṭateṉṟu collukiṟatiṉāl tamiḻ kalanta epirēyupāṣiyum atil kalantirukka vēṇṭum.
acīriyapāṣi niṉivē pāpilōṉ mutaliya nakaraṅkaḷil vaḻaṅki vanta teṉṟum appāṣiyil eḻutappaṭṭa maṇ ōṭukaḷ putinta nakaraṅkaḷil kāṇappaṭukiṉṟaṉaveṉṟum appāṣiyiṉ pala eḻuttukkaḷiṉ ōci tamiḻp pāṣiyiṉ eḻuttukkaḷiṉ ōciyākavēyirukkiṟa teṉṟum cumēriyar ippaṭṭaṇaṅkaḷik kaṭṭiṉārkaḷ eṉṟum, aracāṭci ceytārka ḷeṉṟum cumēriyar tirāviṭarkaḷā yiruntārkaḷeṉṟum, intiyāviṉ teṉpākattiliruntu aṅkuk kuṭiyēṟiṉārkaḷeṉṟum, kaltēyarukku muṉṉāl pūrvam oru palatta jātiyār aṅkē yiruntu aracāṭci ceytārkaḷeṉṟum, avarkaḷ kappal mūlamākap pāracīkakkuṭāviṉ vaḻiyāy vantārkaḷ eṉṟum, avarkaḷ mīṉ uruvamāṉa teyvatti vaṇaṅki vantārkaḷeṉṟum, vili uyarnta vayiram, cikappu mutaliya kaṟkaḷil mīṉ vaṭivam kāṇappaṭṭateṉṟum, colvatik kavaṉikkiyil iṉṉa kālameṉṟu niccayam colla muṭiyāta pūrvakālattil tamiḻ makkaḷ mecōppottāmiyā nāṭṭilum atic cuṟṟilumuḷḷa pāracīkam, pelujistāṉ mutaliya nāṭukaḷilum kuṭiyēṟiṉārkaḷeṉṟum, aracāṭci ceytārkaḷeṉṟum avarkaḷ pāṣiyē pakkattu nāṭukaḷilum pala pētaṅkaḷiyaṭintu vaḻaṅki vanta teṉṟum eṇṇa iṭamirukkiṟatu. itōṭu intu jermāṉik pāṣiyiyum ataṉ kiḷip pāṣikaḷiyum kavaṉittāl tamiḻ vārttikaḷ ērāḷamāka avaṟṟil kalantiruppatik kāṇalām.
airōppiya pāṣiyil kāṇappaṭum tamiḻ vārttikaḷukku utāraṇamāka 100 vārttikaḷ muṉpu colliyirukkiṟōm. ivvārtti kaḷik kavaṉippōmāṉāl tamiḻ nāṭṭiṉ jaṉaṅkaḷ paḻakkattil cātāraṇamāka upayōkikkum tamiḻ moḻikaḷāyirukkiṉṟaṉaveṉṟu nām aṟivōm. āṉāl jermāṉik allatu airōppiyaṉ kūṭṭattic cērnta pala pāṣikaḷiṉ vārttikaḷil ētāvatu oṉṟu intiya pāṣiyil (tamiḻ moḻiyil) kalavātu pallāyira varuṭaṅkaḷukku muṉpē taṉitta ciṟappuṟṟatāyp pōtumāṉa ilakkaṇa ilakkiyaṅkaḷuṭiyatāyt tērnta kalikaḷuṭiyatāyc caṅkītattil nāḷatu variyum maṟṟavarkaḷāl kaṇṭu piṭikkappaṭāta nuṭpamāṉa pākupāṭukaḷi yuṭiyatāyiruppatik kavaṉittāl intiyāvil oru kālam mikuntu vaḻaṅki vanta tamiḻ moḻiyē pūrvamāṉa moḻi eṉṟu colla niyāyamirukkiṟatu.
oru caṅkiliyiṉ ātiyum antamumāṉa iraṇṭu vaḷiyaṅkaḷip pōl intu jermāṉik pāṣiyiruppatāl itaṉ naṭuvil oṉṟō ṭoṉṟu campantappaṭṭa pala vaḷiyaṅkaḷiruppatu pōl intu pāṣi mutal jermāṉik pāṣi variyum pala kalappuṟṟa pāṣikaḷ vaḻaṅki yirukka vēṇṭumeṉpatu uṇmiyē.
intiyā mutal ettiyōppiyā tēcam variyumuḷḷa 127 tēcaṅkaḷi yum āṇṭu koṇṭirunta ākāsvēruviṉ rājyattik kavaṉippō māṉāl taṉatu cūcāṉ paṭṭaṇattil 127 tēcaṅkaḷiluḷḷa irājarkaḷukkum, pirapukkaḷukkum āṟumātam viruntu ceytāṉ eṉṟu collappaṭukiṟatu. atōṭu cumēriyar pāpilōṉ niṉivē mutaliya iṭaṅkaḷilum aracāṭci ceytu vantārkaḷ. avarkaḷ tamiḻ nāṭṭiliruntupōṉa tamiḻ makkaḷ pāracīkattilum, pelujistāṉ malikaḷilum kuṭiyiruntavarkaḷ pēciya pirakūyis pāṣiyik kavaṉikkumpoḻutum avarkaḷum tamiḻarkaḷākavē yiruntārkaḷ. kaltēyarukku muṉṉirunta pūrva kuṭikaḷ vaṇaṅki vanta mīṉ corupa (tākōṉ vikkiraka)ttik koṇṭum, pacuvik koṇṭum avarkaḷum tamiḻ makkaḷāyirukka vēṇṭum.
cattiyavētattil collappaṭukiṟa tākōṉ eṉṉum vikkirakam mīṉ vaṭivamāyiruntateṉṟum pelistar ati vaṇaṅkiṉārkaḷeṉṟum piṉvarum varikaḷāl kāṇalām.
cattiya vētam ai cāmuvēl 5-2.
“pelistar tēvaṉuṭiya peṭṭiyip piṭittu tākōṉiṉ kōvililē koṇṭu vantu tākōṉaṇṭiyilē vittārkaḷ.”
cattiya vētam niyāyātipatikaḷ 16-23.
“pelistariṉ pirapukkaḷ nammuṭiya pakiñaṉākiya cimcōṉi nammuṭiya tēvaṉ nammuṭiya kiyil oppuk koṭuttār eṉṟu colli taṅkaḷ tēvaṉākiya tākōṉukku oru periya pali celuttavum cantōṣam koṇṭāṭavum kūṭivantārkaḷ.”
Biblical Cyclopedia Page 190.
“Dagon. (1 Sam. V. 2). This was the name of a celebrated idol of the Philistines, worshipped at Gaza, (Judg. XVI. 23) at Ashdod, (1 Sam. V.1.3) at Beth dagon, (“the house or temple of Dagon”) in the bounds of Judah, (Josh XV. 41) in a town of Asher, (Josh XIX. 27) and elsewhere. There are various opinions as to the appearance of this idol, but it is usually represented with the head, hands, and face of a man, and the body like that of a fish. The name was probably derived from dag signifying a large fish. One of the incarnations of the Hindu god Vishnu was of the same form.”
“tākōṉ (1 cāmu. 5.2.) yūtēyā tēcattil uḷḷa (yōcu 15.41) ācēr (yōcu 19.27) eṉṉum nakarilum maṟṟum iṭaṅkaḷilum, kācā (niyā 16.23) astōt (1 cāmu. 5.1-3) pettākōṉ (tākōṉuṭiya vīṭu kōyil) eṉṉum iṭaṅkaḷilum vaṇaṅkappaṭṭa oru pērpōṉa vikkirakattiṉ peyar. anta vikkirakattiṉ uruvattip paṟṟip pala apippirāyaṅkaḷ irunta pōtilum, cātāraṇamāy atu maṉita tali, mukam, kikaḷuṭiyatākavum, mīṉippōṉṟa uṭal uruvamuṭiyatāyumiruntatākat terikiṟatu. Dag eṉpataṟku “oru periya mīṉ” eṉṟa arttam iruntatāka ūkikkalām. intukkaḷuṭiya teyvaṅkaḷil oṉṟākiya viṣṇu mīṉ avatāram eṭuttatākac collappaṭuvatiyum kavaṉikka vēṇṭum.”
mēṟkaṇṭa vacaṉaṅkaḷāl teṉmaturiyil aracāṇṭukoṇṭirunta cattiya virataṉip piraḷayattiṉiṉṟum kāppāṟṟa avataritta makāviṣṇu viṉ mīṉ uruvattip pelistarkaḷum avarkaḷuk karukilirunta ayal nāṭṭārum vaṇaṅki vantirukkiṟārkaḷeṉṟu terikiṟatu. ākiyāl oru kālattil teṉ pāṇṭi nāṭṭiliruntupōṉa tamiḻarkaḷ mecōpottā miyāvukkup pōy aṅkiruntu pala rājyaṅkaḷiyum stāpittu pala rājyattārākavum pala tēcattārākavum pala pāṣikkārarākavum pirintu viruttiyaṭintiruntārkaḷeṉṟum avarkaḷ pēci vanta pāṣi kālak kiramattil pala pāṣikaḷāka aḻikkappaṭiṉum tamiḻmoḻi kalappuṭiyatā yiṟṟeṉṟum colla ētuvirukkiṟatu. annāṭṭil pala rājyattārukkum potuvāka mīṉ corūpam teyvamāyiruntatu pōlat tamiḻ moḻiyē potuvāṉa moḻiyāyiruntirukka vēṇṭum.
camaskirutattil vaḻaṅki varum tamiḻ vārttikaḷiyum camas kirutattiṟkum, tamiḻukkum potuvāṉateṉṟu collappaṭum tamiḻ vārttikaḷiyum, airōppiya pāṣikaḷil kāṇappaṭum tamiḻ vārtti kaḷiyum, cīttiyapāṣiyil kāṇappaṭum tamiḻ vārttikaḷiyum muṉpu utāraṇamākak kāṭṭiyirukkiṟōm.
camaskiruta moḻikaḷum, airōppiya moḻikaḷum, cīttiya moḻikaḷum tamiḻ moḻiyōṭu kalantiruppatāka 2000 varuṭaṅkaḷukku muṉṉuḷḷa tamiḻ nūlkaḷil kāṇamāṭṭōm. itaṉālēyē tamiḻmoḻi ātiyil uṇṭāṉa teṉṟum avaṟṟil iyal ici nāṭakameṉṉum muttamiḻum pōtumāṉa tērcci peṟṟiruntateṉṟum avaṟṟil icittamiḻākiya caṅkītam mikavum naṉṟāka oḻuṅkupaṭuttappaṭṭu maṉatil tōṉṟum karuttukaḷattaṉiyum koṇṭatāṉa irāka amippuṭiya tāyiruntateṉṟum teḷivāyt terikiṟatu.
atōṭu vālillāk kuraṅkukaḷ variciyāyppāṭum paṉṉiru curaṅkaḷē āyappāliyiṉ paṉṉiru curaṅkaḷāka eṭuttuk koṇṭiruppatik koṇṭu itu maṉita uṟpattiyiṉ kāla mutal tamiḻ nāṭṭiliruntu viruttiyāṉa teṉṟu eṇṇa iṭamirukkiṟatu. pāṣiyiṉ ārampattiyum caṅkītattiṉ ārampattiyum maṟṟum tamiḻ makkaḷ vaḻaṅki vanta kalikaḷiṉ uṭkaruttiyum oṉṟu cērttup pārttāl tamiḻ moḻiyiṉ pūrvīkattiyum icit tamiḻiṉ (caṅkītattiṉ) nuṭpattiyum iṉimi yiyum evar kaṇṭu collak kūṭiyavar?
oru stāyiyip paṉṉiraṇṭāyp pirippatil 2/3, 3/4 muṟiyil kiṭikkum 2/3, 3/4, 4/5, 5/6, 3/5, 5/8 mutaliya curaṅkaḷiṉ oṟṟumi yillāmiyi nām kavaṉikkumpoḻutu, ca-pa muṟiyil iṇi iṇiyāy ēḻāvatu. ēḻāvatu irāciyāy ca-ma vāka kiḷi kiḷiyāy aintāvatu aintāvatu irāciyāyk kaṇṭupiṭittirunta pūrva tamiḻ makkaḷiṉ āyappāliyākiya mutalpaṭikkē iṉṉum maṟṟa tēcattavar vantu eṭṭa villi eṉpatu teḷivāka irukkiṟatu. atōṭu āyappāliyāy vaḻaṅki vanta paṉṉiraṇṭu curaṅkaḷum kaṇṭupiṭippatil ca-pavil koñcam koñcam kuṟittu oru stāyiyip paṉṉiraṇṭākat tamiḻ makkaḷ muṟipōl pirittiruntālum cariyāṉa kaṇakkuc collāmiyiṉāl Equal Temperament muṟiyeṉṟu ēḷaṉam ceyyappaṭukiṟatēyoḻiya nallateṉṟu koṇṭāṭap paṭavilli.
oru stāyiyi 24 alakukaḷākap pirittut tamiḻ makkaḷ vaḻaṅki vanta vaṭṭappāliyiṉ irakaciyam teriyāmal oru stāyiyil 22 curutikaḷ varukiṉṟaṉaveṉṟum ammuṟippaṭi irākaṅkaḷ pāṭappaṭa vēṇṭu meṉṟum, camaskiruta nūlōr iraṇṭāvatu paṭiyilēyē cantēkam koṇṭārkaḷ.
mutaṟ paṭiyik kāṇāmalum, iraṇṭāvatu paṭiyiṉ cantēkam tīrāmalu mirukkum poḻutu mūṉṟāvatu, nālāvatu tupaṭikaḷik kēṭpāṉēṉ? āyap pāli, vaṭṭappāli, tirikōṇap pāli, caturap pālikaḷil vaḻaṅki varum nuṭpa curaṅkaḷiyum, paṇkaḷiyum paṭittu aṉupavappaṭṭavarkaḷ tamiḻiṉ pūrvīkattiyum atil icittamiḻiṉ uyarviyum iṉi oruvāṟu aṟivārkaḷ.
maṉita, miruka, paṭci, ūrvaṉa, tāvaraṅkaḷiyum pāṭupavaṉ maṉatiyum kēṭpavaṉ maṉaciyum teyvattiyum cantōṣappaṭuttumpaṭiyāṉa caṅkītam icit tamiḻil mika nuṭpamāṉa curutiyuṭaṉ paṉṉīrāyiram āti icikaḷākat tamiḻ makkaḷāl pāṭappaṭṭu vantatiyum maṟṟa tēcattavar paṉṉiraṇṭu curaṅkaḷukkē tiṭṭamāṉa kaṇakkillāmal 2/3, 3/4 aik kūṭṭip perukkik koṇṭiruppatiyum nām kavaṉippōmāṉāl tamiḻ moḻiyē pūrvamāṉa tāy moḻi eṉṟum icit tamiḻē āti caṅkītameṉṟum cantēka maṟat teḷivākak kāṇpōm.



3. karnāṭaka caṅkītattil vaḻaṅki varum curutikaḷip paṟṟiya muṭivuri.
karuṇāmirta cākarattiṉ elliyāy niṉṟa curam, curutikaḷ, nuṭpamāṉa curutikaḷi ituvariyum kavaṉittu vantōm. caṅkīta cāstirattiṟku iv viṣayam mika mukkiyamāṉateṉṟu eṇṇukiṟēṉ.
tamiḻp pāṣikku uyir eḻuttu, meyyeḻuttu, uyirmeyyeḻuttu, āyuta eḻuttum kaṇitattiṟku mēlvāy ilakkaṅkaḷ kīḻvāy ilakkaṅ kaḷum eppaṭi avaciyamāṉatō appaṭiyē caṅkītattil vaḻaṅki varum ōcikaḷi aṟivataṟku āyappāliyil vaḻaṅki varum paṉṉiraṇṭāṉa aric curaṅkaḷum, vaṭṭappāliyil vaḻaṅki varum irupattunālāṉa kāl curaṅkaḷum, tiri kōṇappāliyil vaḻaṅki varum nāṟpatteṭṭāṉa arikkāl curaṅkaḷum, caturappāliyil vaḻaṅki varum toṇṇūṟṟāṟāṉa vīcam curaṅkaḷum mika mukkiyamāṉavi. ivaṟṟip pūrva tamiḻ makkaḷ payiṉṟu vanta yāḻil kamakaṅkaḷāka vaḻaṅki vantirukkiṟārkaḷ. ippoḻutum yāḻ vācippōr vaḻaṅki varukiṟārkaḷ. itaṉ nuṭpam iṉṉateṉṟu teḷivākac collum pūrva tamiḻ nūlkaḷ maṟintapiṉ “yāṉi kaṇṭa kuruṭareṉa” caṅkītattil vaḻaṅki varum nuṭpamāṉa curaṅkaḷukkup palar palavitamākak kaṇakkuc coṉṉārkaḷ.
atōṭu cumār 2500 varuṭaṅkaḷukkumuṉ intiyāviṟku vantu pōṉavarāṉa pitākōras eṉṉum tattuva ñāṉiyiṉāl ca-pa 2/3, ca-ma 3/4 eṉṟu vīṇit tantiyiṉ aḷavu mēṟṟicikkuk koṇṭu pōkappaṭṭu atiliruntu palavittiyācamāṉa kaṇakkukaḷ ēṟpaṭṭaṉa.
intiyāvilirunta camaskiruta vittuvāṉkaḷiṟ paratar, caṅkīta ratṉākarar pōṉṟavarkaḷ oru stāyiyil 22 curutikaḷ varukiṉṟaṉaveṉṟu curaṅkaḷukkuc curutiyiṉ kaṇakkum irāka ilakṣaṇamum colli vittārkaḷ. itaṉāl karnāṭaka caṅkītattilum, maṟṟum caṅkītattilum vaḻaṅki varum curaṅkaḷiyum, curutikaḷiyum niccayippatu kūṭāta kāriyamāy muṭintatu.
karnāṭaka caṅkītattil vaḻaṅki varum curam curutikaḷ iṉṉaviyeṉṟu terintu koṇṭāloḻiya oru irākatti uṇṭākkavum iṉimiyuṭaṉ pāṭavum kūṭiyatalla veṉpatu niccayam. irākaṅkaḷi uṇṭākkavum, pāṭik koṇṭirukkum irākaṅkaḷiṉ piḻikaḷit tiruttik koḷḷavum kūṭiyatāṉa oru muṟiyik kaṇṭa nāṉ ati caṅkīta vittuva cirō maṇikaḷ yāvarukkum piracittappaṭutti viruttikkuk koṇṭu varuvataṟ kākac caṅkīta vityā makājaṉa caṅkam eṉṟu oru capi 1912 varuṭam mē mātam 27-m tētiyil ēṟpaṭuttiṉēṉ.
atil nāṭṭi irākattil varum curaṅkaḷ iṉṉaviyeṉṟu capi yōrāl vicārikkappaṭṭatu. eḻupattiraṇṭu mēḷakkarttāviṉpaṭi kuṟikka vēṇṭumeṉṟu cilarum tuvāvimcati curutiyiṉpaṭi kuṟikka vēṇṭumeṉṟu cilarum vātāṭiṉārkaḷ. vīṇiyil kaṇṭapaṭi kuṟikka vēṇṭumeṉṟu micca māṉavarkaḷ coṉṉālum curam curutikaḷip paṟṟiya teḷivāṉa apip pirāyam collak kūṭāmiyiṉāl aṭutta kāṉpareṉsil tīrmāṉippa tākavum apippirāyam collakkūṭiyavarkaḷ colla vēṇṭumeṉṟum kēṭṭuk koḷḷappaṭṭatu. appaṭiyē 6 kāṉpareṉcukaḷilum pūrṇamāy vicārikkappaṭṭatu.
curutikaḷip paṟṟic coṉṉavarkaḷiṉ kaṇakkum avarkaḷ aṉupava mum oṉṟaṟkoṉṟu ovvāmalum muṉṉukkup piṉ virōtamāyum iruntataṉāl nāṉum curutiyip paṟṟic cila colla vēṇṭiyatāyiṟṟu. atiṉāl curutikaḷip paṟṟic collum palaruṭiya vevvēṟu apip pirāyaṅkaḷiyum  ellārukkum eṭuttukkāṭṭuvatum tuvāvimcati curuti muṟi karnāṭaka caṅkītattiṟku ottuvarāteṉṟu rucuppaṭuttuvatum avaciya māyiruntatu. intiyāviṉ pūrva kuṭikaḷ vaḻaṅki vanta icittamiḻiṉ nuṭpam iṉṉateṉṟu vicārippatu mukkiyameṉat tōṟṟiṟṟu.
pūrva tamiḻ makkaḷ vaḻaṅki vanta āyappāli, vaṭṭappāli, tirikōṇappāli, caturappāli eṉṟa nālu pālikaḷukkum avarkaḷ collum karuttiṉpaṭi aḷavum, kirakam māṟum poḻutu paṉṉiru pāli yuṇṭākum muṟiyum, avikaḷil ēḻu perumpālikaḷiyum colla nērntatu. ēḻu curaṅkaḷukkum, paṉṉiru aric curaṅkaḷukkum irupattu nāṉku curutikaḷukkum maṟṟum nuṭpamāṉa curutikaḷukkum taṟkālattavar collum ōciyiṉ alikaḷiṉ kaṇakkum ceṉṭs kaṇakkum kāṭṭa vēṇṭiyatāyiṟṟu.
curam curutikaḷippaṟṟic collum kaṇakkil 2/3, 3/4, 4/5, 5/6 pōṉṟa piṉṉa aḷavuḷḷa cariyāṉa ōciyik koṭukkamāṭṭātākiyiṉāl pūrva tamiḻ nūliṉ karuttiṉpaṭikkum caṅkīta ratṉākarariṉ karuttiṉpaṭikkum iraṇṭiṟkuriya turuvalakkattik (Logarithm) koṇṭu curaṅkaḷukkum curutikaḷukkum kaṇakkuk kaṇṭu piṭikkappaṭṭirukkiṟatu. iraṇṭiṟkuriya turuvalakkattiṉpaṭi (Logarithm)  curaṅkaḷukkum curutikaḷukkum kiṭikkum tantiyiṉ aḷavum atil pēcappaṭum curaṅkaḷum iṉṉaviyeṉṟu taṉittu aṭṭavaṇiyākavum koṭukkappaṭṭirukkiṟatu.
av aṭṭavaṇiyil kaṇṭa curaṅkaḷ taṟkālam karnāṭaka caṅkītattil vaḻaṅki varukiṉṟaṉa eṉpataṟku utāraṇamāka 67 karnāṭaka irākaṅkaḷ nālu aṭṭavaṇiyāyk kāṭṭappaṭṭirukkiṉṟaṉa.
atōṭu yāvarum aṟintu koḷḷakkūṭiya vitamāka Staff notationil kuṟikkum muṟiyum mēṟṟici caṅkītattiṟkum intiya caṅkītattiṟkumuḷḷa cura oṟṟumiyum teḷivākak kāṭṭiyirukkiṟēṉ. tamiḻnāṭṭil mikap pūrvamāyuḷḷa icittamiḻip piṟkālattiya tamiḻ aracarkaḷum mikavum ātarittu vantārkaḷeṉṟu kāṇpataṟkuc cila cācaṉaṅkaḷ kāṭṭap paṭṭirukkiṉṟaṉa.
teṉ maturiyilirunta tamiḻ makkaḷ mecōppottāmiyāvukkup pōyk kuṭiyēṟi pāpilōṉ, niṉivē eṉṉum nakaraṅkaḷik kaṭṭiṉārka ḷeṉṟum atil aracāṭci ceytārkaḷeṉṟum, avarkaḷ tamiḻp pēci vantārkaḷeṉṟum, atiliruntu pala pāṣikaḷ uṇṭāyiṉaveṉṟum tamamiḻ moḻiyē tāy moḻiyāyirukka vēṇṭumeṉṟum tamiḻ makkaḷiṭa miruntē caṅkītam, cōtiṭam, vittiyam mutaliya ariya vittikaḷ maṟṟa tēcaṅkaḷukkup paraviṉa veṉṟum tamiḻ moḻi pāṣikaḷ yāvaṟṟilum kalantiruppatiyum, maṟṟap pāṣikaḷiṉ vārttikaḷ tamiḻil kalavā tiruppatiyuṅ koṇṭu tamiḻ moḻiyē mutal moḻiyāyirukka vēṇṭu meṉṟum ettēcattavarum vaḻaṅkātatum aṟintu koḷḷātatumāṉa nuṭpa curaṅkaḷit tamiḻ makkaḷ aṟintu vaḻaṅki vantiruppatiṉāl tamiḻ makkaḷē caṅkītattil mutaṉmi peṟṟavarkaḷ maṟṟavarkaḷ yāvarum avarkkup pintiyavarkaḷē eṉṟum kāṭṭakkūṭiya pūrva carittirak kuṟippukaḷum colliyirukkiṟōm.
mikap pūrvamāṉavareṉṟu maṟṟavarkaḷāl eṇṇappaṭum paratarum, cāraṅkatēvarum eḻutiya tuvāvimcati curutiyiṉ tappu apippirāyattit tirutta ivvaḷavu eḻutavēṇṭiyatāyiṟṟu. atōṭu 2/3, 3/4 āṉa muṟiyē iyaṟki aḷavu eṉṟu colluvōriṉ karuttu cariyāṉatallaveṉṟu rucuppaṭuttik kāṭṭuvataṟkum tamiḻarkaḷukkuc caṅkītam ētu eṉṟu aṟiyātār kūṟuvati māṟṟuvataṟkum atikam eḻuta nēriṭṭatu. caṅkīta viṣayamākavum atic cērntatāṉa carittira viṣayamākavum curuti viṣaya mākavum avaṟṟiṉ kaṇakku viṣayamākavum nāṉ colliyiruppavi mikac coṟpameṉṟē niṉikkiṟēṉ. itil collappaṭum mēṟkoḷḷum tiṣṭāntaṅkaḷum mikac ciṟitāyiruntālum karuttu aṟintu koḷvataṟkup pōtumāṉateṉṟu eṇṇukiṟēṉ.
nūtaṉamāy irākaṅkaḷ colvataṟkum pāṭikkoṇṭirukkum irākaṅkaḷilum kīrttaṉikaḷilum varum piḻikaḷit tiruttik koḷvataṟkumuriya mukkiya amcaṅkaḷi iraṇṭām puttakattil kāṇpōm.
ipputtakam eḻuti muṭiyum camayattil parōṭāvil His Highness makārājā avarkaḷ kūṭṭi vitta All India Music Conferencel curutiyip paṟṟic colla vēṇṭumeṉṟu eṉṉik kēṭṭuk koṇṭataṉāl appaṭiyē ceyya vēṇṭiyatu nēriṭṭatu. ākiyiṉāl avviṣayattip paṟṟic cila colvatum iti vācikkum aṉparkaḷukku upayōkamāyirukkum. av viṣayattip paṟṟi nāṉ coṉṉavum maṟṟavarkaḷ colliyavumāṉa viṣayaṅkaḷ pēppar mūlamāka vantiruppatiṉāl avikaḷi iṅku tokuttukkāṭṭuvatu pōtumeṉṟu niṉikkiṟēṉ.

1913-m varuṭam ākasṭu mātam 9-m tētiyil tañciyil naṭanta nālāvatu caṅkīta vityā makājaṉa caṅkattiṟkup piraciṭeṉṭāyirukkumpaṭi nāṉ Devan Sahib V.P. mātavarāv avarkaḷi nēril kēṭṭuk koṇṭa poḻutu avarkaḷum cantōṣamāy oppuk koṇṭu akkirācaṉam vakittu capiyi mika naṉṟāka naṭattiṉārkaḷ. ataṉ piṉ caṅkīta viṣayamāka ippaṭi oru capiyi nam intiyāviluḷḷa Native  irājākkaḷil oruvar naṭattiṉāl mikap pirayōjaṉamāyirukkum. nam intiya tēca caṅkītam cīrtiruttamaṭiyum. appaṭi oru kāṉperaṉs naṭipeṟumāṉāl tāṅkaḷum vantiruntu mukkiyamāṉa kāriyaṅkaḷil utavi ceyya vēṇṭum eṉṟu kēṭṭuk koṇṭārkaḷ. ataṉpiṟaku appaṭiyē his hiṉas parōṭā makārājā avarkaḷukkum apippirāya miruppatākavum 1915-m varuṣam ṭicampar mātam kāṉpareṉs naṭattap pōkiṟatākavum ataṟku nīṅkaḷum varavēṇṭum eṉṟum eṉakku nēril coṉṉārkaḷ. atikak kuḷirāyiruppatiṉāl pepravari kaṭici allatu mārccu mātattil vittuk koṇṭāl nāṉ varukiṟataṟku aṉukūlamāyirukkumeṉṟu kēṭṭuk koṇṭēṉ. ataṟ kiṇaṅki makārājā avarkaḷukkum maṟṟum avarkaḷ pirajikaḷukkum aṉukūlamāṉa kāmaṉ paṇṭiki naṭakkum tiṉaṅkaḷil mārccu mātam 20-m tēti mutal 25-m tēti variyum miyūcik kāṉpareṉs naṭattappaṭṭatu.
intiyāviṉ pala pākaṅkaḷil curutiyip paṟṟiyum caṅkītattiṉ maṟṟum viṣayaṅkaḷip paṟṟiyum vicārittuk koṇṭirukkum aṟivāḷi kaḷil 23 pērkaḷ memparkaḷākat terinteṭukkappaṭṭatōṭu maṟṟum pala iṭaṅkaḷiliruntum intustāṉi caṅkītam karnāṭaka caṅkītaṅkaḷil tērnta pēr peṟṟa pala vitvāṉkaḷ aḻikkappaṭṭiruntārkaḷ. evvitamāṉa kuṟivumiṉṟi ellōrum cantōṣaṅ koṇṭāṭakkūṭiya vitamāyt taṅkuvataṟkum pōjaṉattiṟkum ēṟṟa vacatikaḷum veku vimariciyāka ēṟpaṭṭiruntaṉa. annāṭkaḷ irājāṅkattiṟkuriya paṇṭiki nāṭkaḷ āṉatāl varuṭantōṟum iyalpāy naṭakkum uṟcavac ciṟappum caṅkīta kaccērikaḷum irājā piṟanta nāḷ koṇṭāṭṭamum miyūcik kāṉpareṉs naṭakkum capiyum oṉṟucērntu iravu pakal iṉṉateṉṟu teriyāmal nāḷ muḻuvatum koṇṭāṭappaṭṭatu.
