13
THE ALL-INDIA MUSIC CONFERENCE
Baroda, 20th March, 1916.
I have read the account of the above conference held on the 20th of March 1916 and the succeeding days at Baroda, from the pen of Mr. Clements I.C.S. This seems to be an account of what Mr.Clements thought about what happened there. It is but natural that accounts of a scientific conference should vary according to the different stand-points from which the proceedings are viewed by different artists. The two most important subjects discussed at the conference (1) the srutis in the use in Indian music and (2) how for the Staff notation could be made use of by all for noting down Indian Ragas. I desire to make a few remakrs on the above subjects.
One of the most noteworthy figures in the conference was that of Mr.Clements who practically demostrated his views as reards Srutis and their calculation based upon those of Sarnga Dev by means of Harmonium specially constructed for the purpose. The concord between Swarams was determined by arithmetical calculations and the pitch thereof was at the same time sounded on the Harmonium. He was warmly supported by Mr.Deval who had brought a number of books and an instrument known as the Bhin for demonstration thereon. Besides the time that had been allotted for them at the several meetings they were given free permission to controvert views that were opposed to them at all times. As their on Srutis were aginst these of Mr. Bhatkandi and others, there was a pleasant war of words between them almost every five minutes. The musical experts present there were closely watching those altercations with as much zest as that of people who had staked their all on favourite race horse! Such a tight was of course necessary for arriving at truth which might be of use to all musicians. This question of Srutis was discussed off and on almost every day.
Besides this on the 22nd of March, I read my essay the whole morning session (33/4 hours) as regards the Srutis of Indian music and practically demostrated the same on the Veena. It was there pointed out that the desciples of Sarnga Dev, while professing to follow his measurements, really followed the Sa-Pa (2/3) and Sa-Ma (3/4) system of Pythagoeras, that this was aginst the system of Sarnga Dev, that the 13 Srutis, for Sa-Pa and the 9 Srutis for Sa-Ma of Sarnga Dev could never be obtined if Sa-Pa was taken to be equal to 2/3 and Sa-Ma to 3/4. It was also clearly demonstrated that the Sruti system of Sarnga Dev as well as of those who followed 2/3 and 3/4 rule would never be scientific nor would they agree with Srutis that have been in use from time immemorial amongst the Tamilians handed down for generations. This was the subject of my first essay.
The second essay dealt with the musical efficiency of the ancient Tamilians as it was found in Silappadikaram, written about 1850 years ago by Ilankovadigal, and Tholkupiam, placed at the Sangam before Athankote Asan who lived in South Madura (or destroyed Lemuria) about 8000 years ago during the regin of Nilantharutheruvil Pandyan. the Conqueror. It was pointed out there how the ancient Tamilians derived 12 Swarams by the Sa-Pa and the Sa-Ma series and used them in their Yal and how they derived 12000 diffeent ragas by the change of Grahaswarams. Agin, it was shown how by the help of the cycle of 12 rasis, the 12 Swarams were obtined at the seventh places proceeding by Sa-Pa series towards the right, and how the same Swarams were obtined at the fifth places proceeding by the Sa-Ma series towards the left. It was shown how each of the rasis was subdivided into two Algus and ganam was made in the 22 Alagus, only omitting an Alagu each in Vilari and Kaikili. The four kinds of Yal setting forth the Swarams to be omitted in the ganam and the four sub-divisions of Jathis in each of the yals were also explined. It was pointed out that these rules had become obsolete when Bharata in the V Century and Sarnga Dev in the XIII Century wrote their works on music. Their 22 Srutis in the Octave became a stumbling block to all, and this, along with the 2/3 and 3/4 system of Pythagoras, made matters worse.
This over, it was shown how ganam was made in Ayapali with 12 Algus, in Vattapali with 24 Alagus, in Thirikonapali with 48 half or two for each of the 24 Alagus and in Chathurapali with 96 quarter Alagus or 2 for each of the 48. A table showing the 67 Ragas derived from the above four Palis, and the table showing the fractions according to Geometrical Progression, number of vibrations, length of wire and cents for the 12 half Swarams, 24 quarter-Swarams, 48 one-eight Swarams and 96 one-sixteenth Swarams were given. Practical demonstrations of ragas given in the four Palis were given according to the wishes of the members. It was listened to with rapt attention by the Karnatic as well as the Hindustani musicians assembled there. Sacruddin Saheb, the court musician of Oodipur, himself joined in the demonstration of the 24 Srutis with Veena and appreciated and admitted the System. When my dughters Maragathavalli Ammal (Mrs. Duripandian) and Kanagavali Ammal (Mrs. Navamoney) sang the 24 Stutis without the help of the Veena the whole assembly was in raptures and clapped their hands saying that a new musical era had dawned upon the world, that there was no longer any necessity for investigating the question of Srutis, and that the systems of Srutis of such and such people had been sent to the bottmless pit for ever! Atiya Fyzee Rahimin Begum, the accomplished and enlightened lady, was so delighted with the performance that she invited Mr.Clements and Mr.Bhatkandi to a very close examination of the Veena and to bestow all thought upon the demonstration. A number of Keerthanams were also sung by my dughters to demonstrate the use of very minute Swarams. When the demonstration was over, I threw out a challenge asking musicians to come forward and state their objections, if any, before the learned audience. None came forward with any objection. Many remarked that the 22 Sruti System should be given up for ever and that there was no need for any further investigation.
His Highness the Gaekwar and her Highness the Maharani expressed a desire to hear the same themselves. So before a select audience consisting of the Royal family including their Highnesses, His excellency Dewan V.P. Madava Row President the Nawab Ali Khan, Mr. Clements, Mr. Bhatkandi, and Mrs. Atya Begum and a few other select people, my dughters and myself were asked to repeat the demonstration of the previous day. So the same thing was gone through once more. Mr. Panchapakesa Bagavattar, Mr.N.P.Subramania Iyer, Mr. Fyzee Rahimin, Mr.Sundra Pandian, and Mrs. Pakiam Abraham were also present. I then pointed out how this conference organised by His Highness came just in time, to set the minds of musicians at ease, as the whole Sruti system of Indian music had been in a state of doubt owing to the disappearance of the ancient eminent music of the Tamilians and the appearance of the 22 Sruti system of Sarnga Dev, made worse by the 2/3 and 3/4 System of Pythagoras, and finished with a prayer for blessings on His Highness for having given orders to translate that ancient Tamil work Tholkupiam into the English language.
I then demonstrated to those assembled, within ten minutes, how the Srutis derived by proceeding by 2/3 and 3/4 and the 22 Srutis had never been in use in music and how they could never be used in the future.
It was also explined clearly how the calculations of Sarnga Dev given in his sutras could be correctly obtined by Geometrical progression.
This was followed for 45 minutes by a few Karnatic and other Keerthanams where the 24 Srutis of the Octave and more minute Srutis occurred.
His Highness the Maharaja and her Highness the Maharani were much delighted and expressed their grateful thanks.
I had already written to Mr. V.N.Bhatkandi that those who read essays on Srutis must practically demonstrate their theories, and that theories without a demonstration should be discarded. The same was emphasised by me on the 22nd and I dmanded practical demonstration for the benefit of the audience. Agin, on the 23rd when Mr. Clements read his essay on Srutis I requested him to demonstrate whether the 22 Srutis of his special Harmonium constructed after the System of Sarnga Dev agreed with the Srutis in practical use. It was decided by the members as well as the President, Mr. Thakur Nawab Ali Khan, that the swarams of the Harmonium of Mr. Clements were rather flat when compared with the swarams of the Ragam Kapi as sung by Sackruddin Saheb of Oodayapur and other Vidwans. In addition to this it was also argued that the interretation of Sanskrit Sootras was inaccurate; and then some of the Sanksrit experts came forward and gave the right interpretation which ended all controversy.
In spite of repeated demonstrations, Mr. Clements had to acknowledge that the Swarams of his Harmonium were really flatter and thus the controversy as regards the usefulness of his intrument practically ended here. I consider this to be one of the most definite results arrived at by the conference, as it consumed the greater part of their time, as it was a question which was very freely discussed, as it was based upon the system of Sarnga Dev and as some of the members took objection to it. The truth of this is well known to Mr.Nawab Ali Khan the President, to Dewan Saheb V.P.Madava Row Avergal who managed the affairs of the conference and to the other members. It would have been some good if Mr.Clements had made mention of this.
The next morning at the conference Mr. Clements sid that I followed the System of Equal Temperament of the westerners which was unsuited to Indian melody and argued that Indian ganam should be according to 22 Srutis. Then with the permission of the President I made the following observations for 3/4 of an hour :-
(1) That the term 22 Srutis is Octave is due to Sarnga Dev’s misconception of the 24 Alagus Sruti system of the ancient Tamilians.
(2) That the system 22 Srutis is wrong becuse, calculating the series by the Sa-Pa system instead of getting 13 Srutis for each of the steps we get 12 for Pa, Ri and 11. for Dha, Gha.
(3) That the 13th Sruti of Sarnga Dev, or PA gets 709 cents according to him while according to the adherents of the 2/3 system it gets 702 cents and that, neither of these coincides with the exact Pa which is in practical use.
(4) That the calculations 2/3 or 3/4 never completely finish the Octave.
It was further pointed out to Mr.Clements that, according to Sarnga Dev, the Srutis of an Octave should be a gradually ascending series without admitting any other possible sound between, that when two Srutis of Sa change their graham the Ga and Ni obtin the places of Ri and Dha, that agin quoting from his own book according to Sarnga Dev when three Srutis change their graham, Ri and Dha with 3 Srutis obtin the places of Sa and Pa. In spite of all these statements he (Mr.Clements) gives Srutis with unequal measurements. Srutis whose cents are as varied as 71, 41, 22, 90 and 49. Swarams with such unequal intervals will never suit the process of singing Graha-Swarams. They are entirely unsuited to music Professor Owen and Mr.Waterhouse mention that even the apes of Java sang the chromtic scale without a flaw! The Western musicians mention that, in tuning a piano by fifths, one should not be rigid but must have the firfths slightly flatter. Equal temperament was used by Mozart and Beethoven only 120 years ago, whereas the Tamilians have been using the system very commonly for the past 2000 years and more. the same system continues even to day. They were demonstrated yesterday on the Veena. I fully believe that this system alone has come to say. I shall be pleased if Mr.Clements could refute my system. Criticisms and remarks were called for and none came forward with any and the meeting terminated.
In the afternoon an essay was read by my dughter Maragathavalli Ammal (Mrs.Duripandian) in which she stated that the English staf notation as understood by many could form the basis for noting the Indian Srutis, that minuter Srutis could be marked by numbers pertining to particular Alagus of the Srutis and that Indian Ragas and Keerthanams could be divided into bars according to the time in which they are written. To illustrate this practically she had reduced to Staff notation the Pallavis of four Keertanams in Ayapali, Vattapali, Thirikonapali and Chathurapali and these were sung before the audience. A Keertanam in the Ragam Kakanakuthoogalam was sung which so attracted the attention of Mr.Fredilis, the Band master of Baroda, that he expressed a desire that it should be reduced to Staff notation. It was accordingly done by my dughter and it was reproduced by Mr.Fredilis in the flute who expressed to the audience the advantage of Staff-notation for Indian music. It would have been very gratifying if Mr.Clements had included these facts in the account.
Mr.Clements who was present throughtout the conference, seeing that I am acquainted with English musical notations says that I am reading English Music into Indian music by adopting Equal temperament and that I reject the theories of Bharata and Sarnga Dev. It is true that I reject Sarnga Dev so far as he says there are 22 Srutis in the Octave which will never suit modern music, and it is equally true that the 12 tempered notes of the westerners exactly correspond to the 12 Swarams used by the ancient Tamilians thousands of years. Mr. Clements does not subscribe to the above two statements, and hence his criticism.
To ask a few plin questions, who rejected the Harmonium of Mr.Clements constructed by him to suit the 22 Srutis of Sarnga Dev? Was it I alone or the President and members of the All India Mysic conference? Are not the 12 Swarams of a harmonium, the 12 Swarams of a Veena and the 12 min Swarams sung by all Indian vocalists one and the same? Are these not after equal Temperament? Dis not the conference in a body resolve to make the use of the Staff notation in these 12 Swarams for Hindustani Ragams for beginners? Was I the only supporter of these 12 Swarams; Were not the adherents of Sarnga Dev and the advocates of the 22 Srutis present there? Why were they not bold enough to stand up and refute these? Am I to blame becuse I made use of Geometrical Progression for the calculations of the 12 Swarams the 24 Srutis and the minuter ones?
Agin, which is prior, whether the system which is found in Silappadikaram written in the first century by Ilankovadigal or that of Mozart and Beethoven dating from the beginning of the 19th century?
Many writers on Srutis say that Sa-Pa=2/3 and give 702 cents for Pa. But it has 701.955 cents. If 701.955 were added on to this and if the result was substracted from 1200, the cents for the Octave, we get 203.910 or the cents for R1. This is the process by which each of the other Sthanams is obtined. The Octave must exactly finish at 1200. But it does not really finish so, as Sa-Pa, taken to be 2/3, is incorrect. By the principle of 2/3, the 22 Srutis finish at 1043 cents, thus falling short of 157 cents. But if we proceed 24 steps by the Sa-Pa series we get 1247 cents. As it is nearer 1200 than the result of the other it is clear that the system of 24 Srutis is better than Sa-Pa 2/3 system or 702 cents for Pa. It is also clear that R1 and Dha with 3 Srutis each should in reality have four Srutis. This sytem of 3 Alagus Srutis for R1 and Dha is found in the system of Neythal Yal of the ancient Tamilians where one Alagu for R1 and Dha was purposely left out.
Are the 12 Swarams of an octave which stand in the relation of Ini and Kili, with 24 Alagus in practical use, in Karnatic music, at the present day the correct ones or the system of Sarnga Dev with 22 Srutis which was rejected the other day at the Conference, as the Harmonium constructed for that special purpose was found to be deficient in the Swarams pertining to the Karaharapirya or Kapi Ragas? We know that 2/3 can never divide itself completely nor can it multiply itself completely it is a recurring decimal. This spectre which has been dominating Western music for 2500 years has also begun its devilish work in India. The right Swarams in vogue can never be obtined by this method. I how that musicians will never hereafter use this measurement for determining the fractions and vibrations of Srutis. It is found that these 12 Swarams with equal measurements were used by the ancient Tamilians, that by the change of graham of these Swarams many ragas were generated, that even milk women, the simplest among the ancient Tamilians, sang their Aychiarkuravi with the help of grahaswarms, that when the book treating about them gradually fell into disuse many new theories were put forward, and that the westerners in the course of their researches adopted these swarams with Equal Temperament. It is not a theory of my own. Any one anxious to locate the Swarams one is dily using in a stringed instrument will find that they are same used by the ancient Tamilians for years.
I asked the other day a Bhagavather who considers himself well versed in Music as well as in the theory of Sarnga Dev, if he could compose a Ragam with the help of the 22nd Srutis of Sarnga Dev, with a given Lakshanam of the same author. He replied that he would be able to do the same after two months! When pressed to give his opinion as regards the systme by which he had become proficient in music he only blinked! The Dwavimsati srutis had never been in practical use at any time in India. To introduce them here will be derogatory to the ancient and dignified music of South India!
To write of the proceedings of a conference in Baroda, without having attended it, can be of very little use to any. I am reluctant to enter into a controversy with people who venture to write without a personal knowledge of what transpired. It would be well, if gentlemen, such as the President of the conference, and other responsbile people, write on the subject.
I read the account of Mr. Clements as well as that of Mr. Subramania Shastrial in the Madras Mail. I am at a loss to know why Mr.Clements is writing to Mr. Shastrial in private instead of openly ventilating his theories in the papers! He does not evidently like the idea of being criticised.
Members of the All India music Conference! In as much as the editors of the “Madras Mail”, “Swadesa Mitran”, “Hindu” and “New India” declined to publish this on account of its lengthness, I had to print it myself and distribute it to you. If either the President or the Secretary had written an account at the time it would have been fairer. I had to write this as Mr. Clements had omitted a few vital points. If my readers who are members of the conference would write about the truth or the otherwise of my statements and their own ideas as to my theory and the practical demonstration thereon I shall be pleased to print and circulate them to all the members.

parōṭāvil naṭanta āl-intiya caṅkīta kāṉpareṉs aṅkaṇattiṉarkaḷukku.
	1916-m varuṭam mārccu mātam 20-m tētiyil Indian Music eṉṟa talippiṉkīḻ ‘parōṭā kāṉpareṉs’ eṉṟa tuvakkattuṭaṉ Mr.E.Clements, I.C.S., turiyavarkaḷ Madras Mailš l eḻutiya viyācattip pārviyiṭṭēṉ. itil “All India Music Conference”l naṭantavikaḷik kuṟittuc colvatākat terikiṟatu. cāstira viṣayamāka naṭakkum oru periya capiyiṉ cārām catti taṅkaḷ taṅkaḷ aṟivukku eṭṭiya vitam palar pala vitamāy eḻutuvatu vaḻakkameṉṟu nām aṟivōm. capiyil naṭanta viṣayaṅkaḷil intiya caṅkītattil vaḻaṅkivarum curaṅkaḷ curutikaḷ iṉṉaviyeṉpatum avikaḷi ellōrum vaḻaṅkakkūṭiya vitamāy Staff notation-l kuṟippatu eppaṭi eṉpatumē mukkiyamāṉavi. ivviṣayattip paṟṟic cila kuṟippukaḷic colla virumpukiṟēṉ.
intiya caṅkītattil iṉṉiṉṉa curutikaḷ vaḻaṅka vēṇṭumeṉpatip paṟṟiyum avaṟṟiṉ kaṇakkukaḷip paṟṟiyum cāraṅkar muṟippaṭi Mr.Clements avarkaḷ tām putitākac ceyta ārmōṉiyam vācittu mika virivāka viyākkiyāṉam paṇṇiṉārkaḷ. curaṅkaḷukkuḷḷa oṟṟumiyik kaṇita mūlamākavum ataṉ ōciyi ārmōṉiyam mūlamākavum eṭuttuk kāṭṭiṉārkaḷ.

V.N.BHATKANDE Esq., B.A., L.L.B.,
Santaram House, Malabar Hil, Bombay.
MY DEAR RAO SAHIB PANDITHER,
It is a practically long time since we separated at Baroda and I think I ought to take up my correspondence with you once more in my own interest. I may sincerely tell you that your great labours and scholarship very nearly stunned me. I shall be always proud of having the privilege of calling you my friend. I may or may not agree with all your views but that will never prevent me from always bearing in mind the fact that you are a great Music scholar. I am so thankful to Dewan Saheb that he brought us together. I shall certinly not fail to derive considerable benefit from your labours. I have to thank you most sincerely for coming to my help in hitting that mischievous sruti harmonium movment on the head in time. It had very nearly turned the heads of several of our workers here. Mr. Deval had almost persuaded the educational authorities of this presidency to introduce the Harmonium as a compulsory accompaniment in our schools. But for you I should not have been able to make my poor voice heard. You disposed of Deval’s Sharangdev’s srutis like a miracle.
Your exposition has however brought to light one fact and that is likely to disappoint all the present music enthusiasts here. I am referring to that part of your book where you say or rather point out- that with the exception of the sa and its octave, none of the intermediate notes will exactly correspond with any of our modern notes. You go on to say agin that all attempts at reviving Sarangadev’s music is bound to be a failure. This conclusion of yours seems to be of tremendous importance.
Yours Sincerely,
(Sd.) V.N.BHATKANDE.

15
LAKSHMIPURAM. 
Mysore, 10-8-1916

DEAR SIR,
In your Tamil letter of invitation, I was glad to find that you are going agin to settle the question of Srutis. I heartily support your contention that Sharanga Dev was inaccurate in many respects, and that your exposition was most convincing. I appreciate only 3 or 4 papers that were presented in that Baroda Conference and yours was the most interesting to me of all. Those of Messrs. Clements and Deval were also learned, but the theories did not agree with their practical demonstrations.
I agree to your division of the octave into 24 srutis and their demonstration through the help of your accomplished dughters. I am sure that the different notes used for the Ragas as expounded by you are correct. Only I am not yet prepared to admit the accuracy of their number of Vibration. It is my desire to call in the aid of a practical scientist in physics and get the Vibrations of notes tested. I have expressed this idea before V.P.Madhava Rao Esq. who has approved of the proposal and if the Baroda Conference meets agin I will induce the audience to have recourse to this arrangement. Can you not take up this suggestion?
If any thing was striking to me in the Baroda Conference, it was your paper and I have made a short reference to it in my book “The Psychology of Music” which will be out in a week or so.
Wishing success to your earnest attempts.
Yours truly,
(Sd.) H.P.KRISHNA RAO.

micūr, 10-8-1916.
piriyamuḷḷa aiyā,
tāṅkaḷ eṉṉik kāṉpareṉsukku aḻitta (tamiḻil eḻutap paṭṭirunta) kaṭitattil kaṇṭapirakāram curuti viṣayattip paṟṟit tirumpa vicārikkappōkiṟōm eṉṟu eḻutiyiruntatu eṉakku metta cantōṣam. cāraṅkatēvar pala viṣayaṅkaḷil picakippōyirukkiṟār eṉṟu tāṅkaḷ colvati nāṉ maṉappūrvamāy oppukkoḷḷukiṟēṉ. tāṅkaḷ caṅkīta viṣayatti vistarittatāṉatu ellāruṭiya maṉatilum naṉṟāyppaṭṭatu. parōṭā kāṉpareṉcil vācikkappaṭṭa upanniyācaṅkaḷil mūṉṟu allatu nālu viyācaṅkaḷ tāṉ eṉakku atika vicēṣamāṉavikaḷāka eṉ maṉatil paṭṭatu. avikaḷil taṅkaḷuṭiyatu tāṉ ellāvaṟṟilum mēlāka eṉakkut tiruptikaratti uṇṭākkukiṟatu. Mr.kiḷamaṇṭs, tēvāl mutaliya varkaḷuṭiya upanniyācaṅkaḷ atikak kalvit tiṟamiyik kāṭṭiṉa pōtilum avarkaḷuṭiya muṟikaḷ vāttiyaṅkaḷiṉ rucuvōṭu ottirukka villi.
oru stāyiyi tāṅkaḷ 24 cama pākaṅkaḷākap piritta muṟi yiyum taṅkaḷuṭiya ciṟappu vāynta kalvit tiṟamiyuḷḷa kumārattikaḷiṉ utavi yāl tāṅkaḷ ati rucuppaṭuttiyatiyum cariyeṉṟu oppuk koḷḷu kiṟēṉ. pala irākaṅkaḷil varuvatākat tāṅkaḷ kāṇpitta curaṅkaḷ cari yeṉpataṟkuc cantēkamilli. āṉāl antac curaṅkaḷiṉ ōci ali kaḷip paṟṟi māttiram eṉakkuk koñcam cantēkamuṇṭu. iyaṟki cāstirattil tēṟiya oru nipuṇariṉ utaviyāl antac curaṅkaḷiṉ ōci alikaḷic cōtittup pārkka vēṇṭumeṉṟa āci eṉakkuṇṭu. nāṉ itu viṣayattip paṟṟi makā-rāca-rāca-ciṟi ē.ña.mātavarāv avarkaḷiṭattil pirastāpittirukkiṟēṉ. avarkaḷ ati aṅkīkarittatumallāmal, iṉṉoru parōṭā kāṉpareṉs kūṭum paṭcattil intavita ārāycci ceyvataṟku vitvāṉkaḷuṭaṉ oḻuṅku ceyvatākavum vākkaḷittārkaḷ. tāṅkaḷ itu viṣayattip paṟṟic ciramam eṭuttuk koḷḷakkūṭātā?
parōṭā kāṉpareṉsil eṉ maṉatil atikamāyp paṭṭatu taṅkaḷ upanniyācantāṉ. nāṉ eḻutiyirukkum “Psychology of Music” eṉṟa puttakattil itippaṟṟi vicēṣamāyc colliyirukkiṟēṉ. intap pustakam oru vārattukkuḷ anēkamāy veḷiyākum.
taṅkaḷuṭiya muyaṟcikaḷil kaṭavuḷ kūṭa iruntu avikaḷic citti peṟac ceyya vēṇṭum eṉṟu pirārttikkiṟēṉ.

parōṭāvil naṭanta āl-intiyā caṅkīta kāṉpareṉs.
ivviyācam tañci caṅkīta vityā makājaṉa caṅkattiṉ ēḻāvatu kāṉpareṉsil makā-rāca-rāca-ciṟi pañcāpakēca pākavatar avarkaḷāl paṭikkappaṭṭatu.
mēṟpaṭi talippeyar pūṇṭa caṅkamoṉṟik kūṭṭi parōṭā rājatāṉiyil his hiṉas makārājā kāykkavār avarkaḷ ātaraviṉ pēril 1916 ௵ mārccu mātam 20m tēti tuvakki 24m tēti variyum naṭipeṟṟu muṭivaṭinta viṣayam ellōrum aṟintatē.
itaṟkāka muṉṉatākavē makārājā avarkaḷ uttiraviṉpēril avvūr tivāṉ makā-rāca-rāca-ciṟi mātavarāv avarkaḷ, kāṉpareṉsukku sekriṭṭēri stāṉam vahitta makā-rāca-rāca-ciṟi cāmuvēl jōci avarkaḷik koṇṭu intiyā muḻumiyum viyāpittuḷḷa caṅkīta cāstira viṣayamāy aṟintuḷḷa palaril viyāsam eḻutum tiṟamiyi iṅkilīṣ pāṣi mūlamāy eḻuti aṉuppumpaṭit terivikkappaṭṭu antappaṭi kāṉpareṉs kūṭṭiya viparamum palar terintu koṇṭirukkalām.
itil teṉṉintiyāviṉ caṅkīta viṣayamāka itteṉṉāṭṭil viḷaṅkum cila paṇṭitarkaḷukku aṟivikkappaṭṭatu. atil tañci nakara vāci yāṉa rāv cāhēp, K. āpirakām paṇṭitar avarkaḷukkum aṟivikkap paṭṭatu.
௸tañci mānakaril cila varuṣakālamāy ēṟpaṭṭuḷḷa caṅkīta samājatti naṭatti atil cērnta talivarkaḷilum oruvarāṉa srī paṇṭitaravarkaḷ kēṭṭuk koḷḷutaluk kicintu oru kāṉpareṉsil piraciṭeṇṭu stāṉatti vahitta tivāṉ mātavarāyaravarkaḷ accamayam pēciyatil mahā rājākkaḷāl naṭattappaṭṭum naṭattakkūṭiyatumāṉa ip peruṅkāriyatti misṭar paṇṭitaravarkaḷ vahittuk koṇṭu naṭatti varuvatip paṟṟi nāṉ mikavum meccik koḷḷukiṟēṉeṉṟum ellā vittikaḷukkum uṟiviṭamāyirunta ittañci camastāṉattil, caṅkīta vittiyum kṣīṇittu viṭāmal ivvita caṅkamoṉṟi ēṟpaṭutti caṅkīta vitvāṉkaḷi ātarikkiṟa avaruṭiya ceyalāṉatu anta vittiyit tirumpa uyirppikkum eṉpatil cantēkamilli yeṉṟum caṅkaṅkaḷ palar kūṭi ceyya vēṇṭiya vēli eṉṟu teḷivāy viḷaṅkak kūṭiyateṉṟum caṅkītak kaḷañciyam eṉṟu pēr vāṅkiya ittañci mānakaril stāpikkap paṭavum ataṉāl iccaṅkam nilittiruntu nalla peyar vāṅkavum kaṭavuḷi nōkkip pirārttikkiṟēṉ eṉṟum nalla maṉatuṭaṉ collap paṭṭirukkiṟatu.
ākiyāl ittañci mānakariyum rāv cāhēp paṇṭitaravarkaḷi yum ñāpakattil vittiruppavarātalāl taṉatu rājyattil naṭattappaṭum ellā intiya caṅkīta kāṉpareṉsukku namatu paṇṭitaravarkaḷum avaciyam varavēṇṭumeṉṟu karuti avarkaḷiṭamiruntu makā-rāca-rāca-ciṟi paṇṭitar avarkaḷukku aḻippup pattiram aṉuppappaṭṭatu.
௸aḻippup pattirattip peṟṟa paṇṭitaravarkaḷ taṉatu muyaṟcikku oru palita kālamā yiruntālum taṉṉuṭiya cukariyattiṟkum tūratēca cañcārattukkum poruttamāyirukka vēṇṭit terivittatiṉ pēril vēṇṭiya aṉukūlaṅkaḷic ceytu koṭuppatu taṉatu kaṭamiyāyirukku meṉpati tivāṉ makā-rāca-rāca-ciṟi mātavarāyar avarkaḷ vaṟpuṟutti eḻutiyatiṉ pēril paṇṭitar avarkaḷum ataṟkiciya nērntatu.
parōṭā vijayam.
rāv cāhēp paṇṭitar avarkaḷukku aṉukūlamāyt taṉatu iraṇṭu kumārikaḷuṭaṉum maṟṟum cila caṅkīta vitvāṉkaḷuṭaṉum puṟappaṭat tīrmāṉittatil atil cilar taṅkaḷ taṅkaḷ cukariyak kuṟivāl varuvataṟkillātu pōṉapōtilum mukkiyamāy vēṇṭiya parivāraṅ kaḷuṭaṉ 1916-m ´ mārccu mātam 15-m tēti putaṉ kiḻami māli 5.30 maṇikkup puṟappaṭalāṉārkaḷ.
eḻumpūr sṭēṣaṉil iṟaṅki, seṉṟal sṭēṣaṉukku etirtta vāṭiyiluḷḷatum pārkku sṭēṣaṉukkuc camīpamāyuḷḷa oru paṅkaḷāvil taṅkiṉārkaḷ.
seṉṟal sṭēṣaṉil puṟappaṭukiṟa ṭelli ekspares pakal oru maṇikku mēl puṟappaṭuvatāl ataṟkuḷ vijayanakaram vīṇi vitvāṉ vēṅkaṭaramaṇatās avarkaḷum milāppūr vāciyāṉa A.P.kaṇēciyar avarkaḷum ēṟkaṉavē kuṟikkappaṭṭavarkaḷil cērntavarkaḷātalāl avviṭam vantu kalantu koṇṭārkaḷ.
piṟaku avaravarkaḷ taṅkaḷ vasatiyāṉa iṭaṅkaḷil snāṉa pōjaṉātikaḷi muṭittuk koṇṭu pakal 12 maṇikkē seṉṟal sṭēṣaṉil oṉṟu kūṭiṉārkaḷ.
accamayattil ceṉṉi pōlīs kamiṣaṉar tivāṉ pakatūr parāṅkuca nāyuṭukāru avarkaḷ sṭēṣaṉil vantiruntu puṟappaṭṭavarkaḷ ellōri yuṅ kaṇṭu kaḷittārkaḷ.
accamayam puṟappaṭṭavarkaḷ 12 pēr. itil paṇṭitaric cērnta iṉam ēḻu pērum avarkaḷi aṉucarittavarkaḷāy aintu pirāmaṇarkaḷum cērntiruntatik kavaṉikkumpoḻutu parakruti curaṅkaḷ ēḻum vikruti curaṅkaḷ aintum āka 12 curaṅkaḷ oṉṟu cēruvatāl tāṉ caṅkītam eṉṟa muḻuppeyari aṭikiṟatu eṉpati naṉkuṇarttiyatu pōlum.
oru stāyiyil puṟappaṭṭa paṉṉiruvarkaḷiyum yār yāri enta stāṉattil vippatu eṉṟu oru tōṟṟa muṇṭākumallavā? ataṟku oruvāṟu ippaṭi amittuk koḷḷalām.
kōmala niṣātattil missas paṇṭitaravarkaḷ, cuttamattimattil kaṉakavalli ammāḷ ṣaṭjastāṉattil paṇṭitaravarkaḷ, pañcama stāṉattil marakatavalli ammāḷ, tīvra riṣapattil turippāṇṭiyaṉ, kōmalakāntārattil cuntarapāṇṭiyaṉ, tīvra tivatattil taṅkiyā, antara kāntārattil vīṇi vēṅkaṭaramaṇatās, kākali niṣātattil eṉ.pi.cuppiramaṇiya aiyar avarkaḷ, pirati mattimattil pañcāpakēcapākavatar, kōmala riṣapattil V.pi.kaṇēciyar avarkaḷ, kōmala tivatattil cēṣa pākavatar. ippaṭiyāka ippaṉṉiruvarkaḷum avaravarkaḷ stāṉaṅkaḷil amarntārkaḷ. tivāṉ pakatūr makā-rāca-rāca-ciṟi parāṅkuca nāyuṭukāru avarkaḷ mikunta aṉpu pārāṭṭi ovvoruvarum cukkiyamāka uṭkārntati vicārittu ṣēmamāyum cantōṣamāyum pōy jeyatti aṭintu cukkiyamāy vantu cēra vāḻttukkaḷ kūṟi aṉpuḷḷa taṉatu malarnta mukattōṭu vaḻiyaṉuppiṉārkaḷ.
pūṉā sṭēṣaṉ vantu cērntatu. aṅkup paṇṭitaravarkaḷukkuc contamāyuḷḷa Rev. ēcuvaṭiyāṉ avarkaḷiṉ utaviyāl pirakiruti vikrutikaḷukkut taṉit taṉiyē avvūril peṅkaḷūriliruntu vantirukkum meṭikkal kālēj māṇavarkaḷil iraṇṭu pirāmaṇac ciṟuvarkaḷiṭam terivittu ௸ kālējiluḷḷa pirāmaṇa viṭutiyil vikrutikaḷukku aṉṉamaḷikkac ceytu pirakaruti curaṅkaḷit taṉatu jākiyil upacarittār.
௸ māṇavarkaḷ mikavum aṉpuṭaṉ pāṉattiṟku ṭīyum snāṉattiṟku vennīrum uṭaṉē pōjaṉamum tantu ati cīkkiramāy vaṇṭi vittu 91/2 maṇikkup puṟappaṭa vēṇṭiya vaṇṭikkut tavakkamaṉṉiyil 10 nimiṣam muṉṉatākavē varumpaṭik koṇṭu vantu viṭṭārkaḷ.
61/2 maṇi mutal 91/2 maṇi variyil ammāṇavarkaḷ iruvarum veku cuṟu cuṟuppāy naṭantu oru nimiṣamum iḷippāṟāmal upacaritta ivarkaḷatu upakāratti niṉikkum pōtu evvaḷavu jaṉmattilum maṟakka muṭiyāta viṣayam eṉṟu ivarkaḷiyum, ivarkaḷi ēviya pātiriyār avarkaḷiyum pativu ceyyappaṭṭatu. uṭaṉē vaṇṭiyum puṟappaṭṭatu.
cantirapakavāṉ nāṉ kāṭṭukiṟa kākṣiyik kāṇak kaṇṇayara vēṇṭām eṉṟār. pakal kaṇṭataṟku itu kaṇkākṣi yeṉṟu niṉittu viḻittiruntōm. rayil vaṇṭiyāṉatu oru iruṭṭaṟiyil pukuntu veḷip paṭṭatu. aṅkup pārttāl oru pakkam maliyiṉ uyarcciyum oru pakkam paḷḷattākkum iruppatum itaṉaṭuvē vaṇṭi pōvatum pārkka iccamayam mittiraṉ utaviyiruntāl, kaṇkākṣi vistāramāyirukkum. ākilum itu kaṇ paṭittavarkaḷukku vittitāṉ pōṉṟu kaḷiyuṟṟōm. ivvāṟu pala kukikaḷil vaṇṭi piravēcittup pōkumpōtu karmapācattiṉāl iḻukkap paṭum jīvaṉ karppavācamum, veḷiyēṟuvatumāṉa ceykipōl tōṟṟiyatu. piṟaku pampāy sṭēṣaṉik kaṇṭōm. viyappuṟṟu tikittōm. vikṭōriyā eṉṉum vaṇṭiyil koñca tūram māṭa māḷikiyuḷḷa vītikaḷiṉ vaḻiyē ceṉṟu maṟṟōr sṭēṣaṉil parōṭāvukkuc cellum vaṇṭiyil amarntōm. kāli 7 maṇikku vaṇṭi puṟappaṭṭatu. 9 maṇi variyil pampāyp paṭṭaṇattit tāṇṭiyatākat teriyavilli. piṟaku oru sṭēṣaṉil varumpoḻutu nāṅkaḷ inta vaṇṭiyil puṟappaṭṭu varuvati parōṭā tivāṉ makā-rāca-rāca-ciṟi mātavarāyar avarkaḷukku oru tanti mūlamāyt terivittuk koḷḷappaṭṭatu. aṉṟu māli aintu maṇi variyil mutal nāḷippōl paḻam, pāltāṉ ākāram.
5 maṇikku parōṭā sṭēṣaṉ vantapōtu tivāṉ makā-rāca-rāca-ciṟi mātavarāyar avarkaḷāl aṉuppappaṭṭa araṇmaṉi utyōkastarkaḷum pala vēlikkārarkaḷumāṉa anēkar kūṭiyiruntārkaḷ. sapta curam pōluḷḷa vārattil ēḻāvatu vāramāṉa stira vārattil vikruti curam pōluḷḷa 5 maṇi vēḷiyil pirakiruti vikruti pētaṅkaḷāl pala irākaṅkaḷ uṇṭākiṉṟaṉa eṉpatik kāṭṭuvatupōl anēka jaṉaṅkaḷ rāv cāhēp paṇṭitar avarkaḷiṭam anurākattōṭu ceṉṟu ātaravuṭaṉ iṉimiyāy ki īntu upacarittu ūṭāṭi ellōrum ēṟṟamuṭaṉ aikkiya māy oṟṟumippaṭṭu ōtiya seḷajaṉyam atik kaṇṭu kaḷiyātārik kāṇakkiṭittōmilli.
uṭaṉē mōṭṭār kārilum iraṭṭippuravi vaṇṭiyilum oṟṟik kutiri pīṭṭaṉilumceṉṟu intiyaṉ kesṭu havus eṉṟa māṭakūṭam tōpput turavukaḷaṭaṅkiya ōr perutta viṭutiyil, cukariyamāy vācam ceyya iṭamaḷittu utaviṉārkaḷ.
vācastala vicēṭam.
oru pakkattil pirāmāṇarkaḷukkup pōjaṉam tayārākiṟatu. maṟṟōr pakkattil vennīr kāyntu koṇṭu cīkkiram snāṉam ceyyuṅkaḷ eṉṟu tūṇṭukiṟatu. maṟṟōr aṟiyil paḻamum, pālum piskōttum nāṅkaḷ iṅku vacikkiṟōm nīṅkaḷ niṉittapōtu utavuvōm eṉṟaṉa. miṉcāra viḷakkukaḷ iṭi iṭiyē paḻaṅkaḷ pōl toṅki, nāṅkaḷ illāta iṭam irāveṉṟaṉa. kāṟṟillāviṭattil kāṟṟāṭi nāṉ upacarippēṉ eṉkiṟatu. ippaṭiyāka niṉittati aṉupavikkak koṭukkum navaniti pōlum āvali aṭakkum tēvalōkampōlum viḷaṅki maṉa makiḻcciyik koṭuttatāl snāṉam, tiyāṉam, pūji, pōjaṉam ivikaḷi vaḻuvaṟa naṭatti tūratēcap pirayāṇaciramatti iḷippāṟi iruntu veṉṟōm.
maṟunāḷ ātivāram tōṉṟiyatu. aṉṟu kāli tivāṉ makā-rāca-rāca-ciṟi mātava rāyar avarkaḷum maṟṟa upasātakarkaḷuṭaṉ tōṉṟi vēṇṭiya cukariyaṅkaḷip paṇṭitar avarkaḷiṭam vicārittu iruppatupōka illātataṟku ēviṉārkaḷ.
maṟunāḷ mutal naṭakkappōkum kāṉpareṉsukku vanta pala tēcattavarkaḷum taṅkuvataṟku anēka jākikaḷ amarttap paṭṭirunta pōtilum itutāṉ taṅkaḷukku cukariyamāyuḷḷatu eṉṟum aṟivittār.
kāṉpareṉs kāla aṭṭavaṇiyil (programme) mutalāvatāṉa teyva vaṇakkatti rāv cāhēp paṇṭitar avarkaḷiṉ kumārikaḷāl stōt tirikkappaṭum eṉṟu eḻutappaṭṭiruntapaṭiyāl ataṟkuriya stōttirap pāṭalkaḷil etippāṭalām eṉṟu yōcittu tivāṉ makā-rāca-rāca-ciṟi mātavarāyar avarkaḷum makā-rāca-rāca-ciṟi pātkaṇṭē avarkaḷum, kāṉpareṉs piraciṭeṇṭ stāṉatti vakikka irukkum makā-rāca-rāca-ciṟi navāp ālikkāṉ avarkaḷum, tiyākarājacuvāmi kīrttaṉaṅkaḷil mukkiyamā yuḷḷatum, urukkamāyuḷḷatum - kālattiṟkēṟṟatum hintustāṉ irākaṅkaḷil cērātatāyumuḷḷa aṭāṉā tēvakāntāri eṉṟu collap paṭum irākaṅkaḷiluḷḷa iraṇṭu kīrttaṉikaḷip pāṭat tīrmāṉittārkaḷ.
aṉṟu māli tivāṉ makā-rāca-rāca-ciṟi mātavarāyar avarkaḷ kirukattil ōr cap kamiṭṭi mīṟṟiṅ kūṭṭappaṭṭu ovvoru viyācattiṟkum kuṟippiṭṭirukkum kālattiṟku mēṟpaṭṭuk koñcam kāla aḷavit tara vēṇṭumeṉṟu makā-rāca-rāca-ciṟi harinākapūṣaṇamiyar avarkaḷ mutalāṉa cilar vātāṭik kēṭṭuk koṇṭārkaḷ. kaṭiciyāka srī āpirakām paṇṭitar avarkaḷāl ellā viyācaṅkaḷum purōkirāmil kaṇṭapaṭiyē kuṟitta kālattiṟkuḷ vācikkappaṭa vēṇṭumeṉṟum ataṟkēṟṟa vitamāy mukkiyamāṉa iṭaṅkaḷi māttiram vācittu muṭikka vēṇṭumeṉṟum nām nāḷiya tiṉam naṭakka vēṇṭiya kāriyaṅkaḷi yōcikka vēṇṭumeṉṟum collappaṭṭu capiyōr yāvarālum aṅkīkarikkappaṭṭatu.
uṭaṉē tivāṉ makā-rāca-rāca-ciṟi mātavarāyaravarkaḷāl paṇṭitar avarkaḷōṭu paṇṭitar avarkaḷiṉ kuḻantikaḷ evvitamāṉa cukariyat tōṭu uṭkārntu pāṭavēṇṭumō avvitam amiyap peṟumpaṭi kāṉpareṉs hālil cīrtiruttam ceyyappaṭṭatu. atupōla maṟu nāḷ cōmavārattaṉṟu kāṉpareṉsukku vantirukkum vitvāṉkaḷum viyācakarkaḷum, pōṣakarkaḷum, ātarippōrkaḷumāṉa makājaṉaṅkaḷ kāli 5 maṇi mutalākavē snāṉa pāṉātikaḷic ceytu koṇṭu avaravarkaḷ antastukkuriya iṭaṅkaḷil amarntārkaḷ. kaṭiciyāka tivāṉ makā-rāca-rāca-ciṟi mātavarāyar avarkaḷum capiyirukka vēṇṭiya amippu cariyā yuḷḷatā eṉṟu nitāṉittu viṭṭu carvamakājaṉaṅkaḷuṭaṉ makārājā avarkaḷiṉ varaviṟku etirpārttuk koṇṭiruntārkaḷ. koñca nāḻikik kellām makārājā avarkaḷ varukiṟārkaḷeṉṟa aṟikuṟi kāṇappaṭṭatu.
carva jaṉaṅkaḷum āvaluṭaṉ kavaṉitta camayattil makārāṇi camētarāy makārājā avarkaḷ pracaṉṉamāṉatik kaṇṭa carva jaṉaṅkaḷum eḻuntu niṉṟu mariyāti ceyya makārājā avarkaḷum ellōriyum kavaṉittu taṉatu stāṉatti vahittār. accamayam ōr nimiṣam variyil niccaptamum atiliruntu ōr piraṇava nātamum atit toṭarntu teyva vaṇakkamum paṇṭitar avarkaḷiṉ kuḻantikaḷāl pāṭappaṭṭa poḻutu carva jaṉaṅkaḷiṉ maṉatum acivaṟṟu āṉantattiṉāl muḻukap paṭṭu viṭṭatu. uṭaṉē rāja kītamum pāṭappaṭṭatu. piṟaku capi naṭuvil tivāṉ mātavarāyaravarkaḷ eḻuntu kāṉpareṉsiṉ ārampa piracaṅkam ceytu kāṉpareṉsi etōktamākat tuvakka makārājā avarkaḷiṉ anumatiyip pirārttittārkaḷ. uṭaṉē carva jaṉaṅkaḷil karakōṣa mattiyil makārājā avarkaḷ eḻuntu niṉṟu carva vittikaḷilum ciṟantatāṉa iccaṅkīta vittiyi paḷḷiyil paṭikkum āṇkaḷ, peṇkaḷ mutalāy ellōrum eḷitil aṟintu pāṭumpaṭi noṭṭēṣaṉ mūlamāka oḻuṅkupaṭutti veḷippaṭuttuvataṟku ippoḻutu kūṭṭappaṭṭa iccaṅka māṉatu mikunta ātaravaḷikkum eṉṟu nampukiṟēṉ eṉṟu collik kāṉpareṉsit tiṟantu vittār.
uṭaṉē navāp ālikkāṉ avarkaḷip piraciṭeṇṭ stāṉatti vahikkumpaṭi ellōrum kōri āmōtikkappaṭṭu avarum anta stāṉatti vahittār. caṅkīta cāstiratti ārāycci ceytu ataṉ rakaciyaṅkaḷi nūṉmukamāy ēṟkaṉavē veḷippaṭuttiyirukkiṉṟa makā-rāca-rāca-ciṟi pātkaṇṭē avarkaḷ caṅkīta cāstirattil vaṭamoḻiyiṉāl kūṟappaṭum kirantaṅkaḷiṉ ātāraṅkaḷik koṇṭu tvāvimcati curutiyiṉ rakaciyatti oruvāṟu veḷiyiṭṭup pēciṉār. ippaṭiyāka avaravarkaḷ taṅkaḷ taṅkaḷ viyācaṅkaḷik kāla aṭṭavaṇiyiṉ pirakāram paṭittu vantārkaḷ.
௸ kāṉpareṉs ārampattil rāv cāhēp paṇṭitar avarkaḷiṉ puttirikaḷ cupākkiyavati marakatavalliyammāḷum, cupākkiyavati kaṉakavalli ammāḷum teyva vaṇakkamāka mutalāvatu pāṭappeṟṟatu nammellōrum cantōṣikkappaṭum viṣayam. mēlum avvitamākavē capi ārampikkum ovvoru tiṉattilum ivarkaḷiyē pāṭac ceyya ellōruṭiya kōrikkiyum uṇṭāki atupōl naṭantēṟiyatum itteṉṉāṭṭuc caṅkītattiṟkum perumiyāṉatāl ituvum mikunta cantōṣattiṟkuk kāraṇam.
kāṉpareṉsil naṭanta viṣayaṅkaḷ iṅkilīṣ pāṣiyil naṭantatāl viparamāka aṟintu koḷḷa muṭiyavilli. ākilum ac capiyiṉ kuṟippukaḷāl oruvāṟu aṟintu koḷḷakkūṭiyatāka iruntatu. accapiyil mikunta celvākki aṭintirunta ōr makamatiya turicāṇi Atiya Begum Fyzee Rahimin avarkaḷmaṟṟoruvaruṭaṉ pēcikkoṇṭiruntatil collappaṭṭati pakkattilirunta eṉṉāl kēṭkappaṭṭapōtu caṅkīta viṣayam vātippatilum caṇṭiyiṭuvatilum eṉṉa pirayōjaṉam. paṇṭitar avarkaḷiṉ kumarikaḷik koñcam pāṭac coṉṉālum cukamākak kēṭkalām. poḻutō virutāvākap pōkiṟatu. us eṉṟu peru mūccu viṭṭu oruvariṭam coṉṉati nāṉ kēṭṭēṉ. tavira potu jaṉaṅkaḷ aṭintirunta uṟcākak kuṟivik koṇṭum stūlamāka kāṉpa reṉsil vācikkappaṭum viyācaṅkaḷ ivarkaḷukku sāramāka irukka villiyō eṉṟu nāṉ niṉikka nērntatu. ippaṭiyāka iraṇṭu nāḷ mīṭṭiṅ naṭantēṟiyatu. piṟaku mūṉṟāvatu nāḷil paṇṭitar avarkaḷālum viyācam vācikkappaṭṭatu. inta viyācattiṟku 3 maṇi nēram variyil kāla variyiruntatāl maṟṟavarkaḷik kāṭṭilum nīṇṭakāla aḷavip peṟṟirunta inta viyācattiṟku ēṟkaṉavē vācikkappaṭṭa viyācaṅkaḷiṉ kālattiṉ aḷavi viyācaṅkaḷukkut takkapaṭi kuṟippiṭṭirunta kālatti liruntu 5 nimiṣam 10 nimiṣam kuṟittu muṭikkumpaṭi tūṇṭik koṇṭu vanta piraciṭeṇṭ navāp ālikkāṉ avarkaḷ 3 maṇi nērattip peṟṟirukkum namatu paṇṭitar avarkaḷiṉ viyācattiyum avvāṟu kuṟikkac ceyvārō eṉṟa kavali mēlāṭik koṇṭiruntatu. āṉāl piraciṭeṇṭ stāṉatti vahittuḷḷa navāp ālikkāṉ avarkaḷiṉ tiṟamiyi yōjikkumpōtu ³yār caṅkīta viṟpaṉṉar, ārmōṉiyam vācippatil oru kiyiṉāl tāḷam pōṭṭuk koṇṭu maṟṟoru kiyiṉāl vācikkiṟa paḻakkatti iraṇṭu kikaḷukkum paḻakki vittiruppavar, susvaramāyp pāṭakkūṭiya caktiyuḷḷavar, perutta jamīṉtār, nalla kuṇamuḷḷavar eṉṟu viḷaṅkiyatik koṇṭu ari maṇi nēram atikamāka naṭantiruppatikkūṭa maṟantu viṣayattiṉ cārattil kavaṉam celuttiyirukkiṟār eṉṟu teriya vantatu.
rāvcāhēp paṇṭitar avarkaḷiṉ viyācatti avaratu marumakaṉ makā-rāca-rāca-ciṟiturippāṇṭi avarkaḷālum makā-rāca-rāca-ciṟi N.P.cuppiramaṇiya aiyar avarkaḷālum vācikkappaṭṭa uṭaṉē maṟṟa viṣayaṅkaḷiyum capiyōrukku eṭuttuc colla paṇṭitar avarkaḷ eḻuntu tāṉ pēcuvatu tamiḻppāṣiyāṉatāl carvajaṉaṅkaḷum terintu koḷḷa makā-rāca-rāca-ciṟi N.P. cuppiramaṇiya aiyar avarkaḷum piṟaku ceṉṉi vāciyāṉa C.R.cīṉivāsa aiyaṅkār avarkaḷum tivipāṣikaḷā yiruntu iṅkilīṣil moḻi peyarttut terivittārkaḷ. itil paṇṭitar avarkaḷ tamiḻp pāṣiyiluḷḷa kirantaṅkaḷil nūlmuṟiyuṭaṉ colli yirukkiṟa muṟippaṭi āyappāli, vaṭṭappāli, tirikōṇappāli, caturap pāli eṉṟa pirivil 12, 24, 48, 96 vakikaḷākap pāṭappaṭṭum avvāṟē vīṇiyiṉ stāṉaṅkaḷ pirikkappaṭṭu ippōtuḷḷa 12 iṭaṅkaḷiṉiṉṟum oru oru iṭiveḷikaḷilum ariyākavum, kālākavum, arikkālākavum, vīcamākavum itu aṉupavattiliruppatākavum terivittār. piṟaku “mukkiyamā yuḷḷa 24 stāṉaṅkaḷi ivvita rakaciyattic cilar uṇarāmalum uṇarntavarkaḷiṟ cilar viḷakkic collat teriyāmal mayaṅki 22 stāṉattuṭaṉ niṉṟuviṭṭārkaḷ. ivikaḷippaṟṟi nāṉ pēcum poḻu tellām eṉṉiccilar caṅkītattiṉ nuṭpatti nāṉaṟiyavilli eṉṟum eṉṉip pittiyakkāraṉeṉṟum collat talippaṭṭārkaḷ. āṉālum eṉatu peṇṇāṉa marakatavalli ammāḷiṉ utaviyik koṇṭu kāṉattil viḷaṅkum ovvoru curuti stāṉaṅkaḷiyum yāṉ kavaṉittu aṉupava kītattiṟkum tamiḻ nūl ātāraṅkaḷukkum ottumiyāyuḷḷa inta irakaciyatti eṉṉāl aṭakki viṭa muṭiyātu. itaṟkāka eṉṉāl ōr nūleḻuti vantu koṇṭirukkiṟatu. inta irakaciya muṟikaḷi eṉ piḷḷikaḷukkup paṭittuk koṭukkum upāttiyāyarāy ippoḻutu piṭil vācitta makā-rāca-rāca-ciṟi pañcāpakēca pākavatarāṉa ivarukkum nāṉ collavilli. avarum 22 curutiyiyē nampikkoṇṭiruppavar. uṅkaḷōṭu avarum oruvarāy ippoḻututāṉ terintu koḷḷap pōkiṟār.” eṉkiṟavariyil coṉṉārkaḷ. intac camayam capiyiluḷḷa ellōrum eṉṉi orē kālattil pārkkum pākkiyatti aṭintēṉ. āṉāl nāṉ veṭkatti aṭiyavēṇṭiyatirukkumeṉṟu cilar niṉikka nērntālum nāṉ makiḻcciyuḷḷavaṉākavē iruntēṉ. ēṉeṉṟāl caṅkītam, camuttira rūpamāyuḷḷapōtu, oruvaṉ collakkūṭiya svalpamākat tāṉ irukkum; itaṉāl “kaṟṟatu kimmaṇṇaḷavu, kallātatulakaḷavu” eṉṟa vākkiyattiyē niṉippil vittirukkiṟa eṉakku veṭkattit taravilli. tavira namatu māṇākkarkaḷukkāvatu inta irakaciyam terintirukkiṟatallavā eṉṟa makiḻcciyum tantatu.
itaṉ piṟaku paṇṭitaravarkaḷ tāṉ kuṟippiṭṭu vittirukkiṟa curuti stāṉaṅkaḷil cilavaṟṟi inta irākaṅkaḷil inta curuti stāṉaṅkaḷ vantu koṇṭirukkiṉṟaṉa eṉpati eṉṉāl colli vittirukkiṟa kīrttaṉaṅkaḷ mūlamāy taṉatu peṇkaḷik koṇṭu pāṭacceytu kāṭṭiṉārkaḷ. itil (rāma pāṇatrāṉa) eṉkiṟa sāvēri, irākattil uḷḷa srī tiyākarāja cuvāmikaḷiṉ kīrttaṉattil (rā) eṉkiṟa akṣaratti iḻuttu (ma) eṉkiṟa akṣarattic colluvataṟku muṉṉuḷḷa cutta riṣapa stāṉattil niṟkumpōtu makā-rāca-rāca-ciṟi harinākapūṣaṇamiyar eṉṟa caṅkīta vitvāṉ anta iṭatti iṉṉum kuṟittup piṭikka vēṇṭu meṉṟu tāṉ pāṭikkāṭṭumpōtu ṣaṭja curattiṉāl iḻukkappaṭṭu viṭṭār. ivaratu vātatti makā-rāca-rāca-ciṟi ciṭṭipāpu nāyuṭu eṉpavar camātāṉañ ceytār. itaṉ piṟaku vīṇiyiluḷḷa 24 stāṉaṅkaḷiyum paṭittu varicik kiramamāyum pāṭikkāṭṭappaṭṭatu. iti iraṇṭu taṭavi maṟupaṭi tirumpic coṉṉapōtum tanti nātattiṟkum cārīrattiṟkum oṟṟumiyā yiruntatōṭu koñcamēṉum vittiyācamillāmal iruntati ellōrum kaṇṭu āccariyappaṭṭārkaḷ.
inta camayattil intustāṉ caṅkītam pāṭuvatil kiyāti peṟṟavarum turupat vitvāṉum utayappūr sākruṭīṉ eṉpavar inta curuti varicikaḷit tāṉum camīpattil uṭkārntu vīṇiyuṭaṉ pāṭippārttār. āṉāl mēru mutal aḷavāyuḷḷa 24vatu meṭṭil varavum ṣaṭjastāṉam kiṭittu viṭṭatāka niṉittu niṉṟuviṭṭār. ākilum curuti ñāṉattil tērntavareṉpatil taṭiyilli. ippaṭiyāka varicikkiramamāy intac curuti stāṉaṅkaḷip paṭittuk kāṭṭum poḻutu peṇpiḷḷikaḷā yiruntapōtilum tiriyattuṭaṉum uṟcākattuṭaṉum collappaṭṭu oṟṟumiyāyiruntati niṉittāl vāstavamāy paṇṭitar avarkaḷukku īcaṉuṭiya aruḷ utaviyum cērntirukkiṟatākat tīrmāṉittēṉ. ippaṭiyāka curuti stāṉaṅkaḷic capimattiyil nirūpittu vāttiyattuṭaṉ taṉittaṉiyākavum toṭarcciyāyum aṉupavattiluḷḷatāyum eṭuttuk kāṭṭiyavar namatu paṇṭitaravarkaḷtāṉ; maṟṟavarkaḷ ippaṭi rūpittukkāṭṭa muṉvaravilli. itaṉ pēril kaṉam paṇṭitar avarkaḷ muṭivāka oru viññāpaṉamum ceytu koṇṭārkaḷ. atāvatu “ippōtu nāṉ eṭuttuk kāṭṭiya muṟiyi āṣēpikka iṣṭamuḷḷavarkaḷ kēṭṭāl nāṉ camātāṉam collat tayārāyirukkiṟēṉ” eṉṟum kēṭṭuk koṇṭārkaḷ. appōtu āṣēpikka oruvarum muṉvaravilli. makā-rāca-rāca-ciṟi tivāṉ mātavarāv avarkaḷum parama cantōṣatti aṭintiruntārkaḷ. itaṉāl maṟunāḷ hishiṉas makārājā avarkaḷ tamatu camūkattil naṭatta ēṟpāṭu ceytiruntārkaḷ. antappaṭi mukkiyamāṉa cilaruṭaṉ vīṇiyil mikunta pāṇṭittiyamuḷḷa tamatu makārāṇi avarkaḷuṭaṉ taṉimiyāka iruntu kuḻantikaḷiṉ kāṉattik kēṭṭatuṭaṉ rāvcāhēp paṇṭitaravarkaḷ makā-rāca-rāca-ciṟi N.P.cuppiramaṇiya aiyar avarkaḷ mūlamāka iṅkilīṣil terivikkumpaṭi ceytu caṅkīta cāstirattiṉ perumiyiyum, teṉṉintiyāvil purātaṉamāy cīrtiruttattuṭaṉ naṭipeṟṟu varuvatiyum atil tamiḻ nūlil collappaṭṭirukkiṟa pāli viparaṅkaḷiyum ataṉāl curuti stāṉaṅkaḷ teḷivāy nirṇayamākiṟa teṉṟum ataṟku utaviyāka vīṇiyum iṉṉa ilakṣaṇattuṭaṉ amikkappaṭa vēṇṭumeṉpatiyum vicitamāyum- curukkamāyum terivittārkaḷ. makā-rāca-rāca-ciṟi mātavarāyar avarkaḷum paṇṭitar avarkaḷippaṟṟi ovvoru viṣayattilum nuṭpamāṉa ārāycci ceyyumpōtu evvaḷavu pirayāci yiruntālum piṉvāṅkupavar alla eṉṟum collumpōtu makārājā avarkaḷ vekuvāka cantōṣit tārkaḷ. piṟaku kāṉpareṉsil naṭantatupōl curuti stāṉa viparaṅkaḷum kāṇpikkappaṭṭaṉa. appōtu makārājā avarkaḷ cantōṣittu paṇṭitar avarkaḷiṉ ārāyccikku meccikkoṇṭu pukaḻntārkaḷ.
itil kāṉpareṉs naṭanta kālattil kuḻantikaḷāl paṭikkappaṭṭa kakaṉakutūkalam eṉṟa irākattiluḷḷa rakuvamca ca&tāmaputicantara eṉṟa kīrttaṉattik kēṭṭa pyāṇṭ māsṭar Mr.kucanaṉaṭaḷi veku cantōṣap paṭṭu iti noṭṭēṣaṉil kuṟittuk koṭukkumpaṭi kēṭṭār. atu pōlavē cupākkiyavati marakatavalli ammāḷāl aṭiyāḷattuṭaṉ kuṟittuk koṭukkappaṭṭatu. ati pyāṇṭ māsṭar taṉatu pḷūṭ eṉṟa vāttiyattil ūti makiḻntu koṇṭu evvaḷavu kīrttaṉiyāṉālum tēviyirukkumeṉṟu kēṭṭuk koṇṭār.
maṟṟōr nāḷ makā-rāca-rāca-ciṟi tivāṉ mātavarāyar avarkaḷ paṅkaḷāvil oru mīṭṭiṅ kūṭiyapōtu kuḻantikaḷiṉ kāṉam naṭantatu. aṉṟu atika nēram kiṭittirunta paṭiyāl arumiyāṉa kīrttaṉaṅkaḷ pāṭappaṭṭapōtu ellōrum vicēṣa cantōṣatti aṭintārkaḷ. mēṟ colliya pyāṇṭmāsṭarum cantōṣappaṭṭār. aṉṟiya tiṉattilum kāṉpareṉsil naṭantapaṭi 24 curuti stāṉaṅkaḷiyum pāṭik kāṇpikka nērntapōtu mēṟpaṭi piyāṇṭ māsṭar turiyavarkaḷ vīṇiyiṉ mēl niṣātastāṉam kuṟivāyiruppatupōl niṉittu āṭcēpittār. maṟṟavarkaḷ cariyāyiruppatāy vātittārkaḷ. paṇṭitar avarkaḷum cariyā yuḷḷa teṉṟu terivittārkaḷ. appōtu turiyavarkaḷ palastāyikaḷil cañcāram ceyyum anēka vāttiyaṅkaḷ vācikkappaṭum kālattil ētāvatu oṉṟu ēṟṟattāḻvaṭintāl atik kaṇṭupiṭikkum tīraṉ nāṉ eṉpati nīṅkaḷ nampa vēṇṭumeṉṟu āṅkilattil coṉṉa avvārttiyi makā-rāca-rāca-ciṟi tivāṉ avarkaḷ tamiḻil eṭutturittārkaḷ. atikkēṭṭa paṇṭitaravarkaḷ vāyiṉāl 12 curuti ūtappaṭukiṟa perutta nātattik kaṇṭupiṭikkum tiṟami vāyntavarkaḷukku intiya caṅkītattil varum nuṭpa curaṅkaḷik kaṇṭupiṭikka muṭiyātu eṉṟu viṭiyaḷittārkaḷ. piṟaku vijaya nakaram vīṇi vitvāṉ vēṅkaṭaramaṇatās avarkaḷiṉ vīṇiyiyum cērttuppārtta kālattil turiyavarkaḷukkum oppuk koṇṭuviṭa nērntu viṭṭatu.
piṟaku tañci caṅkīta samājattil pirati kāṉpareṉsukku vantirunta varum, lakṣaṇalakṣiya vitvāṉum pūvaṉūrvāciyumāṉa makā-rāca-rāca-ciṟi piratāpa rāmacāmi pākavatar avarkaḷum ceṉṉi ṭākṭar nañcuṇṭarāv avarkaḷ mūlamāy aḻippup pattiram peṟṟu parōṭā kāṉpareṉsukku ōr memparāyum tākkal ceytu koṇṭa ³ pākavatar accamayam iruntavarātalāl avaratu apippirāyam ētāvatu pētamaṭintirukkiṟatā veṉṟu terintu koḷḷa paṇṭitar avarkaḷ pākavatar avarkaḷip pārttu “vīṇiyiṉ curutikaḷik kavaṉittīrkaḷā” eṉṟār. pākavatar vīṇi naṉṟā yirukkiṟatākac coṉṉār. “curuti viṣayattit terintu koṇṭīrkaḷā” eṉṟu paṇṭitar avarkaḷāl kēṭkappaṭṭatu. ataṟkup pākavatar avarkaḷ “ūrppōyp pēcikkoḷvōm” eṉṟār. appōtu tivāṉ makā-rāca-rāca-ciṟi mātavarāyar avarkaḷ ētāvatu carcci ceyvatāṉāl ippoḻutē ceyyalām eṉṟārkaḷ. ataṟkuḷ pākavatar 24 curutikku ātāram kiṭikka villi eṉṟār. paṇṭitar avarkaḷ tamiḻ nūlil collappaṭṭirukkiṟa teṉṟārkaḷ.
piṟaku pākavatar tamiḻ nūlil caṅkītattip paṟṟi virivākac colli yirukkiṟa cilappatikārattil ivviṣayam kāṇappaṭavilli eṉṟārkaḷ. paṇṭitar avarkaḷ nūl maṟippi vilakki āḻntu kavaṉittāl aṟiyak kūṭum eṉṟārkaḷ. iṉṉum koñcam campāṣaṇi naṭantatu. piṟaku pākavatar muṉatti vakittār.
itaṉ piṟaku ellōriṭamum uttiravu peṟṟuk koṇṭu parōṭāvi viṭṭup puṟappaṭṭu pampāy vantu cērnta aṉṟu oru lekcar hālil paṇṭitar avarkaḷiṉ upanniyācam eṉ.pi.cuppiramaṇiya aiyar iṅkilīṣ moḻi peyarppuṭaṉ naṭantatu. paṇṭitar avarkaḷiṉ puttirikaḷ kāṉamum naṭantu vantirunta kiṟistuva matappaṟṟuḷḷa ellōrum cantōṣa maṭintārkaḷ. piṟaku aṅkiruntu puṟappaṭṭu ceṉṉikku vantu cēra tivāṉ pakatūr makā-rāca-rāca-ciṟi parāṅkuca nāyuṭukāru avarkaḷ paṅkaḷāvil upacarikkappaṭṭu mūṉṟu nāḷ taṅka nērntatu. anēka vitvāṉkaḷum tamiḻp paṇṭitarkaḷum paṇṭitar avarkaḷik kaṇṭu kaḷittu parōṭā vijaya vartta māṉaṅkaḷi aṟintapōtu ellōrum koṇṭāṭiṉārkaḷ.

Miraj,
8th August 1916
DEAR RAO SAHIB PANDITHER,
I am in receipt of your so-called ‘refutation.’
I made no reply to criticisms appearing in the Madras Mail as the question between us is not one in which the public is sufficiently well-informed for discussion in such a paper to be profitable.
1. In the pamphlet you have now printed you do not quote the remarks which you criticize. Most readers will be in the dark as to what the discussion is about.
2. Your method of replying to my criticism is to restate your own case and to call for a test.
3. You cannot seriously entertin the belief that any test of any value whatever was made at Baroda.
4. I took notes then of the dicta of Jakroddin Khan. On my return to Dharwar, I will hunt them up and let you see what absurdities they lead to. As far as the Indian Harmonium was concerned the test was a farce.
5. The remarks you quote from the Bombay Chronicle favour your view of the matter much less than they do mine. They amount to this that the Kafi scale is as follows :
	Sa 	Ri 	Ga 	Ma 	Pa 	Dha 	Ni 	Sa.
	9/8 	16/15 	10/9 	9/8 	9/8 	16/15 	10/9
According to you it should be :-
	Sa 	Ri 	Ga 	Ma 	Pa 	Dha 	Ni 	Sa.
	21/6 	21/12 	21/6 	21/6 	21/6 	21/12 	21/6
According to my experience it is
	Sa 	Ri 	Ga 	Ma 	Pa 	Dha 	Ni 	Sa.
	10/9 	16/15 	9/8 	9/8 	10/9 	16/15 	9/8
6. Kindly ask yourself how many of the ‘experts’ who attended the Conference had undergone the preliminary trining with the help of a specially tuned instrument necessary to enable their ears to recognize the difference between the tempered tone, the major tone, the minor tone and other simple harmonic intervals. Several members of the Conference spoke in familiar terms of intervals represented by simple ratios such as 9/8, 10/9, 5/4, 6/5. How many of them could recognize these intervals with certinty if they heard them or could clim to be able to distinguish any of them from intervals tempered or otherwise which approximate to them?
7. To come to the singing of your dughters which seems to you a vindication of your theories.
8. I would like to ask why you discard the drone which I have always found associated with Indian music? Let them sing to a drone of two tamburas. You will find in Raga Kedargavla and in Shankarabharanam they will sing not your ga but the ga which is 5/4 of shadj. In Raga Hanumantodi they will sing the dha which is 8/5 of Shadj; in raga Natabhiravi, they will sing the ga which is 6/5 of shadj. To put the matter more briefly they will sing real music.
9. Artificial music is an abomination.
10. I venture to prophesy that it will be discarded in Europe before many centuries have passed. In Europe many factors combined to reconcile musicians to its obvious faults and deficiencies. I have endeavoured to treat the subjects in an article in the September to November 1915 numbers of Indian Education (Longmans Green and Co., Hornby Road, Bombay.) That article might prove of interest to you.
11. To resume, if you make inquiries you will find that an unaccompanied singer or violinist has great difficulty in rendering artificial intervals correctly, your dughters are no exception.
12. When they sing to your special bina they sing the harsh tones of temperament.
13. When they sing with the violin both they and the violinist insensibly drift away into other scales.
14. The scale they tend most towards is the ditonal scale, generally described as the scale of Pythagoras.
Some day I shall write an article on this scale. Books like Blaserna’s ‘Theory of Sound’ have completely misled the ordinary reader as to the part it has played in the history of music. The view I hold is that it never formed the basis of musical art until temperament led to its use. In ancient Greece it was what we might term the Shuddh scale in one method of tuning the Kithara; on account of its convenience for the purpose it became the nucleus of the instrumental notation. The Kithara was furnished with a device for tightening the strings by any interval up to a semitone whatever scale was required was obtined by means of this device, just as the binkar gets any intervals not given by the frets by pressing heavily on the wire or pulling it to one side and so increasing the tension. As far as one can tell, the ditonal scale was never used in any old Greek music; that is to say there was no Raga founded on the Shuddh notes of Pythagorean tuning. In the time of the Byzantine Empire theorists who did not know what they were talking about, added the Pythagorean ratios to scale which were not Pythagorean, just as pandits of modern India who have not practical knowledge of just intervals talk glibly of the 3033/4 ga and 405 dha and so on.
15. I am of opinion that your dughters’ singing, although much admired and commended by Jakroddin and others, is not a test in any sense of the word.
I would like to make clear my position with regard to your equal division of the octave.
16. Indian music, in my opinion, is now, in its best form, and ever was real music.
17. Any system of musical art founded on the use of a drone must be built up from true concord.
18. True concord to the primitive philosopher is a knot impossible to unravel. It is not until the philosopher begins to experiment with string-lengths that he has any notion of the way to set to work.
19. This however, does not dunt him. We find him in ancient India and in ancient Greece, (probably he was busy weaving phantasies of the same kind in Egypt, Assyria, and China), building up a theory of sound, worthless becuse it was not submitted to any scientific test, which explined all scales on the basis of an equal division of the octave. All the philosophers attacked the problem in the same way. They thought there must be some unit interval just as one uses the span or cubit as a unit of length. The only unit which suggested itself was the smallest perceptible difference of pitch. Having arrived so far, they proceed to estimate, with all the introspective mental ingenuity of which they were capable, the number of units contined in the various intervals used by musicians of their time.
20. The circumstance which sets Bharata and his follower Sarangdev on a pedestal above Aristoxenus and the rest of them, including your Tamil philosophers, is that one can trace a connection between the intervals of 13 srutis, 9 srutis, 4.3, 2 srutis and one sruti with which they deal and the harmonic intervals 3/2, 4/3, 9/8, 10/9, 16/15, 81/80.
21. In short my position is that, until modern times, artificial music only existed in the brins of primitive philosophers.
Yours faithfully,
(Sd.) E.CLEMENTS.
APPENDIX
NOTE I
Note on the so-called test of the Indian harmonium.
22. Jakroddin appeared to be influenced by the generally sceptical and disapproving attitude of the audience towards the instrument.
He reluctantly admitted that pa which was exactly 3/2 of sa wass correct. He found ma komal which was exactly 4/3 too low. He found ga komal, an exact minor third above sa (6/5) too low for Bhiravi. He found ni tivra which was a just semitone (16/15) below sa too flat for Yaman.
23. He wouldn’t agree that I had the Kafi notes on the instrument at all as far as I remember, but I have not detiled note of this.
I remember his Kafi took the major tone to start with and not the minor tone. I gave a note to the President giving all detils, but I cannot find a copy of it. All I have is a brief notice from which and from memory I give the above statement.
24. It appeared to me that Jakroddin is not gifted with a phenomenally accurate ear.
19-8-16. 	(Sd.) E.C.
NOTE II
I have recently tested the notes given by the frets of two binas made by Hussenkhan the renowned Sitar-maker of Miraj.
They both gave the following scals.
Tivra notes :-
	Sa 	re 	ga 	ma 	pa 	dha 	ni 	sa.
	9/8 	10/9 	16/15 	9/8 	10/8 	9/8 	16/15
To dha is the low or madhya tivra note.
Komal notes :-
	Sa 	re 	ga 	ma 	pa 	dha 	ni 	sa.
	16/15 	10/9 	9/8 	9/8 	16/15 	10/9 	9/8
The ga and ni are the low ones which I have always found associated with Kafi. Bhimpalas, Miyaki Malhar, Sindhada etc.
The ga and ni of Bhiravi, Jivanpuri etc. are obtined by pressing hard on the fret or pulling the wire to one side and so increasing the tension. Tivra dha is got in the same way.
(Sd.) E.C.
