Introduction to the study of Indian Music Page. 2.
The present work deals with Hindustani Music only; the author hopes to be able to show that a great part of it is directly traceable to the systems set forth in Bharata’s Natya Shastra of about the fifth century A.D. and the Sangit Ratnakar of the thirteenth century. These are the most closely reasoned and critically worded of the early text books.
inta nūl intustāṉ caṅkītattippaṟṟi māttiram pēcukiṟatu. atil colliyirukkum anēka kāriyaṅkaḷ 5-m nūṟṟāṇṭiluḷḷa parata nāṭṭiya cāstirattilum, 13-m nūṟṟāṇṭiluḷḷa caṅkīta ratṉākarattilum colliyirukkum muṟikaḷiṉiṉṟu eṭukkappaṭṭavikaḷtāṉ. āti kirantaṅkaḷil inta iraṇṭu nūlkaḷtāṉ takunta niyāyatāraṅkaḷuḷḷavi yum ārāycciyuḷḷavikaḷumāy irukkiṉṟaṉa.
caṅkīta rattiṉākaramum, parata cāstiramum takunta niyāya ātāraṅkaḷum ārāycciyumuḷḷaviyeṉṟu collukiṟīrkaḷ. inta nūlkaḷi ātāramākak koṇṭē tāṅkaḷ intustāṉ caṅkītattiṟku nūl eḻutukiṟa tākac collukiṟīrkaḷ. aṭutta vākkiyattil caṅkīta ratṉākaratti ārāyntu pārttāl atu intustāṉ caṅkītattippaṟṟic collukiṟa teṉṟu collukiṟīrkaḷ. itu evvaḷavu tūram uṇmiyā yirukkumeṉṟu nām pārkka vēṇṭum.
Introduction to the study of Indian Music Page 2.
“It is reputed that Sarangdev, the author of the Sangit Ratnakar, was an inhabitant of Kashmir. From internal evidence one would conclude that the Music he describes is that of Hindustan. However, the pandits of southern India endeavour to appropriate him to themselves. The present writer hopes to show that it is only by doing violence to his theory that it can be applied to Karnatic Music.”
“caṅkīta ratṉākaram eḻutiṉa cāraṅkatēvar kāṣmīr nakaravāci eṉpatu yāvarukkum terinta viṣayam. nūliṉuḷ ārāyntu pārttāl avar collu kiṟatu intustāṉ caṅkītattip paṟṟi, āṉāl teṉṉintiya caṅkīta paṇṭitarkaḷ avar taṅkaḷic cērntavar eṉṟu collik koḷḷa muyaṟcik kiṟārkaḷ. innūli eḻutukiṟavar eṉṉa rūpikkap pōkiṟā reṉṟāl, avaruṭiya koḷkikku muṟṟum virōtamāṉa oṉṟic coṉṉāltāṉ atu karnāṭaka caṅkītattiṟku ēṟṟatāka muṭiyum.”
cāraṅkatēvar tēvakiri eṉṟa ūril cimmaṇarājaṉ kālattil 1207-1249 variyum camastāṉa vitvāṉāyiruntatākavum akkālattil innūl eḻutappaṭṭatākavum terikiṟatu. 1294kku mēl vintiyamalikkut teṉpākam makamatiyarkaḷ paṭiyeṭuttu vantārkaḷēyoḻiya ataṟkumuṉ aṅku varavilli. avarkaḷ vantapiṉ tēvakirikku araṅkapāttic cērnta tulatapāt eṉṟu peyar vaḻaṅkiṟṟu. itaṉāl intustāṉ caṅkītattiṟku eṉṟu annūl eḻutappaṭṭatallaveṉṟu terikiṟatu. avar intustāṉ caṅkītattiṟku eḻutiyiruppārāṉāl intustāṉ pāṣi pēcuvōr vaḻaṅkum teyvaṅkaḷiṉ peyar, mukkiyamāṉa rājākkaḷiṉ peyar, avar kālattilirunta navāpiṉ peyar mutaliyavikaḷaṉittum nūliṉ colli yiruppārē. avar appaṭic collāmal intukkaḷuṭiya teyvaṅkaḷiyum muṉivarkaḷiyum maṟṟum intukkaḷuṭiya paḻakka vaḻakkaṅ kaḷiyumē muṟṟum colliyirukkiṟār. atōṭu pūrva tamiḻnāṭṭil vaḻaṅki vanta pala irākaṅkaḷil takka eṉpati ṭakka eṉṟum, nāṭṭarākam eṉpati nāṭṭi eṉṟum, cātāri eṉpati rūpacātāri, cutta cātāri eṉṟum, viravam eṉpati piravam eṉṟum, kuṟiñci eṉpati kurāñci eṉṟum, intaḷam eṉpati ittōḷam eṉṟum, taṉāci eṉpati taṉṉiyāci eṉṟum, iṉṉum ivipōl pala paṇkaḷiṉ peyarkaḷiyum māṟṟi avar vaḻaṅki yirukkiṟār.
itōṭu irākacañcāram colvati nām kavaṉippōmāṉāl tamiḻ nāṭṭil vaḻaṅki vanta viravam, varāṭi, takkarākam, intaḷam pōṉṟa irākaṅ kaḷukku ilakṣaṇam collukiṟār. avvirākaṅkaḷiṉ curaṅkaḷum curutikaḷum tamiḻ muṟippaṭi colliyiruppārāṉāl ellōrukkum upayōkappaṭak kūṭiyatāyirukkum. irākaṅkaḷiṉ alaku muṟiyum 22 curutiyil colvatiṉāl avikaḷi muṟṟilum aṉupōkattiṟku varāmal taḷḷumpaṭi nēriṭṭatu.
vēkarañci eṉṟa irākattiṟkuc collum ilakṣaṇattiyum cura cañcārattiyum nām kavaṉippōmāṉāl avikaḷ mēkarañcaṉi eṉṟu taṟkālattil vaḻaṅkum irākattiṟkuriyaviyāyirukkiṉṟaṉa. itit tamiḻ makkaḷ mēka irākam eṉṟu coṉṉārkaḷ. mēka irākam eṉṟa pūrva peyari mēkarañci eṉṟum, vēkarañci eṉṟum māṟṟiṉatēyoḻiya maṟṟappaṭi irākacañcāram mūṉṟukkum oṉṟākavē irukkiṟateṉṟu kāṇpōm. āṉāl 22 curuti muṟiyil ivikaḷ pāṭa muṟṟilum kūṭāta kāriyameṉṟu terikiṟatu.
tamiḻnāṭṭil vaḻaṅkivanta paṇkaḷiyum, irākaṅkaḷiyum, colla vantavar tamiḻ makkaḷ vaḻaṅki vanta 24 curutikaḷ iṉṉaviyeṉṟu aṟintu koḷḷāmal oru stāyiyil 22 eṉṟu mēḷam kaṭṭic coṉṉatiṉālē muṟṟilum avar nūl upayōkappaṭāmal pōyviṭṭatu. teṉṉintiya caṅkīta muṟippaṭi annūl upayōkappaṭavēṇṭumāṉāl kāntārak kirāmattit tēṭip pōyirukkum caṅkīta ratṉākarari varavaḻittu, 24 curuti muṟippaṭi, tāṅkaḷ collum ilakṣaṇaṅkaḷit tiruttik koṭukka vēṇṭumeṉṟu kēṭṭāl tiruntumēyoḻiya vēṟu evvitattilum avar nūl aṉupōkattiṟku varātu. intastāṉ caṅkītam paṭippōrkaḷukku avar eḻutavumilli. avar muṟippaṭi intustāṉ caṅkītamirukkavumilli. intustāṉ caṅkītam paṭippōr itil mayaṅka villi eṉṟu intiya ārmōṉiyattit taḷḷiṉatiṉāl aṟintu cantōṣappaṭukiṟēṉ. caṅkīta ratṉākarariyum paratariyum cariyāṉa niyāya ātārattōṭu uyarnta pīṭattil vitta tāṅkaḷ avarḷi avamāṉap paṭuttukiṟīrkaḷeṉṟu itaṉpiṉ varum taṅkaḷ vacaṉattāl teḷivāyk kāṇkiṟōm.
Introduction to the study of Indian Music, Introduction, Page XIII.
“Modern text books may appear learned to the uninitiated; the historian will, however, frankly admit that, since the days of the Sangit Ratnakar, Indian Musical systems have fallen into such confusion that no one has been able to reconcile the teaching of that authoritative treatise with latter works on the subject or with the practice or theory of modern musicians.”
“cūṭcumam teriyātavarkaḷukkut taṟkāla caṅkīta nūlkaḷ veku kalvittiṟami yuḷḷavikaḷāyk kāṇappaṭalām. āṉāl carittirakkāraṉ eti veḷippaṭiyāy oppuk koḷḷuvāṉeṉṟāl, caṅkīta ratṉākaram tōṉṟiya nāḷ mutal intiya caṅkīta muṟikaḷ catā cantēkattukku iṭamāyviṭṭatu. mūla nūleṉṟum atikāra nūl eṉṟum oppuk koḷḷappaṭṭa caṅkīta ratṉākarattukkum pintiṉa nūlkaḷukkum yātoru campantamumilli yeṉpatu māttiramalla, anta nūlukkum taṟkāla cāstira aṉupōkaṅkaḷukkuṅkūṭa koñcamākilum campantamē yilli.”

mēṟkaṇṭa vacaṉattil ‘caṅkīta ratṉākaram eṉṟa nūli upayōkatti lillāta aḻintu pōṉa paḻiya nūl eṉṟu niṉikkiṟārkaḷ’ eṉṟu collukiṟīrkaḷ. caṅkīta cāstiraṅkaḷ yāvaṟṟilum vīṇiyi uyarvākac collappaṭṭirukkiṟatu. maṉuṭa cārīrattāl collakkūṭiya iṉiya nuṭpamāṉa curaṅkaḷiyum vīṇiyil collalām. maṟṟa vāttiyaṅkaḷil colla muṭiyāta neṭil kuṟil oṟṟukkaḷum iṉṉum niṉikkakkūṭiya iṉiya ōcikaḷum vīṇiyil collappaṭak kūṭiyatāyiruppataṉāl ati uyiruḷḷa vāttiyameṉṟum tēvavāttiyam eṉṟum coṉṉārkaḷ. maṉitaṉi tēvavāttiyameṉṟum allatu kāttira vīṇiyeṉṟum maṉuṭa carīratti ottirukkum ceṅkōṭṭiyāḻi tāru vīṇiyeṉṟum cāma vētattiṉ tuvakkattil collappaṭṭirukkiṟatē. ippaṭi mēṉmi poruntiya vīṇi vācikkum viṇīkarkaḷum pāṭakarkaḷum caṅkīta ratṉākaram aṉupōkattiṟku varāmal aḻintu pōṉa paḻiya nūl eṉṟu colvati muṟṟilum kavaṉiyāmal tāṅkaḷ caṅkīta ratṉākarar muṟiyi eṭuttu niṟuttuvatākac collukiṟīrkaḷ. pūrva tamiḻ makkaḷ yāḻ eṉṟu vaḻaṅki vanta vāttiyatti vīṇi yeṉṟu taṟkālattavar vaḻaṅki varukiṟārkaḷ.

“Verse 51:- Samvadi Svaras are those between which are eight or twelve Srutis.”
“taṅkaḷukkiṭiyē eṭṭu allatu 12 curaṅkaḷuḷḷavi camvātip porutta curaṅkaḷām.”
“It will be noted that to have eight or twelve Srutis between, means intervals of nine and thirteen Srutis respectively.”
“iṭiyil 8 allatu 12 curutikaḷuṭiyaviyeṉṟu collumpōtu 9 allatu 13 iṭiveḷikaḷuḷḷa curutikaḷ eṉṟu tāṟpariyam.”

5. eṉṉuṭiya iraṇṭāvatu viyācattil nāṉ koṭuttirukkum aṭṭavaṇiyiṉpaṭi vīṇi ceytu aḷantu meṭṭu vittu atil taṟkālam vaṭanāṭṭil pāṭappaṭum curaṅkaḷi aṉupōka pūrvamāyp pāṭik koṇṭirukkum muṟippaṭiyē kavaṉittāl 13-āvatu curutiyākiya pañcamattiṉ pētam uṅkaḷukkut teriyum. ulakam eṅkum paṭikkappaṭṭu varum pañcamam uṅkaḷ aṉupōkattil kaṇṭu koṇṭapiṉ, pañcamam 13-āvatu curutiyeṉṟu cāraṅkar collum muṟi cariyāṉatallaveṉṟu mikat teḷivākat terintu koḷvīrkaḷ.

Geometrical Progression muṟippaṭi pañcamattiṟku 700 ceṉṭs varukiṟatu. itaṟkuk kaṇakkuc collāmal nuṭpamāṉa cura ñāṉattik koṇṭu ca-pa, ca-pa vāka oru stāyiyil 12 curaṅkaḷ amitta mēṟṟiciyāriṉ pañcamam 700 ceṉṭskaḷāka varukiṟatu. pañcamam 700 ceṉṭskaḷāka irukka vēṇṭumeṉṟu coṉṉa Mozart, Beethoven aip pārkkilum taṅkaḷ ārāycciyum aṉupōkamum periteṉṟu oruvarum oppuk koḷḷa māṭṭārkaḷ. tāṅkaḷ eṭuttukkoṇṭa 2/3kku caṟṟēṟak kuṟiya 702 ceṉṭskaḷ varukiṉṟaṉa.itu 709 ceṉṭskaḷukku eppaṭip poruntum? muṟṟilum poruntāta oru aḷaveṉṟu tāṅkaḷ kavaṉikka vēṇṭum.
6. mēlum ca-pa, pa-ri, ri-ta, ta-ka, ka-ni, ni-ma, ma-ri, ri-ta, ta-ka, ka-ni, ni-ma, ma-ca eṉṟu porutta curaṅkaḷ varukiṟatākap pūrva tamiḻ nūlkaḷil collap paṭṭiruk kiṟatu. oru stāyiyil 22 curutikaḷ eṉṟa muṟiyilum ip poruttamē collappaṭukiṟatu. aṭiyil varum aṭṭavaṇiyil teḷivāyk kāṇpōm.
cāraṅkatēvar ca-pa muṟiyāy 13 curutikaḷ varum eṉṟu colvatu
tavaṟutal eṉṟu kāṭṭum aṭṭavaṇi
caṅkīta ratṉākarar collum alaku muṟiyil ēḻāvatu variyiluḷḷa ca-pa vukku 13 alakukaḷ varukiṉṟaṉa. appaṭiyē 2, 4, 5, 6 eṉṟa varikaḷum 13 ākavē varukiṉṟaṉa. āṉāl mutal variyiluḷḷa pa-ri 12 alakākavum 3-āvatu variyiluḷḷa ta-ka II alakākavum varukiṟatē. ivikaḷ eppaṭip poruntum? tāṅkaḷ koñcam kavaṉippīrkaḷāṉāl ca-pa viṉ poruttam kiṭikkāta oru muṟiyic coṉṉār eṉṟu teḷivākak kāṇpīrkaḷ. iṉṉum iraṇṭu curutikaḷ cērntāl māttiram ca-pa poruntumeṉṟu teḷivākat terikiṟatu. mummūṉṟāka varum iraṇṭu curaṅkaḷil ov voṉṟu cērttuc colla vēṇṭum.
ippaṭiyē oṉpatu curutiyuṭiya ca-ma poruttamum oṉpatu, oṉpatāy vara vēṇṭiyataṟkup patil pattum patiṉoṉṟumāka varukiṟatu. ivikaḷik kavaṉikkāmal 22 curutiyi viḻuṅki 25 curutiyi ēppamiṭukiṟīrkaḷ. pūrva tamiḻmakkaḷ vaḻaṅki vanta 24 curutikaḷil iraṇṭu alaku kuṟittuk kamakamāyp pāṭavēṇṭumeṉṟa cūṭcumatti aṟiyāmal paratariyum caṅkīta ratṉākarariyum uyarnta pīṭattil vikkiṟīrkaḷ.
tāṅkaḷ pūrva tamiḻ nūl muṟikaḷip pārkkāta kuṟiyē yoḻiya vēṟilli. ātiyōṭan tamāyt teḷivākac collum nūlkaḷillāmi yiṉāl tamiḻ nāṭṭilullōrum 22 eṉṟu cātikka ārampittārkaḷ. tuvāvimcati curutiyiṉ mayakkam koṇṭa caṅkīta vitvāṉkaḷ muṉ oṉṟum piṉ oṉṟumākap pēcik kutarkkam ceytārkaḷ. eṉṟālum vivēkikaḷ uṇmiyiyum aṉupōkattiyum aṟintu tiriyappaṭut tiṉārkaḷ. tāṅkaḷ ōcikaḷ ēṇiyippōla cama aḷavuṭiyavikaḷā yirukkavēṇṭumeṉṟu muṟippaṭiyē nāṉ kaṇitattilum, aṉupōkattilum kāṭṭiṉēṉ. itaṟku mēlum tāṅkaḷ aṟiyāmaliruppatu eṉ atiruṣṭan tāṉ.
7. itōṭu tāṅkaḷ collum ārmōṉik iṭiveḷikaḷip paṟṟi caṟṟup pārppōm.
(1) inta ārmōṉik iṭiveḷikaḷip paratarum caṅkīta ratṉākararum kaṉavilum kaṇṭiruppatilli.
(2) ca-pa 2/3, ca-ma 3/4 eṉṟa aḷavi avarkaḷ curam kaṇṭupiṭippataṟku nūlkaḷil collavumilli.
(3) ca-pa 13 curutikaḷiyuṭiyavi ca-ma 9 curutikaḷiyuṭiyaviyeṉṟu coṉṉārkaḷē yoḻiya 2/3, 3/4 eṉṟu collavilli.
(4) avar muṟippaṭi ca-pa 709 ceṉṭskaḷākavum ca-ma 491 ceṉṭs kaḷākavum varukiṉṟaṉa. itaṟkum 702 ceṉṭskaḷāy varum 2/3 kkum 498 ceṉṭskaḷāka varum 3/4kkum eṉṉa campantamirukkiṟatu? iti uṟṟup pārkkāmal Harmonic Ratio eṉṟu caṅkīta vitvāṉkaḷukkut teriyāta kaṇakkukaḷic collukiṟīrkaḷ. intak kaṇakkilēyā caṅkītam irukkiṟatu? ikkaṇakku maṟṟavarukkut teriyāteṉṟu parikācamum paṇṇukiṟīrkaḷ.
pallāyira varuṭaṅkaḷākap parampariyāyt tamiḻ makkaḷ pāṭik koṇṭirukkum caṅkītattik kavaṉippīrkaḷāṉāl patiṉmūṉṟu oṉpatu eṉṟa muṟiyum aṅku illi. 2/3, 3/4 eṉṟa puraḷiyum aṅku illi. pa 2/3, ma 3/4, ka5/6 mutaliya piṉṉaṅkaḷi eṭuttuk koṇṭu avikaḷi oṉṟōṭoṉṟu perukki varum eṇkaḷi iṅkē colkiṟīrkaḷ. tāṅkaḷ collukiṟa piṉṉak kaṇakku cariyallavē. āṉāl muṉṉuḷḷa periyōrkaḷ ippaṭic collavilli. atāvatu ca-pa, ca-pa vāka oru stāyiyil 12 curaṅkaḷ varum eṉṟu coṉṉārkaḷ. avarōkaṇa muṟiyāy ca-ma, ca-ma vāka oru stāyiyil 12 curaṅkaḷum varukiṉṟaṉa veṉṟu coṉṉārkaḷē yoḻiya 2/3 āl cila curaṅkaḷiyum, 3/4 āl cila curaṅkaḷiyum, 5/6 āl cila curaṅkaḷiyum, kaṇṭupiṭikkac coṉṉārkaḷā? 2/3, 2/3 ākap perukki oru stāyiyil 22 curutikaḷit tāṅkaḷ kaṇṭu piṭittāl appōtu varumpiṉṉa eṇkaḷiṉ viparītam taṅkaḷukkut teriyum. ippiṉṉaṅkaḷukkum 13, 9, 4, 3, 2, 1 eṉṟa caṅkīta ratṉākarariṉ ilakkaṅ kaḷukkum evvita campantamumilli. ivikaḷippaṟṟit tāṅkaḷ collukiṟatu pōla āṭamparamāka nāṉ collalām. āṉāl nāṉ colvatit teḷivākat tāṅkaḷ aṟintu koṇṭu maṉantiruntuvataṟku ēṟṟa aḷavu māttiram coṉṉēṉ. taṅkaḷukku ivi pōtāteṉṟāl iṉṉa iṉṉa viṣayam eṉṟu kuṟittu eḻutuṅkaḷ. tāṅkaḷ tiruptiyākum varikkum uṇmiyāṉavikaḷi eḻuta mikap piriyamāyirukkiṟēṉ. uṇmiyaṟṟavikaḷi nāṉ eḻuta virumpavilli. nāṉ ārāyntu pārkkāta oṉṟiyumtaṅkaḷukku eḻuta māṭṭēṉ. tāṅkaḷ intiya caṅkītatti vicārikkat tuvaṅkum poḻutē ‘variyāṭṭuk kuṭṭikaḷiṉ kālmoḻikaḷip puraṭṭiviṭṭu vaḷartta rāpiṉcaṉ kurucōvippōl’ tappitamāṉa kaṇakkiṉāl vēṟu oru ticikkut taṅkaḷi tiruppi viṭṭārkaḷ. tāṅkaḷ cellum kōṇalāṉa vaḻiyi viṭṭu oḻuṅkāṉa pātikkut tirumpuṅkaḷ. tirumpuṅkaḷ eṉṟu mikavum kēṭṭuk koḷḷu kiṟēṉ. ‘muḷḷil utippatu uṉakku kaṭiṉamām’ eṉṟu cuvāmi collum paṭi naṭanta muraṭṭuc cavultāṉē maṉan tiruntiyapiṉ paricutta pavul appōstalaṉāṉār.
21. “curukkamāka eṉ apippirāyam eṉṉa veṉṟāl taṟkālam vari Artificial caṅkītamāṉatu āti cāstirikaḷiṉ mūḷikaḷil iruntatē yallāmal nicamāy upayōkattililli eṉpatē.”
mēṟkāṭṭiya kuṟippiṉāl cama aḷavāṉa iṭiveḷikaḷiyuṭiya caṅkītam āti cāstirikaḷiṉ mūḷiyil iruntatēyallāmal uṇmi yāy upayōkattil illi eṉkiṟīrkaḷ. tāṅkaḷ āti cāstirikaḷiṉ mūḷikaḷip pārttirukkiṟatākac collukiṟīrkaḷ. epṭip pārttīrkaḷō eṉṟu nāṉ āccariyappaṭukiṟēṉ. pīraṅkiyiṉ iruppuk kuṇṭukaḷip pōla eppakkattilum kaṉatta ōṭukaḷiṉāl mūṭappaṭṭuḷḷa mūḷikaḷ taṅkaḷukku ilakuvāka eppaṭit terintaṉa? vāyiṉāl nāḷatu variyum tamiḻ makkaḷ pāṭikkoṇṭirukkum kītam iṉṉateṉṟu aṟintukoḷvatu mikac culapa meṉṟu eṇṇukiṟēṉ. aṉupōkattilikkum icculapamāṉa muṟiyit terintu koḷḷātirukkiṟa tāṅkaḷ, kaṇṇukkup pulappaṭātirukkum mūḷikkuṭ pōy eppaṭik kaṇṭupiṭittīrkaḷ?
oru vēḷi tāṅkaḷ mūḷi eṉṟu colvati avarkaḷ eḻutiya nūliṉ karutteṉṟu collukiṟatāka vittukkoṇṭāl, tamiḻ ici nūlkaḷ taṅkaḷukkut teriyātē. avikaḷiṉ karutti itu variyilu muḷḷa tamiḻmakkaḷum caṅkīta ratṉākararum ataṉ muṉ paratarum cariyāy aṟintu koḷḷātirukkiyil tāṅkaḷ aṟintukoṇṭatu eppaṭi, curaṅkaḷum curutikaḷum cama aḷavuṭiyavikaḷāyirukka vēṇṭumeṉṟu avarkaḷ coṉṉārkaḷ eṉṟu collukiṟīrkaḷ. tāṅkaḷum ‘curamum curutiyum cama iṭiveḷikaḷuṭiyatāy vara vēṇṭum. ca-pa, ca-ma muṟiyāy curaṅkaḷ kaṇṭupiṭikkappaṭa vēṇṭumeṉṟa pūrvattāriṉ muṟippaṭiyē cura varicikaḷ cama aḷavuṭiyavikaḷāyirukkum. avikaḷ ēṇippaḻuvip pōla ēṟutaṟkum iṟaṅkutaṟkum aṉukūlamāyirukka vēṇṭum’ eṉṟu tiṣṭāntam colli eccarittum irukkiṟīrkaḷ. āṉāl taṅkaḷ mūḷiyi liruntapaṭi aṉupōkattiṟku varavilliyē. oḻuṅkīṉamāṉa iṭiveḷi kaḷiyuṭiya 25 curutikaḷit tāṅkaḷ collukiṟīrkaḷ. avikaḷi itaṉ muṉ pārttirukkiṟōm. uṇmi taṅkaḷ taliyil iruntirukkiṟatu. kiyil vantatō apattam. iti aṉupōkattilirukkum curaṅkaḷukku ottuvaravilliyeṉṟu āl intiya mīyūcik kāṉpareṉsil vantirunta vitvāṉkaḷ kaṇṭu taḷḷiṉārkaḷē. piṉṉi ēṉ tāṅkaḷ maṟṟavarkaḷip paḻikka vēṇṭum? col oṉṟum ceyki vēṟumāyiruntāl ulakam aruvarukkumē.
pūrva tamiḻ makkaḷ curutikaḷ camamāyirukka vēṇṭumeṉṟu tāṅkaḷ niṉittavikaḷiyē coṉṉārkaḷ. coṉṉavikaḷiyē cātittuk kāṭṭi yirukkiṟārkaḷ. avarkaḷ kāṭṭiyapaṭiyē nāḷatu variyum aṉupōkamu mirukkiṟatu. ivikaḷit terintu koḷvataṟku muṉ nāṉum taṅkaḷip pōlavē kalaṅkiṉēṉ. āṉāl taṅkaḷippōl pustakamum ārmōṉiya mum ceytukoḷḷavilli. iravu pakal itē niṉivāyiruntu vēli ceytu koṇṭu varukiyil teyvātīṉamāy iraṇṭu, mūṉṟu kuṟippukaḷ terintu avikaḷ aṉupōkattukku vantaṉa. aṉupōkattiṟku vantirunta taṉāl tamiḻ nūliṟ colliya viṣayaṅkaḷi aṟintu koḷḷak kūṭiya vaṉāṉēṉ. illiyāṉāl nāṉum taṅkaḷip pōliruppēṉ. oru stāyiyil 24 curutikaḷ irukkiṉṟaṉaveṉṟu aṟinta nāṉ oru irāka cañcārattiṟkuriya pūraṇa amcaṅkaḷiyum kāṭṭakkūṭiya kītam eḻutavum, avikaḷil kīrttaṉam uṇṭākkavum kūṭiya tiṟamiyiyaṭintēṉ. avikaḷic ceytu kāṭṭa nōkkamuṭiyavaṉāy aṅku vantēṉ. tāṅkaḷ curutiyip paṟṟi vātāṭum camayattil capiyōr koṭutta oru ārōkaṇa avarōkaṇattil oru kīrttaṉamāvatu irākac cāyiyāvatu putitākac ceytu pāṭik kāṭṭumpaṭi uṅkaḷik kēṭka vēṇṭumeṉṟu piraciṭeṇṭ navāp ālikkāṉ avarkaḷukkuk kaṭitattil eḻuti ñāpakappaṭuttiṉēṉ. āṉāl avarkaḷ ‘itu yārāl muṭiyum?’ eṉṟu taṅkaḷik kēṭkāmal niṟutti viṭṭārkaḷ.
nāṉō tāṅkaḷ koṭukkum ārōkaṇa avarōkaṇattil irāka cañcāramāvatu, kītamāvatu, kīrttaṉamāvatu ceyyat tayarāy vantiruntēṉ. nāṉ eṉṉip perumiyāyc collik koḷvatu cariyalla. āyiṉum eṉṉip paṟṟi muṟṟilum teriyāta taṅkaḷukkuc cila kuṟippukaḷic colvatu tappitamākātu. nāṉ karnāṭaka caṅkītattil vaḻaṅki varum curam curutikaḷ iṉṉaviyeṉṟum iṉṉiṉṉa curutikaḷ iṉṉiṉṉa kīrttaṉaṅ kaḷōṭu varukiṉṟaṉaveṉṟum kaṇṭupiṭitta piṉ tamiḻ nūlil itaṉ viparam aṟintēṉ. appaṭiyē kītam ceyvataṟkum kīrttaṉaṅkaḷ ceyvataṟ kumuriya muṟi terinta piṉpē pūrva tamiḻ nūlkaḷil avikaḷ collap paṭṭirukkiṉṟaṉa eṉṟu kaṇṭēṉ. ivikaḷ yāvum irākaṅkaḷip paṟṟic collum iraṇṭām puttakattil viparamāy veḷi varum. nāṉ kaṇṭu piṭittēṉ eṉṟa perumi pārāṭṭik koḷvatip pārkkilum ivikaḷuk kuriya ātāramāṉa vitivakikaḷ pūrva tamiḻ nūlkaḷil kāṇappaṭuvataṉāl avikaḷiyē eṉakku ātāramāka eṭuttukkoṇṭēṉ. nāṉ eṭuttuk koṇṭa viṣayattil tamiḻ nūlkaḷ mūlamāyt teyvam ivvaḷavāvatu kirupi ceytārē yeṉṟu mikunta cantōṣamaṭintēṉ.
atōṭu eṉṉic cantikkum tērnta vitvāṉkaḷ palarukkum kītam paṭittukkāṭṭi oppukkoḷḷappaṭṭirukkiṟatu. micūr camastāṉa vitvāṉ viṇīka cikāmaṇi makā-rāca-rāca-ciṟi cēṣaṇṇā avarkaḷum, vijayanakaram camastāṉa vitvāṉ viṇīka cirōmaṇi makā-rāca-rāca-ciṟi vēṅkaṭa ramaṇatās avarkaḷum, arikēcavanallūr, makā-rāca-rāca-ciṟi muttiyāya pākavatar avarkaḷum, tañci, vīṇi vēṅkaṭācalamiyar avarkaḷum kīta muṟikaḷik kēṭṭu mikavum cantōṣattuṭaṉ oppuk koṇṭirukkiṟārkaḷ. kīta muṟikaḷik kēṭṭuc cantōṣamaṭinta micūr, makā-rāca-rāca-ciṟi kiruṣṇa rāv B.A. avarkaḷiṉ apippirāyatti aṭiyil varum cila varikaḷil kāṇka.
Indian Music Journal By H.P.Krishna Rao, B.A. Vol.I. No.5. 191, Page 102, 103.
“Two days-25th and 26th were spent at Tanjore in the company of Rao Sahib Abraham Pandither avl. The Rao Sahib is a very popular gentleman both by his profession and good nature. He is an ardent admirer of music and the treatise on music that he is writing is likely to be of immense good to the students only if he would carry out the plans he has chalked out. All his children are well-versed in music, eastern and well as western, and it is a great pleasure to every friend of the Pandit to listen to the sweet singing of his children in solo or in concert. One admirable work that he is engaged in is the laying down of a set of rules for enabling every student of music to compose Gitams, Swarajatis and other Pieces.
makā-rāca-rāca-ciṟi II, P. kiruṣṇarāv B.A. avarkaḷuṭiya intiyaṉ miyūcik jarṉal Vol.I. No.5.  1911 pakkam 102, 103.
“25 ām, 26 ām tētikaḷākiya iraṇṭu nāṭkaḷiyum tañcāvūril Rao Sahib Pandither avarkaḷuṭaṉ kaḻittōm. taṉṉuṭiya toḻil mūlamāyum caṟkuṇattiṉ mūlamāyum Rao Sahib avarkaḷ yāvarālum naṉku matikkap paṭṭārkaḷ. caṅkītattil avarkaḷukku attiyanta pirīti. ippōtu avarkaḷ eḻutik koṇṭu varum caṅkīta nūlāṉatu avarkaḷ maṉatil niṉittiruk kiṟa piḷāṉpaṭi muṭivaṭiyumāṉāl caṅkītam paṭippavarkaḷukku atika pirayōcaṉamuḷḷatāy irukkum. avarkaḷ kumārar kumārattikaḷ ellārum mēṟṟici caṅkītattilum kīḻttici caṅkītattilum tērntavarkaḷāṉatāl avarkaḷ iṉṉiciyōṭu taṉittup pāṭuvatiyum ellōrum oṉṟu cērntu pāṭuvatiyum avarkaḷ cinēkitarellōrum kēṭṭu āṉantikkum paṭiyāṉa cilākkiyam irukkiṟatu. ippōtu avarkaḷ ceytu varum vēli yiṉ arumiyāṉa pākam eṉṉaveṉṟāl caṅkītam kaṟkum ovvoru varum tāṉāy kītam, svarajati mutaliyavaṟṟi eḻutum paṭikkāṉa vitikaḷi eḻutikkoṇṭu varuvatē.”
itaṉ arumiyi mutal mutal tamiḻ makkaḷum ataṉpiṉ maṟṟavarum veku cīkkiram aṟivārkaḷ. eṉ niṉippiliruntatiyē vāyiṉāl coṉṉēṉ. kiyiṉāl ceytu kāṭṭiṉēṉ. piḷḷikaḷ pāṭiṉārkaḷ. tāṅkaḷ ca-pa muṟiyāka varum curaṅkaḷ cama iṭiveḷikaḷuṭiyavikaḷāyirukka vēṇṭumeṉṟu colvatum, ēṇip paḻukkaḷip pōl ēṟutaṟkum, iṟaṅkutaṟkum utaviyāyirukka vēṇṭu meṉṟu colvataṟkup poruntuvatum, aṉupōkattukku varakkūṭiyatum, pallāyira varuṭaṅkaḷākat tamiḻ makkaḷ pāṭikkoṇṭiruppatum ivikaḷē. ivikaḷittāṉē āti cāstirikaḷiṉ mūḷiyiliruntavi eṉṟum taṅkaḷ mūḷiyil iruppavi eṉṟum tāṅkaḷ collukiṟīrkaḷ.
itit tāṅkaḷ artificial iṭiveḷikaḷuṭiya teṉṟu ēḷaṉañ ceykiṟīrkaḷ. oṉṟāyirunta ātāra caṭcam paṭippaṭiyāy mēlē pōkum poḻutu mattiyastāyi caṭcam iraṇṭākavum ataṉ mēl tāra caṭcam pōkum poḻutu nālākavum varum eṉṟa caṅkīta ratṉākarariṉ vacaṉam Geometrical Progression aittāṉ kuṟikkum eṉṟu aṟivāḷikaḷ oppuk koḷvārkaḷē. ataṉ irakaciyam taṅkaḷukku itaṉmuṉ terintiruntāl iti artificial eṉṟu colliyirukkamāṭṭīrkaḷ. taṅkaḷ pustakam 34 ām pakkattil oru stāyiyi iraṇṭākavum mūṉṟāvum paṉṉiraṇṭākavum pirippataṟku lākarta muṟippaṭiyirukka vēṇṭumeṉṟu mika aṟpamākat taṅkaḷukkut tōṉṟiyirukkiṟatu. eṉṟālum atu ‘kuruṭaṉ taṉ kālil taṭṭiya paṇappiyik kalleṉṟu niṉittuk kālāl taḷḷiviṭṭu appuṟam pōṉatu pōl’ uṅkaḷit tavaṟutalāka naṭatta ētuvāyiruntatē yoḻiya cariyāṉa muṟikku vaḻi naṭattavilli. cariyāṉa muṟiyākac collum cila mēṟṟiciyāriṉ nūlkaḷiyum tāṅkaḷ pārkkavilli pōlirukkiṟatu.
The art of tuning the Pianoforte by Hermann Smith, Page. 75, 76.
“Mr.W.H.B.Woolhouse remarks truly, “It is very misleading to suppose that the necessity of temperament applies only to instruments which have fixed tones. Singers and performers on perfect instruments must all temper their intervals, or they could not keep in tune with each other, or even with themselves; and on arriving at the same notes by different routes would be continually finding a want of agreement. The scale of Equal temperament obviates all such inconveniences, and continues to be universally accepted with unqualified satisfaction by the most eminent vocalists; and equally so by the most renowned and accomplished performers on stringed instruments, although these instruments are capable of an infinite variety of intonation. The high development of modern instrumentl Music would not have been possible, and could not have been acquired, without the manifold advantages of the tempered intonation by equal semitones, and it has, in consequence, long become the established basis of tunning.”
“Mr.Woolhouse eṉpavar eṉṉa collukiṟār eṉṟāl, curaṅkaḷ stāpamāyirukkappaṭṭa vāttiyaṅkaḷukkuttāṉ curaṅkaḷukkuc caripākamāyp pirikkummuṟi avaciyam, maṟṟavikaḷukku avaciyamalla eṉṟu niṉippatu picaku. pūraṇavāttiyaṅkaḷi vittup pāṭupavarkaḷum, vācippavarkaḷum kūṭa taṅkaḷ curaṅkaḷic curutikkēṟka amittuk koḷḷāviṭṭāl, maṟṟavarkaḷōṭu cērntu pāṭavāvatu tāṅkaḷē cutta curattil pāṭavāvatu kūṭātu. pala vaḻikaḷiṉ mūlamāy orē curaṅkaḷil vantu cēravēṇṭiya avaciyam iruppatāl aṭikkaṭi vācippōrukkum pāṭuvōrukkum cura vittiyācaṅkaḷ ēṟpaṭṭuk koṇṭēyirukkakkūṭiyatu. curutikaḷi camapākamākap pirittu stāpikkappaṭṭa ārōkaṇamāṉatu ivvita vittiyā caṅkaḷi uṇṭākka māṭṭātu. atuvē caṅkītam pāṭukiṟa vitvāṉkaḷ muṟi. vāttiyaṅkaḷ palavum palavitamāy curutiyēṟṟak kūṭiyaviyā yirunta pōtilum tantivāttiyaṅkaḷil nipuṇarāṉa ellā caṅkīta vitvāṉkaḷum cariyeṉṟu oppukkoḷḷum vaḻiyum ituvē. ippaṭi curaṅkaḷukkiṭiyiluḷḷa iṭiveḷikaḷi camapākaṅkaḷākap pirikkum muṟi ēṟpaṭṭapiṟakutāṉ, caṅkīta vāttiyakāṉamāṉatu atika tērcciyaṭin tirukkiṟatu mallāmal, atuvē ellā vāttiyaṅkaḷiyum curutikkēṟkak koṇṭuvarum muṟiyeṉṟum, atiṉāl uṇṭākum pirayōcaṉaṅkaḷ aṉantam eṉṟum, yāvarālum oppukkoḷḷappaṭukiṟatu.”
itaṉāl curutikaḷic camapākamākap pirikka vēṇṭum eṉṟum nipuṇarāṉa ellā vittuvāṉkaḷum oppukkoḷḷum muṟi yeṉṟum curaṅkaḷ camamāyp pirikkappaṭṭapiṉ tāṉ caṅkītam mikavum tērcci yaṭintirukkiṟateṉṟum camamāyp pirippataṉāl uṇṭākum pirayōcaṉam aṉanta meṉṟum collukiṟārē. tāṅkaḷ ēṇiyippōl tāṉē ituvum irukkiṟatu. piṉṉiyēṉ oḻuṅkaṟṟa muṟikaḷic cātikkiṟīrkaḷ? cama  aḷavāṉa 12 curaṅkaḷiyum atōṭu kamakamāyc cērttup pāṭum nuṭpa curaṅkaḷiyum aṟiyātataṉāl ippaṭi mayaṅkiṉīrkaḷ. iṉi ammayakkam vēṇṭām. pūrva tamiḻmakkaḷiṉ muṟiyum ituvē. pōtumāṉa ātāramu mirukkiṟatu.

taṅkaḷ intiyaṉ ārmōṉiyattik kūṭivantavarkaḷ yāvarum aruvaruttu appiriyattik kāṇpittārkaḷ eṉṟum anta apippirāyat tiṉāl cākruṭīṉ cāyapu iḻukkappaṭṭuk keṭṭa apippirāyappaṭṭār eṉṟum collukiṟīrkaḷ. niyāyamillāmal oru vāttiyatti capiyiluḷḷa yāvarum aruvarukkamāṭṭārkaḷ. aṅkē vantiruntavarkaḷ caṅkītattil tērnta navāpukaḷum, ciṟṟaracarkaḷum, Professor kaḷum, pala uyarnta utti yōkattiluḷḷavarkaḷum, mēṟṟici caṅkītattilum intiya caṅkītattilum tērnta kaṉamporuntiya pala turicāṇikaḷum, caṅkītamē jīvaṉamākak koṇṭa vitvāṉkaḷumāyiruntārkaḷ. ivarkaḷ ellōrum taṅkaḷ ārmōṉiyatti aruvaruppataṟku av ārmōṉiyattiṉ curaṅkaḷ aruvaruppāyiruntatē kāraṇam. kāraṇamillāmal avarkaḷ aruvaruttut taḷḷavilli. pārapaṭcamuḷḷavarkaḷ iraṇṭoruvar iruntārkaḷō illiyō aṟiyēṉ. āṉāl capiyiluḷḷa perumpāṉmiyōri nāṉ kavaṉittatil avarkaḷ mukattil viḷaṅkiya tējaciṉālum – vārtti yiṉālum - piracaṅkaṅkaḷiṉālum avarkaḷ oru vārttiyum tavaṟāta cattiya cīlarkaḷ eṉṟu eṉakkuppaṭṭatu. taṅkaḷ apippirāyattiṟku mika aṟparkaḷ eṉṟu paṭṭatu eṉ maṉatiṟku vētaṉiyāyirukkiṟatu. maṟṟavar aruvarukka ataṉāl iḻukkuṇṭa cākruṭīṉ cāyapum keṭṭa apippirāyap paṭṭār eṉṟu collumpoḻutu avar maṉacāṭciyillātavar eṉṟum, cattiyam tavaṟic collukiṟavar eṉṟum, maṟṟavarkaḷ collukiṟapaṭi yellām āṭukiṟavareṉṟum karutiṭamākiṟatē. takunta vitvāṉ eṉṟu vaṭanāṭṭil koṇṭāṭappaṭum oru vitvāṉi ippaṭit tāṅkaḷ ava mariyātiyāyc colvati niṉittu varuttappaṭukiṟēṉ. tāṅkaḷē karakarappiriyāvil varum curaṅkaḷukkut taṅkaḷ ārmōṉiyattiṉ curaṅkaḷ kuṟikiṉṟaṉaveṉṟu capimuṉ oppukkoṇṭapiṉ ippaṭic colvatu niyāyamākumā?
23. “eṉakkut terinta variyil kāpi irāka curaṅkaḷ ārmōṉiyattil koñcamāvatu cariyāyirukkavilli eṉṟār. āṉāl itippaṟṟi nuṭpamāy nāṉ kuṟittu vikka villi.”
avar pāṭiya kāpi irākam Major tone-il ārampittatu. Minor tone-il ārampikkavilli. ivikaḷi yellām kuṟittu nāṉ President  kkuk koṭuttirukkiṟēṉ. āṉāl eṉṉiṭattil ataṟkuk kāppi illi. eṉ kiyiliruppatu coṟpak kuṟipputāṉ. maṟṟaviyellām eṉ ñāpakatti liruntē eḻutukiṟēṉ.”
‘kāpi irākattil varum curaṅkaḷ ārmōṉiyattil koñcamāvatu cariyāyirukkavilli eṉṟār’ eṉṟu ivvaḷavāvatu uṇmi coṉṉīrkaḷē. capi muṉ kāpi irākattil varum curaṅkaḷukku ārmōṉi yattil varum curaṅkaḷ kuṟikiṉṟaṉaveṉṟu tāṅkaḷē vāyiṉāl oppuk koṇṭīrkaḷē. kāpi irākam Major tone-il avar ārampittup pāṭiṉāl. Minor tone-il atu ārampikka māṭṭātu. Minor tone-il ārampittāl ‘nāma nārāyaṇi’ eṉṟa aimpatāvatu mēḷakkarttāvil jaṉitta ‘kucumapōki’ eṉṟa irākamākum. tāṅkaḷ Minor tone--il ārampittataṉāl kāpiyiṉ curaṅkaḷukku muṟṟilum poruntavilli. Major tone -il tāṅkaḷ ārampittup pāṭiya poḻutu kāpi irākattiṟkuk kūṭutalāyiruntatu. ippaṭippaṭṭa oru apacurak kuṭukkiyik koṇṭu vantāl pittiyakkārarkaḷē ati ām eṉṟu colvārkaḷ.

cākruṭīṉ cāyapu nuṭpamāṉa curaṅkaḷip pakuttaṟiyak kūṭiya kātuṭiyavaralla eṉṟu collukiṟīrkaḷ. eṉṉiṭattil avarippaṟṟit tāṅkaḷ colla eṉṉa avaciyamirukkiṟatu? eppoḻutu avar vāyit tiṟantu taṉṉāl kūṭiya atikanēram orē curutiyil curattic coṉṉārō appoḻutē avar takunta vitvāṉ eṉṟu nāṉ eṇṇiṉēṉ. avar taṅkaḷ ārmōṉiyattiṉ curam cariyāyirukkiṟatō illiyō eṉṟu tāṅkaḷ pala taṭavi pārkkum variyilum taṅkaḷ ārmōṉiyattiṉ apacuram taṉ kātiṟpukāmal kiyik kātil vittuk koṇṭu oru curattilēyē alivillāmalum kūṭutal kuṟivillāmalum niṉṟār. tāṅkaḷ ārmōṉiyattiṉ kāṟṟāṭiyip palamāka mitittum cura stāṉattip palamāka aḻuttiyum Major tone-kkum Minor tonekkum māṟṟi māṟṟip pārttīrkaḷ. 25 curuti variciyil etiyāvatu piṭittuk kāṭṭi viṭalāmeṉṟu pala nimiṣam pirayattaṉappaṭṭīrkaḷ. āṉāl avarō mikunta kāmpīramāy muṉ piṉ pōkāmal oru curattilēyē niṉṟu kāṭṭiṉār. ippaṭik kāṭṭiṉa oru vitvāṉi atika curañāṉam uḷḷavar eṉṟu collat tayārāyilli eṉkiṟīrkaḷ. yār uṅkaḷit tērnta vitvāṉ eṉṟu collumpaṭik kēṭṭārkaḷ? piḷḷikaḷ vīṇiyil 24 curutikaḷip pāṭik kāṭṭukiyil atōṭu avarum cērntu 24 curutikaḷi vāyiṉāl pāṭikkāṭṭiṉārē. atit tāṅkaḷum kēṭṭuk koṇṭiruntīrkaḷ. appaṭip paṭṭa oruvari curaṅkaḷip pakuttaṟiyakkūṭiya kātuṭiyavaralla eṉṟu collukiṟīrkaḷē, itu niyāyamā yirukkiṟatā? maṟṟavarkaḷ tāṅkaḷ colvati oppukkoḷvārkaḷā?
tāṅkaḷ intustāṉi irākaṅkaḷil vaḻaṅki varum curaṅkaḷukku ottuvarāta ārmōṉiyam ceytu vantatiṉāl intustāṉi caṅkītatti lāvatu, piḷḷikaḷ pāṭiyapoḻutu ‘vēṟu ārōkaṇa avarōkaṇaṅkaḷukku māṟip pōṉārkaḷ’ eṉṟu colvatiṉāl karnāṭaka caṅkītattilāvatu, curaṅkaḷ cama aḷavuṭiyatāy ēṇip paḻuvippōl varavēṇṭumeṉṟu colliviṭṭu ‘paṇṭitar Equal Temperament muṟikku iḻukkiṟār, piḷḷikaḷ artificial iṭiveḷikaḷi upayōkippatiṉāl kāṉam aruvaruppāyiruntatu’ eṉṟu colvatiṉāl iṅkilīṣ miyūcikkilāvatu taṅkaḷukkut takunta ñāṉamilli eṉṟu teḷivākak kāṭṭukiṟīrkaḷ. immūṉṟu vitamāṉa caṅkītamum teriyāta tāṅkaḷ cākruṭīṉ cāyapu avarkaḷi niyāyantīrppatu eppaṭi? ati yār oppukkoḷvārkaḷ? taṅkattukkum korintu tēcattiṉ pittaḷikkum pētamilliyā?
avarip paṟṟic colvatu taṅkaḷ mēl kuṟṟamilli. tāṅkaḷ 2/3, 3/4 eṉṟa cura ñāṉa maṟṟavarkaḷ collum kaṇakki eṭuttukkoṇṭu kaṇṭupiṭikkum oḻuṅkaṟṟa curuti muṟiyic collik kāṭṭum ārmōṉiyatti nāṅkaḷ pārttum atiluḷḷa apacuraṅkaḷik kēṭṭu mirukkiṟōm. apacurak kuṭukkiyākiya av ārmōṉiyattiṉāl uṅkaḷ kātu keṭṭuppōyirukkiṟatu. ellōrum mikunta piriyamāy periya vitvāṉ eṉṟu koṇṭāṭi rājacapiyilum pāṭumpaṭic ceyta avari mikat tērnta vitvāṉ alla eṉṟu colvataṟkuk kāraṇam intiya caṅkītattil taṅkaḷukku irukkum kuṟinta aṟivē eṉṟu eṇṇukiṟēṉ. capiyōr yāvariyum āṉantikkac ceyta kuḻantikaḷiṉ kāṉam taṅkaḷi māttiram aruvarukkac ceyta kāraṇam yātu? taṅkaḷiṉ ārmōṉiyattil varum apacuramallavā? palavita puṣpaṅkaḷik kaṭṭum pūkkaṭṭi vīṭṭut tiṇṇiyil, irāttiri paṭuttirukka vēṇṭumeṉṟu uttiravu kēṭṭup paṭuttirunta vaḻippōkkarāṉa mīṉ viyāpārikaḷ, puṣpa vācaṉiyiṉāl tūkkam varāmal neṭunēram puraṇṭu puraṇṭu caṅkaṭappaṭṭup piṉpu taṅkaḷ mīṉ kūṭiyi eṭuttut taliyil kaviḻttuk koṇṭu naṉṟāyt tūṅkiṉārkaḷ eṉpatupōla, apacuram niṟinta ārmōṉiyam taṅkaḷ kāti evvaḷavākak keṭuttirukkiṟateṉṟu aṟintu, itaṟkup parikāramilliyō eṉṟu varuttappaṭukiṟēṉ.
itōṭu tāṅkaḷ collum cila pariṭcikaḷum cila irākaṅkaḷil varum curaṅkaḷiṉ tīrmāṉamum 2/3, 3/4 eṉṟa aḷaviṉāl tāṅkaḷ kaṇṭu colvatik koṇṭu avikaḷip paṟṟi nāṉ colvatu vīṇvēli yākum eṉṟu viṭṭuviṭṭēṉ.
aṉpuḷḷa turiyē! nāṉ eḻutiya maṟuppil taṅkaḷ kaṇakkil 2/3, 3/4 ākap pōkum muṟi muṟṟilum tappitameṉṟum oru stāyiyil 22 allatu 25 curutikaḷ eṉṟu tāṅkaḷ collum muṟi oru nāḷum kūṭāta kāriyameṉṟum teḷivākac coṉṉēṉ. atōṭu āyaṉacayaḷa āyaṭi-il tāṅkaḷ eḻutāmal viṭṭa viṣayaṅkaḷiyum eḻutiṉēṉ. ivikaḷil etiyāvatu eṭuttut takunta ātāram colli maṟuppu eḻutavēṇṭiyatu ciramam. appaṭiyiruntāl tāṅkaḷ eḻutiya viyācam vācippōrkaḷukkup pirayōcaṉamāyirukkum. taṅkaḷ viyācattiṉmēl kuṟippu colvataṟkāka 24 nampar pōṭṭup pirittēṉēyoḻiya ati māṟṟiviṭa niṉikkavilli. tāṅkaḷ eḻutiṉa kaṭitattiyē ippaṭip pirittēṉ.
eṉ maṉatiṟkut taṅkaḷ viyācattip pārttavuṭaṉ mika aruvaruppā yiruntatu. eṉṟālum eṉ maṉati camātāṉappaṭuttikkoṇṭu cila kuṟippukaḷ eḻutiṉēṉ.
tāṅkaḷ eḻutiya viyācattiṉ ciṟcila kuṟippukaḷiṉāl piṉ varum tappitaṅkaḷ ceykiṟatākat terikiṟatu.
atāvatu :-
1. ‘parōṭā kāṉpareṉsil enta vitamāṉa rucuvum carivara naṭattappaṭavilli’ eṉpataṉāl āl intiya miyūcik capiyip paṟṟik kuṟivākavum, 										(3)
2. ‘ārmōṉiyattippaṟṟi naṭanta pariṣiyāṉatu parikācak kūttāyiruntatu’ eṉpataṉāl capiyil vantiruntavarkaḷ atippariṭcikkat takuntavarkaḷ alla eṉṟum, 								(4)
3. ‘capiyil vantirunta vitvāṉkaḷ Major tone, Minor tone, Tempered Scale mutaliya nuṭpamāṉa vittiyācaṅkaḷit teriyātavarkaḷ. āṉāl piṉṉa eṇkaḷit taṅkaḷukkut teriyāmalē upayōkikkiṟārkaḷ’ eṉpatiṉāl capiyil vantirunta vitvāṉkaḷ caṅkītamāvatu, kaṇitamāvatu uṅkaḷip pōl teriyātavarkaḷ eṉṟum, 						(6)
4. ‘piḷḷikaḷ pāṭiyatu uṅkaḷ apippirāyatti niliniṟuttiṉatāka niṉikkiṟīrkaḷ’ eṉpataṉāl eṉ apippirāyam vēṟu piḷḷikaḷiṉ kāṉam vēṟāyiruntateṉṟum, 									(7)
5. ‘tampurāvi vittup pāṭātataṉāl avarkaḷ cariyāṉa caṅkītam pāṭavilli’ eṉpataṉāl avarkaḷ tappāṉa caṅkītam pāṭiṉārkaḷ eṉṟum, 													(8)
6. ‘Artificial iṭiveḷikaḷi upayōkittataṉāl aruvaruppāyiruntatu. iṉimiyāyilli, vēṟu ārōkaṇa avarōkaṇaṅkaḷukku māṟi viṭṭārkaḷ’ eṉṟu colvataṉāl piḷḷikaḷ pāṭiya pāṭalkaḷ muṟṟum tavaṟutaleṉṟum, 									(9, 11, 12, 13)
7. ‘curaṅkaḷ cama aḷavuṭiyatāyp pirikka vēṇṭumeṉṟa cāsti rōktamillāta oru caṅkīta muṟiyi ēṟpaṭuttiṉārkaḷ’ eṉṟu colvataṉāl cama aḷavāyp piritta pūrva tamiḻ muṉivarkaḷiyum eṉṉiyum payittiyakkārarkaḷeṉṟum, 						(19)
8. ‘Artificial caṅkītamāṉatu āti cāstirikaḷiṉ mūḷiyi liruntatē yallāmal upayōkattililli’ eṉpataṉāl avarkaḷ aṉupōka maṟṟavarkaḷ eṉṟum, vīṇāṉa cāstiraṅkaḷi eḻuti vittārkaḷeṉṟum, 													(21)
9. ‘capiyil vantiruntavarkaḷ taṅkaḷ ārmōṉiyatti aruvaruttu appiriyappaṭṭārkaḷ’ eṉpataṉāl avarkaḷ pārapaṭcamuḷḷavarkaḷeṉṟum niyāyantīrkkan takutiyaṟṟavarkaḷ eṉṟum,					 (22)
10. ‘cākruṭīṉ cāyapu atiṉāl iḻukkappaṭṭār’ eṉṟu colvataṉāl avar oru niliyil nilittirāta pattāmpacali cōṭāpāṭṭilip pōla niccaya puttiyillātava reṉṟum. 							(22)
11. ‘cākruṭīṉ cāyapu atika nuṭpamāṉa kātuṭiyavareṉṟu collat tayārāyilli’yeṉṟu tāṅkaḷ colvataṉāl avarukku caṅkītat tiṟami pōtātu eṉṟum collukiṟīrkaḷ. 						(24)
ivviṣayaṅkaḷit tāṅkaḷ naṉṟāyk kavaṉittup pārttīrkaḷāṉāl ikkuṟippukaḷil enta oṉṟiyāvatu colla muṟṟilum takutiyaṟṟavarkaḷ eṉṟu tōṉṟum, āyiṉum taṅkaḷ ārmōṉiyam taḷḷappaṭṭataṉāl uṇṭākiya maṉa varuttattiṉālum - maṉakkuḻappattiṉālum - paṇac celaviṉālum - avamāṉattiṉālum ippaṭic collukiṟīrkaḷ eṉṟu eṉṉic cāntappaṭuttikkoṇṭu iti eḻutiṉēṉ.
tāṅkaḷ oppukkoḷḷum mukkiyamāṉa iraṇṭu kuṟippukaḷ.
(1) ‘karakarappiriyā irākattil varum curaṅkaḷukku ārmōṉiyam kuṟintateṉṟu cākruṭīṉ cāyapu coṉṉār’ eṉṟu colvatum taṅkaḷ ārmōṉiyam capimuṉ pariṭcikkappaṭṭut taḷḷappaṭṭatu eṉṟa karut taṭaṅkiya vārttikaḷic colvatum,
(2) ‘taṅkaḷ kuḻantikaḷiṉ kāṉam cākruṭīṉālum maṟṟavarkaḷālum atikamāyp pukaḻappaṭṭatu’ (aticayikkappaṭṭatu) eṉṟu colvatum caṟṟu uṇmiyāyirukkiṉṟatu.
ivviraṇṭiyum tāṅkaḷ oppukkoṇṭatē pōtum. ivviraṇṭi yum paṟṟiyē muṉ viyācattil eḻutiyiruntēṉ. ippōtum oppuk koḷḷukiṟīrkaḷ. taṅkaḷ ārmōṉiyam taḷḷappaṭṭatum piḷḷikaḷiṉ kāṉam oppukkoḷḷappaṭṭatum parōṭāvil naṭantavikaḷil mukkiya māṉavi. ivviraṇṭiṉ campantamāy uṇmiyāka naṭantavikaḷi yāvarum aṟintukoḷḷa iṅku eḻutiṉēṉ. ivviraṇṭiyum tāṅkaḷ oppukkoṇṭa piṉ iṉimēl maṟuttu eḻutap peṉ eṭukkat tuṇiya māṭṭīrkaḷeṉṟu niṉikkiṟēṉ. ārmōṉiyam taḷḷappaṭṭatu piḷḷikaḷiṉ kāṉam yāvarālum atikamākap pukaḻappaṭṭatu (āccariyamāy eṇṇappaṭṭatu) eṉṟu māttiram colliyiruppīrkaḷāṉāl tāṅkaḷ mikunta pukaḻccikku pāttirarāyiruppīrkaḷ. ettaṉi peyarip puṇpaṭuttiviṭṭīrkaḷ. itu intiya caṅkītattiṟku utaviyalla, upattiravam, upattiravap paṭuttum taṅkaḷippōl puṇṇiyavāṉkaḷ iṉi oruvarum taliyeṭukka māṭṭārkaḷ eṉpatu niccayam.
eppaṭiyāvatu taṅkaḷ maṉatil irunta uṇmi veḷivantatu eṉpati muṭivil aṟiya nāṉ mikavum cantōṣappaṭukiṟēṉ. ivviraṇṭu uṇmi kaḷum taṅkaḷi aṟiyāmalē taṅkaḷ mūḷiyiliruntu kivaḻiyāka pēṉāvil iṟaṅki miyiṉāl kaṭitattil eḻutappaṭṭaṉa. taṅkaḷ ārmōṉiyam taḷḷappaṭṭateṉṟum piḷḷikaḷiṉ kāṉam pukaḻappaṭṭa teṉṟum tāṅkaḷē collum poḻutu nāṉ vēṟu eṉṉa colla irukkiṟatu. uṇmiyik kavaṉikkum cila kaṉavāṉkaḷ eḻutiya kaṭitattiṉālum ivikaḷ pulappaṭukiṉṟaṉa. avikaḷil iraṇṭoṉṟit tāṅkaḷ pārkka vēṇṭiyatu avaciyam.
parōṭā kāṉpareṉsukku vantiruntavarkaḷil Mr.Bhatkande B.A., L.L.B.,  avarkaḷiyum micūr camastāṉam viṇīka vitvāṉ Mr.kiruṣṇarāv B.A.avarkaḷiyum tāṅkaḷ aṟivīrkaḷ. avarkaḷ kāṉpareṉsukku vantiruntapoḻutu kavaṉittavikaḷip paṟṟik kaṭitaṅkaḷil eḻutiyavikaḷ taṅkaḷukkum taṅkaḷippōl eṉ apippirāyattiṟku virōtamāy vātāṭum cila kōṇalkaḷukkum pirayōcaṉamāyirukkumeṉṟu eṇṇu kiṟēṉ.
V.N.BHATKANDE Esq., B.A., L.L.B.,
Santaram House, Malabar Hill, Bombay.
MY DEAR RAO SAHIB PANDITHER,
It is a practically long time since we separated at Baroda and In think I ought to take up my correspondence with you once more in my own interest. I may sincerely tell you that your great labours and scholarship very nearly stunned me. I shall be always proud of having the privilege of calling you my friend. I may or may not agree with all your views but that will never prevent me from always bearing in mind the fact that you are a great Music scholar. I am so thankful to Dewan Saheb that he brought us together. I shall certinly not fail to derive considerable benefit from your labours. I have to thank you most sincerely for coming to my help in hitting that mischievous sruti harmonium movement on the head in time. It had very nearly turned the heads of serveral of our workers here. Mr. Deval had almost persuaded the educational authorities of this presidency to introduce the Harmonium as a compulsory accompaniment in our schools. But for you I should not have been able to make my poor voice heard. You disposed of Deval’s Sharangdev’s srutis like a miracle.
Your exposition has however brought to light one fact and that is likely a disappoint all the present music enthusiasts here. I am referring to that part of your book where you say or rather point out-that with the exception of the Sa and its octave, none of the intermediate notes of will exactly correspond with any of our modern notes. You go on to say agin that all attempt at reviving Sarangadev’s music is bound to be a failure. This conclusion of yours seems to be of tremendous importance.
Yours Sincerely,
(Sd.) V.N.BHATKANDE.
eṉatu piriyamuḷḷa rāv cākēp paṇṭitaravarkaḷukku,
nām parōṭāvil oruvariyoruvar viṭṭup pirintu vekukālamāki viṭṭapaṭiyāl eṉṉuṭiya cuyakāriyattiṟkākavē nāṉ tirumpa taṅkaḷukku eḻutuvatu avaciyamāyt tōṉṟukiṟatu. caṅkītattiṟkākat tāṅkaḷ ceyta vēliyum taṅkaḷ kalvit tiṟamiyum eṉakku atipiramippi uṇṭu paṇṇiṉa. taṅkaḷi eppōtum eṉ cinēkitareṉṟu aḻikkum cilākkiya māṉatu eṉakku atika perumi. caṅkīta viṣayamāyt tāṅkaḷ collum apippirāyaṅkaḷi nāṉ cariyeṉṟu oppukkoṇṭālum oppukkoḷḷā viṭṭālum tāṅkaḷ caṅkītattil vitvāṉ eṉkiṟa caṅkatiyāṉatu eppōtum eṉ maṉatil irukkum. nammiruvaruṭiya cinēkitattiṟkum kāraṇarāyirunta Dewan Saheb avarkaḷukku vantaṉam collukiṟēṉ. taṅkaḷuṭiya vēliyiṉ palaṉiliruntu nāṉ atika payaṉ aṭivēṉ eṉpataṟkuc cantēkamilli.
takka camayam pārttut tāṅkaḷ eṉakku utaviyāy vantu anēka keṭutikaḷ ceytu vanta curuti ārmōṉiyak koḷkiyiṉ taliyi uṭittataṟkāka atika naṉṟiyaṟitaluḷḷavaṉāyirukkiṟēṉ. caṅkīta viṣayattil iṅku uḻikkum anēkaruṭiya irutayatti intac curuti ārmōṉiyam koḷḷi koṇṭu pōyviṭṭatu. Mr. tēvāl avarkaḷ inta rājatāṉiyiluḷḷa paḷḷikkūṭaṅkaḷil intac curuti ārmōṉiyat tik kaṭṭāyamāy upayōkappaṭuttumpaṭi kalācāli atipatikaḷi ēṟak kuṟiya cammatikkap paṇṇiviṭṭārkaḷ. tāṅkaḷ eṉ utavikku varātiruntatāl eṉṉuṭiya cattam vaṉāntarattil taṉiyāyk kiṭantu kattukiṟavaṉuṭiya cattam pōlāyirukkumē. Mr. tēvāl avarkaḷuṭiya cāraṅkatēva curutikaḷit tāṅkaḷ aṟputamāṉa vitamāy māyttu viṭṭīrkaḷ.
āṉāl, tāṅkaḷ collum apippirāyattil oru vicēṣamāṉatu iṅkirukkum caṅkīta vitvāṉkaḷukku mikavum atiriyatti uṇṭākku kiṟatu. ateṉṉaveṉṟāl, cāraṅkatēvar muṟippaṭi oru stāyiyil ṣaṭjamattiyum atiṉ eṭṭāvatu curamākiya ṣaṭjamattiyum tavira naṭuvil varum entac curamāvatu taṟkālattil vaḻaṅkum curaṅkaḷukku ottu varātu eṉṟu colluvatutāṉ. cāraṅkatēvaruṭiya caṅkītattit tirumpa eṭuttu niṟuttuvatu kūṭātakāriyameṉṟum tāṅkaḷ collukiṟīrkaḷ. inta muṭivāṉa vārttiyāṉatu atika vicēṣamāṉa oru caṅkati.
taṅkaḷiṉ uṇmiyuḷḷa,
(Sd.) V.N.BHATKANDE.
mēṟkaṇṭa kaṭitattiṉāl taṅkaḷ curuti ārmōṉiyam taḷḷap paṭṭateṉṟum tēvāl eṭuttuccoṉṉa cāraṅkatēvaruṭiya curutikaḷ pirayōjaṉamaṟṟavikaḷ eṉṟu taḷḷappaṭṭaṉaveṉṟum teḷivākac collukiṟār. nāṉ atikam collavēṇṭiyatilli eṉṟu eṇṇu kiṟēṉ.
SHASTARAM HOUSE, MALABAR HILL,
BOMBAY,
Monday 7th Aug. 16
DEAR RAO SAHIB PANDITHER,
Many many thanks for the copies of your refutation of Mr. Clement’s letters to the Madras Mail as also for the two kind letters accompanying the same. I think I have already told you that I would never cease to admire your great labours and scholarship. If I live long enough I won’t be surprised to find you one of these days mentioned as the great leader of the Southern Music School. *     * 	 *      *     *
Then Sharangadeva was dragged in and became their sheet-anchor. I was not able to effectively dislodge them from that position with that success which you obtined the other day. I frankly admit. * *
(In my travels throughout India) Not a single Pandit could argue the Shruti question with anything like precision. No authorities were ever cited or discussed. Many made attempts to say that some of the Ragas admitted smaller tones than semitones but when pressed to explin and demonstrate with reasons and authorities they backed out. No grantha could be cited as authority for the distribution of the Shrutis, which therefore appeared to be to depend on personal whims. As to the use of the well-known 12 notes there was absolutely no disagreement. 		* 	* 	*	*	*
But I had full confidence in my God. “Commit theyself unto God and trust in Him and He will bring it to pass,” was my motto. Who appealed sincerely to God and did not succeed? God Almighty saw that I was unjustly being swamped away by influential mischief-makers and decided to help me. He inspired H.H. The Gaekwar and his most sympathetic prime minister, the large-hearted Dewan Saheb, to take up my cuse. Your great assistance also I ascribe to His inspiration. I take no credit to me for all that happened at the Conference. Mr. Deval and Mr. Clements and their great following collapsed like a pack of cards. The Sanskrit Professors corroborated all my interpretations and falsified Deval’s. I never had a Shruti Theory of my own. I relied upon the 12 notes which were firmly established throughout the country. My contention all through my books was that for popular education in music a system based on the established 12 notes was very convenient and therefore ought to be retined. Of course when the minute Shrutis were unanimously accepted by our scholars and practical experts, I had not the lease objection to bow to their decision. It was naturally a great satisfaction to me that the great Conference came and decided that my contentions were not unreasonable. I shall never be elated with success becuse I know and honestly believe that it was He that was enacting all that was happening there.
*   *    *   *   *
Your 24 Shrutis theory is really very interesting. If it is duly accepted in the South by the musicians there, I should be the first person to give it a trial in our music.
* 	* 	* 	* 	*
Yours sincerely,
(Sd.) V.N.BHATKANDE.
piriyamuḷḷa rāv cākēp paṇṭitaravarkaḷukku,
kiḷameṇṭs turi meyilil eḻutiya kaṭitattiṟkut tāṅkaḷ eḻutiya maṟuppum attuṭaṉ aṉpāy aṉuppappaṭṭa taṅkaḷuṭiya iraṇṭu kaṭitaṅkaḷum kiṭittaṉa. avikaḷukkāka anēka vantaṉam collukiṟēṉ. tāṅkaḷ caṅkīta viṣayattil paṭṭa pirayācaṅkaḷiyum taṅkaḷuṭiya kalvit tiṟamiyiyum viyantu koḷḷum viṣayattil nāṉ orukālum calippatilli yeṉṟu nāṉ muṉṉamē taṅkaḷukkut terivittirukkiṟēṉ. kaṭavuḷ eṉakku āyucik koṭukkum pakṣattil cila varuṣaṅkaḷukkuḷ tāṅkaḷ teṉṉintiya caṅkīta muṟiyi stāpitta periya makāṉ eṉṟu ulakam oppuk koḷvatik kēṭṭāl āccariyappaṭamāṭṭēṉ.

piṟaku (Mr.Clements, Mr.Deval) cāraṅkatēvaruṭiya pustakatti ātāramākak koṇṭu avar mēl taṅkaḷ naṅkūrattip pōṭṭārkaḷ. inta naṅkūrattiliruntu avarkaḷik kiḷappiviṭa eṉakku atikap pirayāciyā yiruntapōtilum, tāṅkaḷ avarkaḷip parōṭā kāṉpareṉcil taṅkaḷ pāykaḷi virittu mutuku kāṭṭi yōṭa aṭittīrkaḷ eṉṟu maṉap pūraṇamāy oppuk koḷḷukiṟēṉ. 	* 	* 	* 	* 	*
(intiyāviṉ pala pākaṅkaḷilum cuṟṟi vantatil) curuti viṣayamāy niyāyātāraṅḷit takunta vitamāy eṭuttup pēcakkūṭiya oru vitvāṉāvatu akappaṭavilli. evarāvatu tāṅkaḷ collukiṟataṟku ātāratti eṭuttuk kāṇpikkak kūṭiyavarkaḷāyilli. anēkar, cila irākaṅkaḷil aric curattiviṭak kuṟinta curutikaḷ irukkiṉṟaṉa eṉṟu colliyum, avikaḷi vāyppāṭṭiṉ mūlamāvatu kaṇakkukaḷiṉ mūlamāvatu rucuppaṭuttak kēṭkappaṭṭapōtu piṉ vāṅki viṭṭārkaḷ. oru stāyiyil curaṅkaḷi eppaṭi niravukiṟatu eṉpataṟkuk kirantaṅkaḷiṉ mūlamāy oru rucuvum ēṟpaṭātatāl avarkaḷ taṅkaḷ maṉatiṟkut tōṉṟiyapaṭi niravi vantārkaḷ eṉṟu veḷiyāyiṟṟu. āṉāl yāvarukkum terintirunta 12 curaṅkaḷip paṟṟi evviṭattilāvatu vittiyācamāṉa apippirāyam ciṟitēṉum kāṇappaṭavilli. 	* 	*	 *	
āṉāl kaṭavuḷiṭattil eṉakku muḻu nampikkiyiruntatu. “uṉ vaḻikaḷik kaṭavuḷiṭam oppu vittu avarmēl nampikkiyāyi.ru avarē uṉ kāriyatti vāykkap paṇṇuvār” eṉpatē nāṉ nampiṉa cattiyam. uṇmiyāyk kaṭavuḷiṭam taṅkaḷ kāriyatti oppuvittavarkaḷil evar cittipeṟāmaṟ pōṉār? uyarnta pataviyil iruntukoṇṭu viṣamam ceykiṟavarkaḷāl nāṉ eṭutta kāriyattiṟku iṭiyūṟu uṇṭākiṟateṉṟu aṟinta kaṭavuḷ eṉakku utavi ceyya muṉ vantār. avar H.H.keykvār makārājā avarkaḷ maṉatilum mikunta paccātāpamum peruntaṉmiyum vāynta avarkaḷ mantiriyākiya Dewan Saheb avarkaḷ maṉatilum pukuntu eṉ kāriyatti eṭuttu niṟuttiṉār. tāṅkaḷ eṉakkuc ceyta pērutaviyum kaṭavuḷiṉ naṭattutaltāṉ. kāṉpareṉcil naṭanta yātoṉṟum eṉ ceyalalla.   *	 *         *         *         	
Mr.tēvālum Mr.kiḷameṇṭsum avarkaḷ kūṭṭamum, ārpāṭṭamum viḷiyāṭum cīṭṭukaḷāl kaṭṭappaṭṭa oru vīṭu aṭiyōṭu cāyvatupōl viḻuntu cāyntu pōṉārkaḷ. eṉ viyākkiyāṉaṅkaḷ ellām cari yeṉṟum tēvāluṭiya viyākkiyāṉaṅkaḷellām poyyeṉṟum camas kiruta paṇṭitarkaḷāl uṟuti ceyyappaṭṭatu. nāṉāka curuti muṟi oṉṟum uṇṭākkavilli. tēcameṅkum cātāraṇamāy vaḻaṅkivarum 12 curaṅkaḷtāṉ eṉṉuṭaya ātāram. eṉṉuṭiya pustakaṅkaḷil nāṉ pēcukiṟa kaṭciyellām yāteṉṟāl cātāraṇa jaṉaṅkaḷukkuc caṅkītam kaṟṟuk koṭuppataṟku 12 curaṅkaḷālāṉa muṟiyē veku culapam. ākiyāl avikaḷiyē upayōkattiṟkuk koṇṭu vara vēṇṭum eṉpatē. āṉāl capiyil vantirunta kalvimāṉkaḷum, caṅkīta vitvāṉkaḷum atinuṭpa curaṅkaḷi ēkōpittu oppukkoṇṭapōtu avarkaḷ tīrmāṉattiṟku yātoru taṭiyumiṉṟi tali kuṉintu vaṇaṅkiṉēṉ. intapperiya kāṉpa reṉs ēṟpaṭṭu nāṉ colliya muṟiyil niyāyattiṟku virōtamāṉatu oṉṟumilli yeṉṟu ceyta tīrppāṉatu eṉakku mikavum tiruptitāṉ. itu iyaṟkitāṉē. āṉāl kaṭavuḷtāṉ aṅku piracaṉṉamāki naṭantavikaḷuk kellām ātikāraṇarāyiruntār eṉṟu nāṉ niccayamākavē aṟintu vicuvācikkiṟapaṭiyāl eṉ kāriyam cittiyāṉataṟkāka nāṉ oru nāḷum perumi koḷḷamāṭṭēṉ.	*	*	*

mēṟkaṇṭa kaṭitattāl ‘paṉṉiraṇṭu cuṅkaḷi ellōrum upayōkat tiṟkuk koṇṭu vara vēṇṭumeṉpatu eṉṉuṭiya nōkkam. āṉāl capiyil vantirunta kalvimāṉkaḷum, caṅkīta vitvāṉkaḷum ati nuṭpa curaṅkaḷi ēkōpittu oppukkoṇṭapōtu avarkaḷ tīrmāṉattiṟku nāṉ yātoru taṭiyumiṉṟit tali kuṉintu vaṇaṅkiṉēṉ’ eṉṟu collu kiṟatit tāṅkaḷ kavaṉik vēṇṭum. curutikaḷip paṟṟiyum, nuṭpa curutikaḷip paṟṟiyum vīṇiyilum vāyppāṭṭiṉālum, āyappāliyil vaḻaṅkum 12 curaṅkaḷiyum, vaṭṭappāliyil vaḻaṅkum 24 curutikaḷiyum, tirikōṇappāliyil vaḻaṅkum 48 curutikaḷiyum, caturappāliyil vaḻaṅkum 96 curutikaḷiyum nāṉ tiṣṭāntappaṭuttik kāṭṭiyapōtu tāṅkaḷum Mr.Bhatkande avarkaḷum pakkam pakkamāy vīṇikkuc camīpattil iruntu kavaṉittuk koṇṭiruntīrkaḷ. tūrattilirunta uṅkaḷi  Mrs Atya Begum Fyzee Rahimin ammāḷ avarkaḷ kiṭṭavantu uṭkārumpaṭi varuntik kēṭṭuk koṇṭārkaḷ. avarkaḷālum maṟṟum capiyiluḷḷa kaṉavāṉkaḷ yāvarālum oruṅkē atikamāy āccariyattōṭu koṇṭāṭappaṭṭa caṅkītam taṅkaḷukku māttiram aruvaruppāyiruntatu eṉṟu collukiṟīrkaḷ.
nuṭpa curutikaḷi ovvoṉṟāy nālu pālikaḷiṉpaṭi vevvēṟu kīrttaṉaṅkaḷil pōtumāṉa paṭi rucuppaṭuttikkāṭṭi itil āṣēpaṉi yirukkumāṉāl collavēṇṭum eṉṟu capiyōrik kēṭkiyil avarkaḷ evvita āṣēpaṉiyum collāmal iruntārkaḷ. ippaṭic cāraṅkar curuti muṟi taṟkāla caṅkītattiṟku utavāteṉṟu rucuppaṭuttik kāṭṭum poḻutum karnāṭaka caṅkītattil vaḻaṅkivarum curutikaḷ Geometrical Progression paṭi varavēṇṭumeṉṟu collumpoḻutum nuṭpamāṉa curutikaḷip pāṭikkāṭṭi tiṣṭāntappaṭuttumpoḻutum āṣēpaṉi yiruntāl collavēṇṭumeṉṟu kēṭṭukkoṇṭēṉē.
akampāvattiṉāl capiyōri alaṭciyamāka nāṉ appaṭik kēṭka villi. periyōrkaḷ anēkar vantiruppārkaḷeṉṟum eṉ muṟiyil tavaṟutalkaḷit tirutti aṉukkirakam ceyvārkaḷ eṉṟum niṉittu mikavum vaṇakkamāyk kēṭṭuk koṇṭēṉ. āṣēpaṉi ceytiruntāl nuṭpa curutikaḷip paṟṟi iṉṉum virivākac colli vistarittiruppēṉ. āṉāl tāṅkaḷ oppuk koṇṭataṟku iṇaṅka avarkaḷ aṉpum ātaravu māṉa pala iṉiya vacaṉaṅkaḷ colli āravāramum ceytārkaḷ. capiyōr yāvarum oppukkoṇṭārkaḷ eṉṟu Mr.Bhatkande collukiṟataṟku māṟāka ‘itu rucuvalla’ eṉṟu collukiṟīrkaḷ. tāṅkaḷ ārmōṉiyatti rucuppaṭuttiviṭa vēṇṭumeṉṟu koṇṭuvantatupōla nāṉ karnāṭaka curuti muṟikaḷi rucuppaṭutti stāpittu viṭalāmeṉṟu niṉittu varavilli. intiyāvil ellā iṭaṅkaḷililumiruntu caṅkītattil tērnta kaṉavāṉkaḷ varum iṭattil pūrva tamiḻ nūliṉ apippirāyattiyum taṟkālattiṉ aṉupōkattiyum terivittu vikka vēṇṭumeṉṟu nāṉ eṇṇiṉēṉ. tivāṉ cākip V.P.mātavarāv avarkaḷ viruppattiṟkum parōṭā makārājar avarkaḷaḻippup pattirattiṟkum nāṉ kīḻppaṭiya vēṇṭumeṉṟu niṉittēṉ. rucuppaṭuttiviṭuvataṟku aṉukūlamāka oruvariyum āmōtikkumpaṭi kēṭṭuk koḷḷavumilli. eṉ apippirāyatti tāṅki rippōrṭṭil eḻutuvārkaḷeṉṟu nāṉ niṉikkavumilli.
31/2 maṇi nēramākavum ataṉpiṉ tāṅkaḷ coṉṉataṟkup patil collum viṣayamāka 3/4 maṇi nēramākavum ellōr maṉatiyum kavarntu koḷḷum paṭiyāka eṉ piracaṅkamum pāṭṭum iruntālum avikaḷik kāṉpareṉs muṭiyum camayattil eṭuttuc colla maṟantu pōṉārkaḷ. capiyār yāvarālum taḷḷappaṭṭa ārmōṉiyattik koṇṭu vanta taṅkaḷip paṟṟiyum, taṅkaḷ cinēkitarip paṟṟiyum, iṉṉuñ cilarip paṟṟiyum māttiram rippōrṭ vācittu muṭittārkaḷ. ēṉ ippaṭic ceytīrkaḷ eṉṟu nāṉ kēṭkumpoḻutu avacaramāy rippōrṭ tayār ceytōm, maṟantu pōṉōm; iṉi cērttuk koḷvōm eṉṟu coṉṉārkaḷ. iviyāvum Fine arts, Mrs.Samuel aṟivār. capiyi luḷḷa yāvariyum āccariyappaṭuttiyatu eṉṟu tāṅkaḷ collum ik kāriyam viṭappaṭṭup pōṉatippaṟṟi nāṉ varuttappaṭavumilli. iṉi rippōrṭ eppaṭit tayār ceyvārkaḷ eṉṟu niṉikkavumilli. eppaṭi yiruntālum “cattiyam pūmiyiliruntu muḷikkum nīti vāṉattiliruntu tāḻappārkkum” (caṅ. 85.11) eṉṟa vēta vacaṉampōla ivikaḷi iṉṉum cila kālattil pūraṇamāyk kāṇpīrkaḷ. nīṅkaḷ māttiram iti oru vēḷi kāṇāmal pōṉālum ulakattavar yāvarum kaṇṭu koḷvārkaḷ eṉpataṟku parōṭā kāṉpareṉsukku vantirunta capiyār yāvarum oppukkoṇṭatē pōtumāṉa cākṣiyeṉṟu niṉikkiṟēṉ. neruppukkup pukiyum nīrukku nuriyum pōla parōṭāvil kūṭiya āl intiya miyucik kāṉpareṉsukku tāṅkaḷum taṅkaḷic cērnta cilarumiruppatu periya kāriyamalla.
LAKSHMIPURAM,
Mysore, 10-8-1916.
DEAR SIR,
In your Tamil letter of invitation, I was glad to find that you were going agin to settle the question of Srutis. I heartly support your contention that Sharanga Dev was inaccurate in many respects, and that your exposition was most convincing. I appreciate only 3 or 4 papers that were presented in that Baroda Conference and yours was the most interesting to me of all. Those of Messrs. Clements and Deval were also learned, but the theories did not agree with their practical demonstrations. *    *     *     *     *
I agree to your division of the octave into 24 stutis and their demonstration through the help of your accomplished dughters. I am sure that the different notes used for the Ragas as expounded by you are correct.  *    *    *    *     *
If anything was striking to me in the Baroda Conference, it was your paper.
Wishing success to your earnest attempts. 
* 	* 	* 	* 	*
Yours truly,
(Sd.) H.P.KRISHNA RAO.

piriyamuḷḷa aiyā,
tāṅkaḷ eṉṉik kāṉpareṉsukku aḻitta (tamiḻil eḻutap paṭṭirunta) kaṭitattil kaṇṭa pirakāram curuti viṣayattip paṟṟit tirumpa vicārikkap pōkiṟōm eṉṟu eḻutiyiruntatu eṉakku metta cantōṣam. cāraṅkatēvar pala viṣayaṅkaḷil picakippōyirukkiṟār eṉṟu tāṅkaḷ colvati nāṉ maṉappūrvamāy oppukkoḷḷukiṟēṉ. tāṅkaḷ caṅkīta viṣayatti vistarittatāṉatu ellāruṭiya maṉatilum naṉṟāyppaṭṭatu. parōṭā kāṉpareṉsil vācikkappaṭṭa upanniyācaṅkaḷil mūṉṟu allatu nālu viyācaṅkaḷ nāṉ atika vicēṣamāṉavikaḷāka eṉ maṉatil paṭṭatu. avikaḷil taṅkaḷuṭiyatutāṉ ellāvaṟṟilum mēlāka eṉakkut tiruptikaratti uṇṭākkukiṟatu. Mr.kiḷameṇṭs tēvāl mutaliyavar kaḷuṭiya upanniyācaṅkaḷ atika kalvit tiṟamiyik kāṭṭiṉa pōtilum avarkaḷuṭiya muṟikaḷ vāttiyaṅkaḷiṉ rucuvōṭu ottirukkavilli.

taṅkaḷ uṇmiyuḷḷa,
(Sd.) H.P.KRISHNA RAO.
mēṟkaṇṭa kaṭitattil (1) cāraṅkatēvar pala viṣayaṅkaḷil tavaṟip pōyirukkiṟār eṉpati maṉappūrvamāy oppukkoḷḷukiṟēṉ; (2) tāṅkaḷ caṅkīta viṣayatti vistarittatāṉatu ellōr maṉatilum naṉṟāyp paṭṭatu; (3) taṅkaḷuṭiyatu (viyācam) tāṉ ellāvaṟṟilum mēlāka eṉakkut tiruptikaratti yuṇṭākkukiṟatu; (4) Mr.Clements, tēvāl mutaliyavar kaḷuṭiya upanniyācaṅkaḷ vāttiyaṅkaḷiṉ rucuvōṭu ottirukkavilli; (5) oru stāyiyi 24 camapākaṅkaḷākap pirippatiyum taṅkaḷ kumārattikaḷiṉ utaviyāl ati rucuppaṭuttiyatiyum cariyeṉṟu oppuk koḷḷukiṟēṉ; (6) pala irākaṅkaḷil varuvatākat tāṅkaḷ kāṇpitta curaṅkaḷ cariyeṉpataṟkuc cantēkamilli; (7) parōṭā kāṉpareṉsil eṉ maṉatil atikamākap paṭṭatu taṅkaḷ upanniyācantāṉ eṉṟu collum kuṟippukaḷit tāṅkaḷ kavaṉippīrkaḷāṉāl eṉ viyācattil colli yirukkum kuṟippukaḷ muṟṟilum cariyāṉaviyeṉṟu taṅkaḷukku viḷaṅkum.
caṅkīta ratṉākararuṭiya tuvāvimcati curuti muṟi taṟkāla caṅkītat tiṟku ottuvarātateṉṟu pala vitattilum rucuppaṭuttik kāṭṭiṉēṉ. taṅkaḷ kaṇita muṟiyum taṅkaḷ ārmōṉiyamum muṟṟilum ottuvaratavi yeṉṟu rucuppaṭuttiṉēṉ. oru stāyiyil paṉṉiraṇṭu 1/2 curaṅkaḷum irupattu nāṉku 1/4 curaṅkaḷum nāṟpatteṭṭu 1/8 curaṅkaḷum toṇṇūṟṟāṟu 1/16 curaṅkaḷum varukiṉṟaṉaveṉṟu kaṇita mūlamākavum vīṇiyil kaṇṭa aḷavu mūlamākavum curam curutikaḷ varum irākaṅkaḷ mūlamākavum viḷakkiṉēṉ. im mūṉṟiyum paṟṟi iṅkē collukiṟa vārttikaḷit tāṅkaḷ kavaṉikka vēṇṭum.
‘cāraṅkar pala viṣayaṅkaḷil tavaṟippōyirukkiṟār. Mr.Clements, tēvāl muṟikaḷ vāttiyaṅkaḷiṉ rucuvōṭu ottirukkavilli. curam curutikaḷit tāṅkaḷ rucuppaṭuttiyati cariyeṉṟu oppukkoḷḷukiṟēṉ. tāṅkaḷ kāṇpitta curaṅkaḷ cariyeṉpataṟkuc cantēkamilli’ eṉṟu collum kuṟippukaḷ eṉ apippirāyam cariyeṉṟu colvataṟkup pōtumāṉaviyallavā?  ivikaḷip pārkkilum nāṉ eṉṉa tiṣṭāntam koṭukkakkūṭum? ‘parōṭā kāṉpareṉsil eṉ maṉatil atikamāyppaṭṭatu taṅkaḷuṭiya viyācantāṉ’ eṉṟu kalvit tiṟamiyuḷḷavarum viṇīka vitvāṉumāyirukkiṟa oruvar collum cattiyatti nīṅkaḷ eppaṭi maṟukkakkūṭum? muḻu apattam eḻutiyikkiṟīrkaḷē. iṉṉum ippaṭippaṭṭa anēka kaṭitaṅkaḷ kāṭṭakkūṭum. ivarkaḷiruvarum parōṭā kāṉpa reṉsukku vantiruntavarkaḷ. ākiyiṉāl ivarkaḷ iruvar kaṭitatti māttiram eṭuttukkoṇṭēṉ.
eṉṉuṭiya curutimuṟi taḷḷappaṭṭatu. taṅkaḷ curuti muṟi yāvarālum aṅkīkarikkappaṭṭatu eṉṟu māttiram eḻutiyiruntāl nāṉ taṅkaḷip perumi pārāṭṭic colla ētuvāyirukkum. ivviraṇṭu kuṟippukaḷukku māttiram patil eḻutiyiruppēṉ. āṉāl ivikaḷōṭu kalanta maṟṟa kuṟippukaḷ avaṟṟiṟku patil eḻutum paṭiyāka eṉṉit tūṇṭiviṭṭaṉa. ellām eḻuti muṭinta piṉ avikaḷuḷ ivviraṇṭiyum paṟṟic colvatu avaciyamāyiṟṟu. taṅkaḷ ārmōṉiyam taḷḷap paṭṭa teṉṟu tāṅkaḷ oppukkoḷḷukiṟīrkaḷ. piḷḷikaḷiṉ kāṉam cākrūṭiṉ cāyapu avarkaḷālum, maṟṟavarkaḷālum atikamāyp pukaḻappaṭṭatu (āccariya māy eṇṇappaṭṭatu) eṉṟum collukiṟīrkaḷ. ivviraṇṭu mukkiyamāṉa kuṟippukaḷiyum tāṅkaḷē oppukkoṇṭatu yāvarālum kavaṉikkappaṭat takkatu.
ivviraṇṭu viṣayaṅkaḷil taṅkaḷ curuti muṟiyum ārmōṉiyat tiluḷḷa curaṅkaḷum capiyiluḷḷa yāvarālum aṉupōkattiṟku varātavi yeṉṟu taḷḷappaṭṭaṉa. tāṅkaḷum antac camayattil oppukkoṇṭu viṭṭataṉāl capiyiluḷḷa oruvar pākkiyillāmal ellōrālum uṅkaḷ curutimuṟi taḷḷappaṭṭatākavilliyā? appaṭiyē piḷḷikaḷ pāṭiya karnāṭaka caṅkītamum oru stāyiyil 12, 24, 48, 96 pōṉṟa nāta vēṟṟumikaḷum aṭaṅkiya nālu aṭṭavaṇikaḷil pala irākaṅkaḷ vācittuk kāṭṭiyapōtu cākrūṭīṉ cāyapu avarkaḷum capiyārummikunta āccariyap paṭṭārkaḷ eṉṟu tāṅkaḷ collum poḻutu ituvariyum kāṇāmalum kēṭkāmalumirunta nūtaṉamāṉa oṉṟik kaṇṭu kēṭṭu āṉantittārkaḷ eṉṟu tāṅkaḷ collukiṟatākat terikiṟatē. tāṅkaḷum piḷḷikaḷiṉ camīpattiliruntu naṉṟāyk kavaṉittīrkaḷ. antac camayam tāṅkaḷ oṉṟum kuṟicollavilli. ‘pukaḻntu koṇṭārkaḷ’ eṉpataṉāl capiyiluḷḷōrum tāṅkaḷum eṉ curuti muṟiyiyum ataṉpaṭi pāṭiya pāṭṭiyum oppuk koṇṭatāyiṟṟē. āṟumātattiṟku muṉ naṭantavikaḷukku virōtamāy ippoḻutu colluvatu muṟṟilum cariyallaveṉṟu itippārkkum aṟivāḷikaḷ yāvarum kāṇpārkaḷ.
uṇmiyāṉa kaṇakkiṟkum iṉimiyāṉa pāṭṭiṟkum aṉupōkamāṉa tiṣṭāntaṅkaḷukkum tāṅkaḷ koñcamāvatu aciyāmal patileḻutak kūṭiya tīrar eṉṟu nāṉ niṉikkiṟēṉ. intiya caṅkītattip paṟṟi maṟṟa tēcattār tavaṟutalāy eṇṇumpaṭi tāṅkaḷ oru iṭaṟu kallā yiruppīrkaḷō eṉṟu tōṉṟiyatāl iti eḻutiṉēṉ.
taṅkaḷip pōlavē teṉṉāṭṭil tuvāvimcati curuti eṉṟu vātāṭukiṟavarkaḷukku.
taṅkaḷippōl oḻuṅkīṉamāṉa cura varicikaḷiyum, kutarkkaṅ kaḷiyum collum palar innāṭṭilumiruntu teṉ intiya caṅkītattiṟkuk kuḻappam uṇṭākkukiṟati aṟintu taṅkaḷukkum, maṟṟavarukkum ilakuvāy viḷaṅkak kūṭiyavikaḷ evikaḷō avikaḷiyē eḻutiṉēṉ.
1. ‘vīṇiyil pañcamam kuṟikiṟa’teṉṟu kāṉpareṉsil vātāṭic capiyōrāl vīṇiyil pañcamam caritāṉ eṉṟu tīrkkappaṭṭut tōlvi yaṭinta ceṉṉi milāppūr cuntaramiyarum,
2. irupattiraṇṭu curutiyiṉpaṭi oru tukkaṭā pāṭikkāṭṭa vēṇṭu meṉṟu kāṉpareṉsil kēṭṭapoḻutu capimuṉ pāṭa muṭiyāmal oḷintu koṇṭa pūvaṉūr makā-rāca-rāca-ciṟi piratāpa irāmacāmi pākavatar avarkaḷum,
3. ‘taṉṉiyāciyil kāntāram kuṟintu varavēṇṭu’meṉṟu colli capiyōrāl kūṭiyē vara vēṇṭum eṉṟu collakkēṭṭu muṉampūṇṭa makā-rāca-rāca-ciṟi pañcāpakēca pākavatar avarkaḷum,
4. ‘oru stāyiyil ca-pa muṟiyil 53 curutikaḷ varavēṇṭu’meṉṟu cātitta makā-rāca-rāca-ciṟi cuppiramaṇiya cāstiri avarkaḷum,
5. ‘cilappatikārattil caṅkītattippaṟṟi iraṇṭu varitāṉ irukkiṉṟaṉa’ eṉṟu tañci kāṉa capiyil coṉṉa makā-rāca-rāca-ciṟi T.N.irātākiruṣṇa aiyar B.A., avarkaḷum,
6. ‘oru stāyiyil 22 curutikaḷ varukiṉṟaṉa’ veṉṟu coṉṉa rāv pakatūr makā-rāca-rāca-ciṟi nākōjirāv B.A. avarkaḷiṉ apippirāyattit tāṅki niṟkum makā-rāca-rāca-ciṟi cuntaramiyar B.A.,L.T. avarkaḷum,
7. ‘curuti viṣayam namatu puttikkeṭṭātatu’ ippoḻutu pirayōjaṉap paṭātatu, oru nāḷum muṭivu peṟāta cāstira caṇṭiyuṭiyatu, nuṭpamāṉa curutikaḷik kavaṉittuk kīrttaṉaṅkaḷ pāṭuvataṟku anēka catur yukaṅkaḷāki viṭum, ivvitamāṉa cīrtiruttam ippōtu namakku vēṇṭām, tañcāvūr caṅkīta kāṉpareṉs 24 curutikaḷukkum 22 curutikaḷukkum ēṟpaṭṭa pōrk kaḷamāy muṭintatu eṉṟu eḻutiya makā-rāca-rāca-ciṟi C.R. cīṉivāca aiyaṅkār B.A.avarkaḷum,
8. milāppūr makā-rāca-rāca-ciṟi A.P.kaṇēca aiyar avarkaḷum iṉṉum ivarkaḷ pōtaṉikkuṭpaṭṭa cila puṇṇiyavāṉkaḷum naṭantavikaḷukku muṟṟilum virōtamākat taṅkaḷippōl pēpparkaḷukku eḻutiṉārkaḷ.
ivarkaḷuṭiya kaṭitam cilavaṟṟiṟku eṉatu cinēkitarkaḷ patil eḻuti yiruntārkaḷ. ellāvaṟṟiṟkum avarkaḷ eḻutavilli. nāṉum eḻuta niṉikkavilli. āṉāl taṅkaḷ kaṭitattiṟku eḻutavēṇṭiyatu avaciya māyiṟṟu. atōṭu taṅkaḷippōl pēpparukku eḻutiya teṉtēcattuk kaṉavāṉkaḷum aṟintukoḷvataṟku mukkiyamāy eḻutavēṇṭiyatāyiṟṟu.
maṟṟum mukkiyamāṉa cila kaṭitaṅkaḷiyum - avikaḷukku eḻutiya patiliyum karuṇāmirta cākarattil ‘teṉṉintiya caṅkītattiṉ curutikaḷum āl intiya caṅkīta kāṉpareṉsum’ eṉṟa talippiṉ kīḻk kāṇalām.
muṭivāka
(1) taṅkaḷ apippirāyattiṉpaṭiyum pūrvattōriṉ apippirāyaṅkaḷiṉ paṭiyum teṉṉintiyāviluḷḷa tavacirēṣṭarkaḷ apippirāyattiṉpaṭiyum tāṅkaḷ tiṣṭāntam koṭutta ēṇippaḻuvip pōlavum camamāṉa ōci yuṭiya curaṅkaḷālāṉa caṅkītamē cariyāṉa caṅkītam.
(2) camamāṉa ōciyuṭiya curaṅkaḷālāṉa caṅkītamē parōṭāvil eṉṉāl kāṭṭappaṭṭatu. ammuṟiyē pūrva tamiḻ makkaḷiṉ cāstira ātārattiṟkum taṟkālaaṉupōkattiṟkum, aṇuppiramāṇamum picakāmal ottuvarakkūṭiyatu. iṉivarum kālattilum, yāvarālum oppuk koḷḷap paṭṭuk koṇṭāṭakkūṭiya muṟiyeṉṟum caṅkīta cāstirattiṟkē putiya uyir nili eṉṟum nāṉ niccayam colvēṉ. āṉāl taṅkaḷ oḻuṅkīṉa māṉa muṟi taḷḷappaṭṭup pōyiṟṟu.
(3) teṉṉintiyāvil piṭivātamāy tuvāvimcati curutiyeṉṟu cātikkum cilariyum muṉ piṉ aṟiyāmal oru stāyiyil 25 curutikaḷ eṉṟu cātikkum taṅkaḷiyum tavira taṟkāla aṉupōkattiyum pūrva muṟikaḷiyum kavaṉikkum aṟivāḷikaḷum iṉivarum cantatiyārum aṉuṣṭikkakkūṭiya uttamamāṉa muṟi eṉ muṟiyēyeṉṟu nāṉ niccayamāyc colluvēṉ.
(4) curuti camamāy varavēṇṭumeṉṟa pūrva tamiḻ muṟippaṭiyē pala aṉupōkaṅkaḷik koṇṭu tiṣṭāntap paṭuttik kāṭṭuvēṉ. avi kaḷukku nēr virōtamāyc ceyyum taṅkaḷuṭiya muṟi muṟṟilum oḻuṅkīṉamāṉateṉṟum oḻuṅkāyirukkum karnāṭaka caṅkītattiyum intustāṉ caṅkītattiyum keṭuttuk koṇṭirukkum eṉṟum nāṉ niccayamākac colvēṉ. tāṅkaḷ iṉi ippaṭic ceyyātirukkumpaṭi mikavum vaṇakkamāyk kēṭṭukkoḷḷukiṟēṉ. atōṭu tāṅkaḷ ippōtu eḻutiyirukkum kaṭitattippōl eḻutuvīrkaḷāṉāl iṅkilīṣ caṅkīta māvatu karnāṭaka caṅkītamāvatu intustāṉ caṅkītamāvatu muṟṟilum teriyātavarkaḷeṉṟu maṟṟavarkaḷ uṅkaḷi ēḷaṉam ceyyumpaṭi nēriṭum. ēṉeṉṟāl pūrva tamiḻ makkaḷ āyappāliyil vaḻaṅki vanta 12 curaṅkaḷum intustāṉ kītattilum, iṅkilīṣ caṅkītattilum vaḻaṅki varum curaṅkaḷum oṉṟākavē irukkiṉṟaṉa.
(5) parōṭā makā rājā avarkaḷ naṭattiya capiyiyum capiyil vantirunta vitvāṉkaḷiyum avamatikkiṟatōṭu aṅku naṭanta uṇmi kaḷi veḷiyiṭāmal ataṟku nēr virōtamāṉavikaḷit tāṅkaḷ veḷiyiṭṭirukkiṟīrkaḷ. intiya caṅkītattiṟku ētāvatu naṉmi ceyya vēṇṭumeṉṟu tāṅkaḷ koṇṭa āvali nāṉ mikavum meccik koḷḷukiṟēṉ.
(6) tāṅkaḷ eṇṇukiṟapaṭi oru kālattilum intiya caṅkītatti eṭuttu niṟutta taṅkaḷāl muṭiyāteṉṟu niccayam colluvēṉ. curutikaḷ cama aḷavuṭiyavikaḷāy varavēṇṭumeṉṟu coṉṉa pūrva teṉ tamiḻ muṉivarkaḷi ‘cāstirōktamillāta oru muṟiyik kaṇṭupiṭittāṉ’ eṉṟu coṉṉataṟkup patil avarkaḷ taṅkaḷ muṟiyiyē parikācak kūttākkiviṭṭārkaḷeṉṟu nīṅkaḷ naṉṟāy niṉikka vēṇṭum.
(7) itaṉmuṉ caṅkīta viṣayamāy yātum aṟiyāta nāṉ vicārikkat toṭaṅkiya kālam mutal appōtikkappōtu aṟintu koḷḷa vēṇṭiya aḷaviṟkut takuntapaṭi aṟiyātavikaḷi aṟiyumpaṭi ceytu ivvaḷavu tūram eṉakku aṉukkirakam ceyta periyōr taṅkaḷukkum aṉuk kirakikkumpaṭi kaṭavuḷip pirārttikkiṟēṉ.
aṉpuḷḷa turiyē! taṅkaḷ kaṭitattiṟku vēlit tolliyiṉāl patil eḻutak kūṭāmaliruntālum curukkamākat taṅkaḷukku iti eḻutiṉēṉ. eṉ vēlikaḷic ceyya vēṇṭiyiruppatāl taṟcamayam taṅkaḷiṭattil uttiravu peṟṟuk koḷḷukiṟēṉ. tāṅkaḷ eṉ muṟippaṭi intiya caṅkītattiṉ uṇmiyi aṟintukoḷvīrkaḷāṉāl cantōṣa maṭivīrkaḷ. taṅkaḷukku eṉ aṉpāṉa vantaṉam.
taṅkaḷ uṇmiyuḷḷa,
K.āpirakām paṇṭitar,
tañcāvūr.
LETTER NO.19
SHANTARAM HOUSE, MALABAR HILL,
BOMBAY.
Monday, 7th Aug. 16.
DEAR RAO SAHEB PANDITHER,
Many many thanks for the copies of your refutation of Mr.Clement’s letters to the Madras Mail as also for the two kind letters accompanying the same. I think I have already told you that I would never cease to admire your great labours and scholarship. If I live long enough I won’t be surprised to find you, one of these days, mentioned as the great leader of the Southern Music School.
I write to-day explining generally my activities on this side and thereby removing any possible misapprehension that may have crept into your mind about my attitude towards some of the leading questions on the subject of music. I do not know which of my publications have come to your notice, but I hope you have seen my Hindustani Sangit Paddhati in Marathi. The Second Volume of the Paddhati briefly deals with the Shruti theories of our writers here. I have personally no Shruti theory of my own. The Shruti discussion in the beginning of the 2nd Volume of the Paddhati is practically a refutation of Mr. Deval’s theories by the Reductio ad absurdum method. The irony running through the chapter is patent to an intelligent Marathi reader. My publications Parijat Praveshika and Ragabodha Praveshika became necessary when Mr. Deval and his comrades were pressing Ahobala and Sommath into service. These publications put a stop to further mischief in that direction.
Then Sharangadeva was dragged in and became their sheet-anchor. I was not able to effectively dislodge them from that position with that success which you obtined the other day, I frankly admit.
But in the Paddhati I could show that Mr.Deval could not father his Shrutis on the author of Ratnakar. I shall now tell you, in brief, the whole history from our point of view.
I travelled for two or three months in the Southern Preisdency in search of useful information in the cold weather of 1904. I had learnet my Hindusthani music under first class masters and was thinking of taking some steps to evolve a tolerably workable music system for popular use on this side. I wanted a good rational and workable model for the same. I consulted the late Mr.Tirumalaya Naidu and Pandit Singarachary at Madras. Under their advice I visited Tanjore. I made then the acquaitance of Messrs. C. Nagoji Rao, P. Subrahmanya Shastri, Srinivas Rao, Ramanna, Jagannath Goswami, Panchapkesa Bhagavat, Muttaya Bhagvat, Seturam Das Swami and some others and freely discussed music with them through interpreters. P.Subrahmanya Sastri was not so well up in the subject then as he appears to be now. There was one thing which invariably came into my observation and it was this. The 12 Hindustani notes I sang to them were declared by the musicians there as their own 12 principal notes also. It was very encouraging to me. I was anxious ot obtin a system of Parent modes or Melakartas, which would be at once scientific and exhustive for the classification of the 150 Ragams in use in our part of the country. My idea was that such a good foundation for the system would combine permanensce and rationality. I visited the Sarasvati Bhandara or Palace Library but did not find any Sanskrit Grantha there, which was likely to solve my dificulty. Jagannath Goswami did show me a Sanskrit Manuscript contining the 72 Melas and their Jayna Ragas, but the same was incomplete. I have already published that small work and called it Raga Lakshna, becuse the Swami sid that was its name. From Tanjore I was directed by C. Nagoji Rao to Ettayapuram, where the late Subrama Dikshit Pandit lived. I learned good many things from that gentleman. He was really a great man and I liked him very much. He gave me a copy of the most valuable manuscript Chaturdandi Prakashika. He died before sending me the sfirst and the last chapters but I got almost all I wanted through my valuable friend, Mr. A. Krishnaswami Aiyar of Tinnelvelly. I have the highest respect for Venkatmakhi Pandit, who could write a work like that. I liked his frankness and powerful language as also his spirit. I visited Mysore, Ramnad, Rameshwar, Shrirang Madura and other places, but did not obtin much that, in my opinion, would be of material use to the Northern system of music. I knew full well that the northern system had many points quite peculiar to itself, but the fact that the principal 12 notes in the country were the same decided me to adopt chaturdandi’s 72 Melakarta system as a good basis for the Northern Ragas. The method of classifying Ragams under their Janaka Melas was a very old one and I saw no objection to adopt it for my design. The next three or four cold weather tours were undertaken by me to the Northern cities to satisfy myself that the Northern Musicians had none of their own independent systems, and to collect opinions on the question of differentiating characteristics of the different Ragas and so forth. I found Ratnakar and Darpana constantly cited as authorities in the north, but none who could rationally explin how they became useful. I visited Nagpur, Calcutta, Puri, Vijayanagar, Hyderabad, Nasik, Delhi, Agra, Jeypore, Mathura, Lucknow, Benares, Gaya, Baroda, Kathiawar, Karachi, Cutch, Lahore and several other places - but failed to meet a single decent Pandit who could argue the subject on the strength of any Sanskrit Granthas. I got much valuale practical information no doubt and I utilized all that in the books I have written.
(In my travels throughout India) Not a single Pandit could argue the Shruti question with anything like precision. No authorities were ever cited or discussed. Many made attempts to say that some of the Ragas admitted smaller tones than semitones but when pressed to explin and demonstrate with reasons and authorities they backed out. No grantha could be cited as authority for the distribution of the Shrutis, which therefore appeared to be to depend on personal whims. As to the use of the well-known 12 notes there was absolutely no disagreement.
I finished my last tour in 1909 and took up the work of writing my book. I retired from business for that purpose and devoted my whole time to the work. I first wrote the Sanskrit Lakshya Sangit, in which I included all that I had to say about the Hindusthani system. My friends who were in my confidence told me tha the theories in the book could not be followed quite clearly and asked me to write a commentary in Marathi. Thus the Hindustani Paddhati came into existence, I took, as I sid, Chaturdandi Melakartas as my foundation and classified all the Northern Ragas thereunder. My friends tell me that my works are favourably received and that even the professionals accepted them as authoritative. I have cited Sanskrit Texts all through to show how the Ragas went through different phases before they assumed their present shapes which I have fully explined in all possible detils and with due illustration. I won’t refer to that now and shall come to he point where Mr. Deval comes in.
Messrs. Deval and friends came in the mean while on the scene. They brought out the 22 Shrituis of the ancient Rishis of 2000 years ago. They supported them by quotations or rather misquotations from Parijat and Ragabodha. They sid I was wrong in establishing a popular music system on the basis of 12 notes. They flourished their Dichord and dazzled their audiences. Mr.Clements interested himself in the subject and that added considerably to the strength of the combination. Mr. Deval was neither a musician nor a scholar, but the same could not be sid of Mr. Clements. I wrote the 2 Praveshikas and showed that the 22 Shrutis of Deval had no basis in those books which they cited. The Phil-harmonic Society was my own suggestion and I was present at its first meeting at Satara, but I could not later on associate with its work which I knew to be wrong and had to keep aloof from it. In the meantime Mr.Clements brought out into prominence the great 22 Shruti harmonium and sought the patronage of the Governor and the Director of Public Instruction for the same. Indeed it was feared at one time that the instrument would have a place in every one of the Musical institutions in this Presidency, under the control of Government. The War came in and postponed the project. My Praveshikas had one effect. Mr.Deva. gave up his original stand on the the Granthas of Ahobala and Somnatha and quietly fathered the 22 Shrutis on Sharangadeva! That led to my including a chapter on the Shrutis in the 2nd Vol. of the Paddhati. The reductio ad absurdum process there is, as I sid, patent to any Marathi reader My writings no doubt succeeded in throwing suspicion on Mr. Deval’s Shrutis, but the influences of Mr. Clements still invested his book with some importance and I should say capacity for mischief. Mr.Deval continued to give demonstrations of his Shrutis in the Southern Marata country but after my publications, he did not meet with the success he expected. He never ventured to bring his demonstrations to Bombay. His agitation was however cusing me any amount of anxiety becuse it was quite unfairly destroying the useful work I was doing. I knew he was wrong but I could not cope with the influence of his champion Mr.Clements. I have a very great respect for Mr.Clements. He is a great scholar and takes real interest in Indian Music. I tried to explin matters to him in the right spirit but he was so fascinated with Deval’s Shrutis - perhaps he sincerely believed that Deval interpreted Sharangadeva right - that he practically refused to listen to me. He ignored me and my labours and set about distributing the 22 Shrutis among the Hindusthani Ragas with the help of musicins not carrying any very high reputation in the north. He began by giving 3 Shruti Ri and 3 Shruti Dha and Ati Komal Gqa and Atikomal Ni to the common Raga Kaphi. He sid that was the real Shudha Scale of the ancient Rishis and munis as also of Sharangdevqa, commenced to evolve scales for Kalian, Khawaja. and etc. from that scale. This, I saw, was rather serious. The northern musicians, as also the Southern ones. used Chatushrutis Ri and Dha and Sadharama Ga, Kaishik Ni in Kaphi Ragam, and I told him so, but he sid Mr. Deval was right and I was wrong, and went on with his new classifications. I drew his attention to this practice of the Vainikas in the country but was told that they were all playing wrong. He went the length of writing to me that it was the Vina players and the Nagsur players who had spoiled the real Hindusthani music. Reconcilliations between us thus became impossible. I appealed to Deval and requested him to correct the slight errors he had drifted into and thus come and co-operate with me. I told him I was not aginst the use of micro-tones or Shrutis in such of the Ragas as realy required them, but all I wanted was they should not be fathered on the Sanskrit writers so as to render their works rediculous. I proposed that we should fix the Shrutis for the Ragas in a sort of Conference of the Pandits and experts. He refused the offer saying he had gone too far to recede, and sid he would stand or fall with his protector Mr.Clements. Thus a great cloud was hanging over my head. The position was this. Either Deval was right or I was, all my labours, perfectly honest and disinterested, were to come to nothing simply becuse Deval had a strong and influential friend and I had not.
But I had full confidence in my God. “Commit theyself unto God and trust in Him and He will bring it to pass,” was my motto. Who appealed sincerely to God and did not succeed? God Almighty saw that I was unjustly being swamped away by influential mischief-makers and decided to help me. He inspired H.H. The Gaekwar and his most sympathetic prime minister, the large-hearted Dewan Saheb, to take up my cuse. Your great assistance also I ascrisbe to His inspiration. I take no credit to me for all that happened at the Conference. Mr. Deval and Mr. Clements and their great following collapsed like a pack of cards. The Sanskrit Professors corroborated all my interpretations and falsified Deval’s. I never had a Shruti Theory of my own. I relied upon the 12 notes which were firmly established throughout the country. My contention all through my books was that for popular education in music a system based on the established 12 notes was very convenient and therefore ought to be retined. Of course when the minute Shrutis were unanimously accepted by our scholars and practical experts, I had not the least objection to bow to their decision. It was naturally a great satisfaction to me that the great Conference came and decided that my contentions were not unreasonable. I shall never be elated with success becuse I know and honestly believe that it was He that was enacting all that was happening there.
I have nothing more to tell you now about my relations with Deval and his friends. I still love them as my friends and brothers becuse I know they too are working in the cuse of our Indian Music with the same enthusiam. Such tifts are quite naqtural and unavoidable. They invariably lead to good results. I never climed to be infallible myself. I have always corrected mistakes which I committed as will appear from my Hindusthani Paddhati. One must humbly go on working without regard to name or fame and leave it to Him to do the rest. Our ancestors - whom we can never equal-wrote their great works without caring to say who they were or when they wrote! But I must not be a philosopher.
I shall distribute the pamphlets you have kindly sent to my friends. I thank you most sincerely for the kind invititon for the Sangit Conference at Tanjore next week. I am sorry owing to some unavoidable engagement here I cannot make it convenient to attend this time. I beg to be excused on that account. Give my best compliments to our worthy friend the Dewan Saheb. You may assure him that I shall never forget the kindness he has constantly shown to me ever since our acquaintance. I shall write to him separately in a day or two.
You are good enough to ask me how I have liked your exposition of Sharangadeva’s Shruits. What answer can I make? You have a better means of understanding Shrangadeva than myself. I do see there is considerable force in your arguments and it will require a greater intellect than mine to find flaws in them. Wheat I would like you now to do2is to take up the Ragams and Jatis of Ratnakar - a few of them - and show your Shrutis and Swarams fit into them. Sharangadeva’s is a great work admittedly. The Ragams he names and describes are known to us by their names at least. We sing them all in our own way. You will be doing invaluable service by tackling them; at least some of them. It will not be enough to say Sharangadeva misunderstood some Tamil texts and based his system on impossible lines. Shrutis and Swarams after all are intended to represent actual practical music i.e., the Ragams, and if that is so, it naturally follows that those Shrutis or Swaras only will be acceptable which render these Ragams intelligible. I think you will quite agree with me in the above line of argument. Sharangadeva is comparatively a recent writer, and as such, must have sung his Ragams very nearly just as we have been singing them now. An attempt therefore should be made to solve his music with the help of the Shrutis and Swarams you have deduced from his own descriptions. When you succeed in doing that all controversy will come to an end. “The taste of the pudding is in its eating” as they say. I am only puting forward the common sense view. Sharangadeva was either a musicinaro a fool. A fool could not have written, people will say, what he has written. If he was then a great musician, show what he sang practically by correctly explining his Ragams with the help of his Lakshanas and obtin the verdict in your favour. So long as that is not done people will simply say “here is another theory which is worth consideration, but which remins to be proved.” I put before you the argument of the lay mind.
Your 24 Shrutis theory is really very interesting. If it is duly accepted in the South by the musicians there, I should be the first person to give it a trial in our music.
But I should submit it to a special committee of the Northern experts for geting it tested. It is just such things that are tobe done in a conference. My idea is that everything we do for the public should be done with their full consent and knowledge. Discord is hardly the best instrument of success.
Pardon me for having inflicted such a long letter on your valuable time and patience I had no right to do so. I only did it becuse I thought you might be under the mis-apprehension that I have had a Shruti theory for myself and was reticent in my arguments or exchange of views.
With best Namaskarams to yourself and your sons and dughters.
I remin,
Yours sincerely,
BHATKHANDE.

aṭutta nālintu varuṣaṅkaḷil kuḷir kālam ārampittavuṭaṉ vaṭa tēcattiluḷḷa mukkiya nakaraṅkaḷic cuṟṟippārttu, vaṭatēcattār tāṅkaḷāy uṇṭu paṇṇiṉa muṟi ētāvatu irukkiṟatā eṉṟu vicārittēṉ. antanta irākaṅkaḷukkuriya taṉi lakṣaṇaṅkaḷippaṟṟi eṉṉeṉṉa apippirāyaṅkaḷ collappaṭukiṟateṉṟum kavaṉittēṉ. vaṭatēcattil anēka iṭaṅkaḷil ratṉākaram tarppaṇā eṉṟa nūlkaḷ ātāra nūlkaḷākac collappaṭṭa pōtilum, avikaḷ appaṭi eṇṇappaṭuvataṟkut takunta niyāyaṅkaḷi eṭuttuc colvār oruvarumilli. vaṭatēcattil nākappūr, kalkuttā, pūri, vijayanakaram, aitarāpāt, nācik, ṭilli, ācirā, jeyappūr, mattirā, laknu, kāci, kayā, parōṭā, kattiyavār, karācci, kūc, lākūr iṉṉum anēka iṭaṅkaḷic cuṟṟiṉēṉ. āṉal enta iṭattilāvatu camaskiruta kirāntaṅkaḷi ātāra māy vittuk koṇṭu caṅkīta viṣayattil tarkkam ceyyakkūṭiya entap paṇṭitariyāvatu nāṉ kaṇṭēṉilli. āṉāl anēka iṭaṅkaḷil pāṭal vāttiyam vācittal mutaliyavikaḷip paṟṟiya anēkamāṉa viṣayaṅkaḷ eṉakkuk kiṭittaṉa. avikaḷi yellām nāṉ eḻutiya nūlkaḷil aṅkaṅkē kāṇpittirukkiṟēṉ.
