Dear Sir,
Many thanks for the two Pamphlets “Mr.E.Clements on Indian Music” and your remarks on his second letter. Kindly excuse me for the delay I made in acknowledging the above two books. From the very beginning I was reading with interest your replies to Mr.Clements. as I was away from here I could not write to your earlier. Day before yesterday I had a long talk with my friend Mr. Veena Venkataramana Doss, the famous Veena Player. He explined to me your theory of Srutis and I read the book with much interest. There was also another Veena Player Sriman K. Padmanabhaswamy Garu who was also a court musician in the time of the late Maharaja. He is also of opinion that your theory of Srutis is correct. Mr. Venkata Ramanadoss showed me your wire and he sid that he is proceeding to you in 2 or 3 days. I am extremely happy to hear that you are a Vidwan of Vidwans in spite ofyour multifarious duties. On the 16th instant Vynika Sikamani Seshanna came here in connection with the mariage festivities of the Yuva Raj and I had some talk with him about the musical controversy between you and Mr.Clements. He also tells me that your system of Music is quite correct. He has much regard for you and, I think, you quite deserve it.
Mr. Venkata Ramanadoss was telling me that you have a music Conference every year at Tanjore. Will you please let me know the month in which you have it? I am glad you are happy father of two ladies who are well accomplished in music. I was hearing of their high attinment in music. Is the report (full) of the first All Indian Music Conference published? I have also written to my friend Mr. V.N.Bhatkhande and I think he will send me a copy of it.
I request you to send me a copy of Karunamirtha Sagaram, as soon you publish to it.
If the book is published in Tamil I am sorry I am quite unable to read and if the book is published in Telugu or English or even Sanskrit, I can easily go through it.

The Social Reform Advocate - 7th April 1917.
The Srutis in Indian Music
This book is a refutation of the position taken up by Mr.E.Clements that there are 32 Srutis in the Indian octave and is in reply to a letter from this gentleman to the Rao Sahib controverting the position assumed by the Rao Sahib. The reply sometimes oversteps the bounds of controversial dignity and is full of humorous bits which are not always graceful.
The question at issue between the disputants is as to whether there are 22 or 24 Srutis in the octave and primarily whether the octave divisions are of equal temperament or unequal and according to some natural scale.
Mr.Clements clims that the scales used are naturl scales and that the system of equal temperament is quite alien to Indian music. On the other hand the Rao Sahib clims that the Indian scale is one based on equal temperament and so the octave is divided into 12 semitones, these being further sub-divided into 24 quarter tones and so on. His qrgument receives strong testimny from some verses on Isi Tamil in an ancient Tamil work of about the 3rd century A.D., which show that in the South at any rate the system of equal temperament was in vogue. The question is rather a difficult one to decide without the opportunity of hearing the melodies rendered according to both systems. The Rao Sahib certinly has the better of the argument and if his dictum is true it will be much easier for Hindu music lovers to evolve a regular system which can be used by the ordinary person with a certin amount of ease.
As far as one can gather the special harmonium constructed by Mr.Clements and produced before the Baroda Conference failed entirely to give a correct interpretation of Indian ragas and did not commend itself to the musical experts present.
It is a great pity that the report of this Baroda Conference has not yet been published. It is to be regretted that musical questions of this sort should become matters of bitter controversy rather than matters of serious and friendly discussion.
It is hoped that other will take up this matter and try to work it out by careful experiment rather than by reference to ancient classics.
Both protagonists are to be commended for the study which they have given to Indian music; and the Rao Sahib is to be congratulated upon his careful researches into ancient classics as well as upon his scientific experiments upon the notes themselves. We hope that His Highness the Maharajah of Baroda will shortly summon another Conference on Indian music and that the question of the Stutis in present use may be settled once for all so that an ordered system may be built up.
As it is, we have to decide upon insufficient evidence for one side or the other, and in a matter which will vitally affect Indian Music in the future. If Mr. Clement’s position is adopted, then Indian Music must either return to its chotic condition or else become a kind of westernised product. If on the other hand the Rao Sahib is correct, there willbe no difficulty in accurately rendering all Indian notes and in teaching Indian Music according to a thoroughly scientific system. It may be sid that the practice in the South has always very largely folowed the method commended by the Rao Sahib while the North has relied far more upon tradition for the production of the proper notes. This fact partly accounts for the positions taken up by the two protagonists, Mr. Clements having lived in the North and not having come into contact with Carnatic Music.
The Social Reform Advocate 7th April 1917.

iru vātakkārarukkum uḷḷa vivātam eṉṉaveṉṟāl stāyiyil uḷḷa curutikaḷ irupattiraṇṭō, irupattunāṉkō eṉpatum avikaḷ camapākamuḷḷaviyō allatu oḻuṅkīṉa iṭiveḷikaḷālāṉa Natural  skēlic cērntaviyō eṉpatumtāṉ.

Few Remarks on Messrs K.B.Deval’s 22 Srutis and E.Clement’s (I.C.S.) 24 and 25 Srutis, by Rao Sahib M.Abraham Pandither.
(The Lawley Electric Printing Press, Tanjore)
This little pamphlet of 16 pages is intended to be a criticism on the views of Messrs. Deval and Clements regarding the number of Srutis used in Indian music. This is a much-discussed point in the theory of Indian music and we do not think that definite conclusion has been come to on it till now. It is very difficult to see how any such conclusion can be arrived at. No system of music denies the fundamental 7 notes and there we have the common basis of all kinds of music. With regard to the different Srutis employed there may and must be differences.
The pamphlet is obviously too technical to be of any use to the lay reader; but one who studies it throughly will find much food for thought. Mr.Pandither takes exception to some of the opinions of Mesrs. Deval and Clements, but we do not feel sure if some of the author’s statements cannot be takne exception to. The author pronounces opinions but does not seem to prove them from the standpoint of those whose views he criticises. There is one observatin which is certinly true and which every musician will acknowledge as such; and that is :- “when the swarams are arranged in equal semi-tones in an octave, the change of gramam would not result in any new swaram. The same applies to the scale with 22 Srutis also. No new swaram can possibly occur in the middle in spite of the change of gramam. The general opinion is that however the Srutis might be changed for a gramam, the total number of Srutis cannot possibly more than 22. Change of gramam is only relative and no intrinsic alteration can take place in the mutual relation between the different Srutis of a scale by such a change.
The tables on pages 4. 14 and 15 are very instructive and throw a flood of light on many of the obscurities in the theory of Indian music. Our author must have taken a good deal of trouble in preparing them, and we congratulate him theoreon.
One observation we would make here. After all there does not seem to be much practical use is discussing the question about the number of Srutis. There is no difference of opinion as far as the r2 primary Srutis are concerned; and as for the intermediate Srutis, each individual musician is automatically using some of them. While experts employ them consciously and make diliberate use of them in the variation of a tune, an ordinary singer unconsciously makes use of some of them. And, agin, it may be asked why there should be only 22 or 24 or 25 Srutis; in fact interval between any two consecutive Srutis can be divided into many sub-divisions and the Srutis resulting there from may be used-at lease those of them which produce a pleasing effect on the hearer. A self-consistent system can he developed with any or all of these divisions and different authors in ancient India have evidently followed their own different systems though some of them approach one another to a very great extent.	
										R.S.

oru stāyiyil ettaṉi curutikaḷ allatu kāl curaṅkaḷ uṇṭu eṉṟa kēḷvitāṉ patil colvataṟku atika kaṭiṉamāṉa kēḷvikaḷil oṉṟu - ativiṭak kaṭiṉamāṉa kēḷviyē kiṭiyātu eṉṟu nām collukiṟatilli. itu viṣayamāy iraṇṭu caṅkītakkārarāvatu ēka apippirāyam collukiṟatilli. kāl curaṅkaḷ varappeṟāta airōppiya caṅkītattil oru stāyiyil ēḻu svaraṅkaḷiyum 12 ari svaraṅ kaḷiyum stāpittirukkiṟārkaḷ. curaṅkaḷukkiṭiyiluḷḷa veḷikaḷic camamākap pirittu avarkaḷ taṅkaḷ maṉatiluḷḷa eṇṇaṅkaḷi maṟṟavar ilēcil kirakikkumpaṭiyāṉa vitamāy noṭṭēṣaṉil eḻuti vittatu mallāmal piyōṉō mutaliya vāttiyaṅkaḷilum atē vitamāy niliyāṉa svaraṅkaḷi ēṟpaṭutti caṅkītam yāvarum eḷitil kaṟṟuk koḷḷumpaṭiyāṉa oḻuṅkukaḷiyum ceytirukkiṟārkaḷ. āṉāl nām intiya caṅkītattip paṟṟi ippaṭi oru oḻuṅku irukkiṟatākac colla muṭiyātu. ivvita oḻuṅki stāpikkumuṉ oru stāyiyil ettaṉi curutikaḷ irukkiṉṟaṉaveṉpati niccayamāy muṭivāy stāpittāltāṉ intiya caṅkītatti oḻuṅkupaṭuttuvatil ēṟpaṭum kaṣṭaṅkaḷil oṉṟu nivirttiyākum. mutalāvatu curuti viṣayattip paṟṟi eḻutiṉavar cāraṅkatēvar. ivar 13-vatu nūṟṟāṇṭil anēka narampukaḷ mīṭṭiya vīṇi allatu cōṉamīṟṟar mūlamāy oru stāyiyil 22 ciṟiya iṭiveḷikaḷ uṇṭeṉṟum, iṭiveḷikaḷukku curutikaḷ eṉṟu peyareṉṟum eḻutiyirukkiṟār. vaṭa intiyāvil perumpālum vaḻakkattilirukkiṟa intustāṉi caṅkītattiṟku ātāram inta cāraṅkatēvaruṭiya koḷki yē. coṟpa varuṣaṅkaḷukkuḷ taṟkālattuḷḷavarkaḷ avaruṭiya apip pirāyatti cāstira viṣayamāy ārāycci ceytu atiṉ tāratam miyaṅkaḷik kaṇṭupiṭikkat toṭaṅkiyirukkiṟārkaḷ. avarkaḷukkuḷ Mr.tēvāl Mr.kiḷameṇṭs mutaliyavarkaḷic collalām. tēvāl eṉpavar kaṇakkukaḷiṉ mūlamāy ati stāpikkap pirayācappaṭṭār. Mr.kiḷameṇṭs eṉpavarum atēvita apippirāyatti stāpikka muyaṉṟatil 22 curutikaḷuḷḷa skēl tāṉ cātāraṇamāyuḷḷatu eṉṟum, āṉāl avikaḷukkiṭiyiluḷḷa iṭiveḷikaḷ caṟṟu peritāyiruppatāl cāraṅkatēvaruṭiya 22 curutikaḷukkumēl oru stāyiyil 24 allatu 25 curutikaḷ varalāmeṉṟum collukiṟār. āṉāl namakku avaciyamāy vēṇṭiyaviyellām inta 22 curutikaḷukkuḷ aṭaṅkiṉatu eṉṟu iruvarum apippirāyappaṭṭu ataṟkēṟṟa vitamāy oru curuti ārmōṉiyamum uṇṭu paṇṇiṉārkaḷ. āṉāl itu parōṭāvil naṭanta āl intiyā miyūcik kāṉpareṉcil cariyāṉatallaveṉṟu taḷḷappaṭṭatu.
Mr.āpirakām paṇṭitaravarkaḷ-avarkaḷiviṭa karnāṭaka caṅkītattil pāṇṭittiyamuḷḷavarkaḷ teṉṉintiyāvil kiṭippatu aritu-tēvāl kiḷameṇṭs mutaliyavarkaḷ eṭuttukkoṇṭa kakṣi tappu eṉṟu avarkaḷuṭiya koḷkikaḷik kaṇṭikkiṟārkaḷ. Mr.kiḷameṇṭsuṭiya iraṇṭāvatu kaṭitattiṟkup paṇṭitaravarkaḷ eḻutiṉa maṟuppilum. tēvāluṭiya 22 curutikaḷiyum kiḷameṇṭsuṭiya 24 allatu 25 curutikaḷiyum kaṇṭittu eḻutiṉatālum ivarkaḷ iruvaruṭiya koḷkikaḷum teṉṉintiyāvil orunāḷum nilipeṟātu eṉṟu eṭuttuk kāṇpittirukkiṟārkaḷ. cāraṅkatēvar colluvataṟku mēl iraṇṭu nōṭṭukaḷ uṇṭeṉṟu tēvāl taṉ kaṇakkukaḷil kāṇpippatāl tēvāluṭiya skēlum cāraṅkatēvaruṭiya skēlum oṉṟalla eṉṟum cāraṅkatēvaruṭiya skēlil varum curaṅkaḷip peṟuvataṟkāka avi kaḷik koñcam kuṟittu avar colluvatu kaṇakku viṣayattil utikkiṟateṉṟum paṇṭitaravarkaḷ rucuppaṭuttiyirukkiṟārkaḷ. kiḷameṇṭs turiyum cāraṅkatēvaruṭiya curutikaḷukku mēlāka iraṇṭu mūṉṟu putu curutikaḷik kātukku iṉimiyāyirukkiṉṟaṉaveṉṟa kāraṇat tiṟkākap putitāy uṇṭu paṇṇukiṟatiṉāl avarum picakippōyirukkiṟār eṉṟu eṭuttuk kāṭṭukiṟārkaḷ. ippaṭi ovvoru vitvāṉum taṉ iṣṭap pirakāram curutikaḷi uṇṭupaṇṇalām eṉṟāl tāṉum iraṇṭu mūṉṟu curaṅkaḷ māttiramalla anēkam putu curaṅkaḷi uṇṭupaṇṇak kūṭum eṉṟu paṇṭitaravarkaḷ apippirāyappaṭukiṟārkaḷ. ēṉeṉṟāl cāraṅkatēvaruṭiya curuti iṭiveḷikaḷ karnāṭaka caṅkītattiṟku ēṟkāta periya iṭiveḷi kaḷuḷḷaviyāy irukkiṉṟaṉa. tokiyāyc colla vēṇṭumāṉāl Mr.paṇṭitaravarkaḷ kiḷameṇṭs turikku muṟṟilum virōtamāṉa apippirāyatti ātāramāka vittu vēli ceykiṟārkaḷ.
kiḷameṇṭs turiyuṭiya ātāra apippirāyam eṉṉaveṉṟāl nāmāy cariyāy vittuk koṇṭa kikaḷālāṉa cama iṭiveḷikaḷuḷḷa ariccuraṅkaḷālāṉa caṅkītam aruvaruppāṉatu. ivvita iṭiveḷikaḷ vantu nuḻinta kālamutal airōppiya caṅkītam cīr kulintu varukiṟatu eṉpatutāṉ. mēṟṟici caṅkītam inta aruvaruppik kaḷintu muṉṉōruṭiya iṉimiyāṉa cama iṭiveḷikaḷillāta Natural  skēlukku eppōtu tirumpum eṉṟu āvalōṭu kāttiruppatākavum kiḷameṇṭs collukiṟār. intiya caṅkītam cama iṭiveḷi kaḷuṭiyatāy irātatāl tāṉ atu atika iṉimiyuḷḷatāyirukkiṟatu eṉṟu avar apippirāyappaṭukiṟār. āṉāl etirkkaṭciyilō Mr.paṇṭitaravarkaḷ stāyiyi 24 cama pākaṅkaḷāka vakuttatiṉāl tāṉ karnāṭaka caṅkītam attaṉi aḻakum, cuttamum, ciṟappum, makimiyum porunti yiruppatākac colliyirukkiṟārkaḷ. taṉakku ātāramāka anēkamāyiram varuṣaṅkaḷukku muṉṉirunta tamiḻ nūlkaḷi mēṟkōḷākac colli appōtu iruntatupōlavē taṟkālattilum karnāṭaka caṅkītam irukkiṟatu eṉkiṟārkaḷ. tamiḻ vitvāṉkaḷ stāyiyi 48, 96 cama pākaṅkaḷākap piritta nuṭpa curaṅkaḷi upayōkikkiṟārkaḷ eṉṟāl karnāṭaka caṅkītattiṉ arumiyum, iṉimiyum, vistāramum ātmāvi nirappip paravacap paṭuttattakka nuṭpamum vistāramumuḷḷatu eṉṟu eṭuttuc collavum vēṇṭumā? parōṭāvil kūṭiyirunta pirapala vitvāṉkaḷ Mr.paṇṭitaravar kaḷuṭiya kalvittiṟami vāynta kumārattikaḷiṉ caṅkītattip pukaḻntu koṇṭāṭiṉatu āccariyamalla.
curutikaḷip paṟṟiya kaṭiṉamāṉa kēḷviyip paṟṟi atil tērnta pulavarkaḷ caṇṭipōṭumpaṭi nām viṭṭuviṭṭu paṇṭitaravarkaḷiṉ poṟumiyuṭaṉ kūṭiya pirayācattip paṟṟip pēcuvōm. maṟṟavēlit tontaravukaḷiṉ mattiyil poṭṭerittuppōṉa ōli ēṭukaḷi ārāynta teṉṉintiya caṅkītattippaṟṟip pūrvat tamiḻ ñāṉikaḷ coṉṉatip paṇṭitaravarkaḷ veḷippaṭuttiyirukkiṟārkaḷ. avarkaḷ ceyta ārāycci yāṉatu avarkaḷuṭiya caripākamuḷḷa 24 curutimuṟiyi stāpikkiṟatu. iti ivarkaḷ kaṇakkukaḷiṉ mūlamāy rucuppaṭuttiṉatu mallāmal taṉ kumārattikaḷik koṇṭu vitvāṉkaḷ āccariyappaṭumpaṭiyāka vīṇi pāṭṭu mutaliyavaṟṟālum rucuppaṭuttiyumirukkiṟārkaḷ. taṟkālam tirāviṭa ruṭiya kalvi mutaliyavi tirumpa uyirppikkappaṭukiṉṟaṉa. atu viṣayattil āriyarkaḷ teṉṉintiyāvil piravēcikkum muṉṉatākavē teṉṉintiyar tam conta nākarīkam, kavittiṟami, caṅkītam, ciṟpavēli, cittirameḻututal mutaliya kalikaḷil ciṟantu viḷaṅkiṉārkaḷ eṉṟu ulakattukku veḷiyākkappaṭukiṟatu. intac camayattil ātit tamiḻariṉ mēlāṉa caṅkītat tērcciyi eṭuttu stāpikkumpaṭi oru intiya kiṟista varukkuk koṭuttu vittatāṉatu mēṉmiyē. āriyaruṭiya nākarīka māṉatu maṟṟak kalikaḷic cūḻntu koṇṭatupōlavē caṅkīta vittiyum āriya uṭiyit tarittuk koṇṭatil anta cāstirattil upayōkap paṭum vārttikaḷ anēkam māṟiṉa pōtilum, tamiḻc caṅkītattiṉ mukkiya amcam allatu uyir appaṭiyē māṟāmal iruntu camaskiruta caṅkītattiviṭa mēleḻumpi uyarntu caṅkītattil piriyaṅkoṇṭa āyira māyiram āṉmākkaḷi cantōṣappaṭuttikkoṇṭu varukiṟatu. karnāṭaka caṅkītattippaṟṟi oḻuṅkuṭaṉ colli vistarikkum paṇṭitaravarkaḷuṭiya karuṇāmirta cākaram eṉṉum nūl eppōtu veḷiyākumeṉṟu āvaluṭaṉ etirpārkkiṟōm. itaṟkiṭiyil karnāṭaka caṅkītattiṟkeṉṟu avvaḷavu cilākkiyamāṉa nūli eḻutiya paṇṭitaravarkaḷukku vāḻttutal collukiṟōm. taṅkaḷ takappaṉāruṭiya muṟiyi rucuppaṭuttuvatil tamatu mēlāṉa tiṟamiyik kāṇpitta avarkaḷ kumārattikaḷukkum vāḻttutal collukiṟōm.
S.I.
(True Translation)
muṭivuri
kaṭavuḷ kirupiyāl ipputtakattiṉ muṭivikkāṇap peṟṟōm. itit toṭarntu kavaṉittu vanta aṉparkaḷē! pūrvattamiḻ makkaḷ, tām vaḻaṅki vanta icit tamiḻākiya caṅkītattil mikat tērntavarkaḷā yiruntārkaḷeṉṟum, curuti viṣayamāy mika mēlāṉa patattic colli yirukkiṟārkaḷeṉṟum, avikaḷē taṟkālam vaḻakkattilirukkiṉṟaṉa veṉṟum iṉi varuṅkālattilum nilittirukkak kūṭiyaviyeṉṟum meyppippatu pōtum eṉpataṟku utaviyāka, pūrva tamiḻ nāṭṭip paṟṟiyum, tamiḻ moḻiyippaṟṟiyum tamiḻ iciyippaṟṟiyum, muttamiḻiyum vaḷarttu vanta pāṇṭiya aracarkaḷip paṟṟiyum, muccaṅkaṅkaḷippaṟṟiyum, iciyil tērnta pulavarkaḷip paṟṟiyum, cila colla vēṇṭiyatu avaciya māyiṟṟu.
atōṭu curuti viṣayamāyp palar apippirāyaṅkaḷiyum, caṅkīta ratṉākarar, pārijātakkārar mutaliyavarkaḷiṉ apippirāyaṅkaḷiyum, kaṇita mūlamāy viḷakkik kāṭṭi, avikaḷ taṟkāla kāṉattiṟkup porutta muḷḷaviyalla eṉṟu collit, tamiḻ nāṭṭil pūrvantoṭṭu vaḻaṅki vanta nālu pālikaḷiyum, nālvaki yāḻkaḷiyum, avaṟṟil vaḻaṅki varum navvālu jātikaḷiyum, patiṉāṟu jātippaṇkaḷiyum eṭuttukkāṭṭi, ca-pa muṟiyāy oru stāyiyil amiyum paṉṉiraṇṭu curaṅkaḷukkum, vaṭṭappāliyil vaḻaṅki varum 24 curutikaḷukkum, ataṉ mēl tirikōṇap pāli, caturappālikaḷil vaḻaṅki varum 48, 96 āṉa curutikaḷukkum, lākarita muṟippaṭi ceṇṭs kaṇakkum, viparēṣaṉ kaṇakkum, oru stāyiyil curam, curutikaḷ amiyum aḷavu kaṇakkum, avvaḷavil kiṭikkum ōci yiṉpaṭi taṟkāla aṉupōkattil vaḻaṅkivarum kīrttaṉikaḷukku nālu aṭṭavaṇiyum, koṭukka vēṇṭiyatāyiṟṟu.
atōṭu 1916 varuṣam mārccu mātam 20-ām tēti, his hiṉas keykvār makā rājā avarkaḷ kūṭṭi vitta āl intiya miyūcik kāṉpa reṉsil araṅkēṟṟi, yāvarālum oppuk koḷḷappaṭṭa viṣayattip paṟṟiya kaṭitappōkku varattum, āṣēpaṉikaḷum, avikaḷukku maṟuppum, ittuṭaṉ cērkkavēṇṭiyatāyiṟṟu. rippōrṭṭu iṉṉum varavilli.
1916 varuṣam ākasṭu mātam 19m tēti kūṭiya tañci caṅkīta vityā makā jaṉa caṅkattil pañcāyattār muṉṉiliyil naṭanta viṣayaṅkaḷum, pañcāyattār tīrmāṉamum, iccaṅkattiṟku talimi vakitta parōṭā, tivāṉ cākip makā-rāca-rāca-ciṟi V.P. mātavarāv C.I.E.avarkaḷiṉ muṭivāṉa apippirāyaṅkaḷum, cērkkappaṭṭirukkiṉṟaṉa.
curutiyip paṟṟic colli vanta pala kaṉavāṉkaḷum, nūlāciriyar kaḷum tamakkut tōṉṟiyapaṭi colliyiruppatāl, avarkaḷ matattik kaṇṭittu, pūrva tamiḻ makkaḷ vaḻaṅki vanta icit tamiḻiṉ ilakkaṇamē mikac ciṟantateṉṟu meyppikka vēṇṭiyatāyiṟṟu. curutikaḷip paṟṟi iṉi orukkālum cantēkam uṇṭākātirukkavum, avikaḷit tiṭṭamāyaṟintu koḷvataṟkum, ituvē pōtumeṉṟu niṉikkiṟēṉ. taṟkālam caṅkītaṅ kaṟṟukkoḷvōrukku evi avaciyameṉṟu tōṉṟiṟṟō, avikaḷi maṭṭum iṅku eḻutiṉēṉ. aṟiviṟ ciṟanta periyōr, itil kāṇappaṭum kuṟṟaṅkaḷi maṉṉittu, kuṇamāṉavikaḷi virutti ceyya vēṇṭu meṉṟu mikavum vaṇakkamāyk kēṭṭuk koḷḷukiṟēṉ.
iraṇṭām puttakam.
ciṟantateṉṟu yāvarālum koṇṭāṭappaṭum teṉṉintiyāvil vaḻaṅkivarum irākaṅkaḷip paṟṟi, mutaṟputtakamāka eḻutip piracurikka niṉitta nāṉ, tañci caṅkīta vityā makā jaṉa caṅkattil curutikaḷip paṟṟi uṇṭāṉa vātatti muṉṉiṭṭu, avikaḷ caṅkītattiṟku mukkiya māṉavi eṉṟum palarāl pala cantēkam ēṟkak kūṭiyavi eṉṟum, aṟintu teṉṉintiya caṅkītattiṉ curutikaḷip paṟṟi mutal puttamāka eḻuta vēṇṭiyatāyiṟṟu.
iṉivarum iraṇṭām puttakattil, irākaṅkaḷum, oru ārōkaṇa avarōkaṇattil kītam uṇṭākkum muṟiyum, avaṟṟiṉ jīva curam kaṇṭu piṭikkum vaḻiyum, irāka cañcāram ceyyum vitamum collappaṭum. itu putitāka oru irākam uṇṭākkuvataṟku utavuvatu māttiramallāmal, paḻamiyāyp pāṭivarum irākaṅkaḷil piḻikaḷit tiruttik koḷḷavum utaviyāka irukkum. curañāṉam vantavarkaḷukku innūl mika arumi yāṉatu. ulakiṟku cūriyaṉ, cantiraṉum antakaṟku kaṇṇum pōla caṅkīta vitvāṉkaḷukku iṉpan tarattakkatu. accil irukkiṟatu. virivil veḷi varum. eḻuvakit tōṟṟamāy, aviyāvaṟṟiṉ uyirāy, uyiril uṇar vāy, uṇarvil aṟivāy, aṟivil āṉantamāy, āṉantattil kītamāy, kītattil ilayamāy āṉanta niruttamiṭum ellām valla perumāṉiṉ tiruvaruḷi vēṇṭukiṟōm.
tañcāvūr 							        K.āpirakām paṇṭitar.
1-6-1917.
mutaṟ puttakam muṟṟiṟṟu.
